US-46 · Approved agent PRs ship without a manual nudge — added 2026-10-07 (Brad chose option a after #124/#129 stalled in auto-ship; PR #134)

As Brad, who took himself out of the merge loop (auto-ship, 2026-08-10), an agent PR that has a sha-pinned reviewer APPROVE and a green test ships through the 30-minute veto window on its own. It is never stranded by which check finished first, and a fake or failed test never ships it.

  • AC1 (wait, don't race): auto-ship waits up to 10 minutes for test on the head sha to finish, polling every 15 s, instead of reading it once when the review completes.
  • AC2 (only the real test counts): a test success counts only if GitHub Actions ran it and its check suite's workflow is .github/workflows/ci.yml. A test job from another workflow or another app never ships a PR.
  • AC3 (fail closed): if every test run finished without a success, nothing ships (exit 0, as before). If one GitHub API call fails, the poll counts it as pending and tries again; it never counts as a pass.
  • AC4 (no silent stall): if test is still pending at 10 minutes, nothing ships and the auto-ship run fails red, so the stall is visible.
  • Usage signal: the ratio of auto-ship runs that reach the veto issue to approved agent PRs. Before: #124 and #129 both needed a manual review re-run on 2026-10-07.
  • Tests: no unit harness for workflows. Six cases were checked by hand against a mocked gh (PR #134 body); the first agent PR after merge is the live check.

US-47 · Documentation Artifacts built from Markdown keep their links working — added 2026-10-12 (Brad's standing rule that the .md is the source of truth; Codex and adversary findings on the link rewrite)

As Brad, reading a planning doc or piece of documentation as a published claude.ai Artifact that tools/md-artifact.mjs built from its .md, every relative link on the page takes me somewhere real, and the page still says exactly what the .md says.

  • AC1 (relative links work on the published page): a relative link target (inline text, with balanced parentheses or <angle> form, or a reference definition, blockquoted or not) resolved against the .md's own directory goes, on the rendered page, to the linked .md's artifact: URL when it has one, else its GitHub URL (blob, or tree for a folder, on main), keeping any #fragment. The build embeds a map from each target path to its URL; a marked walkTokens hook on the page applies it. Only files git tracks get a GitHub URL; a missing, untracked or gitignored file, or a Windows path, stays as written and prints unresolved link on stderr (best effort: no warning for an image or a target that looks like code). URLs with a scheme (x://, mailto:, tel:, data:, javascript:), #anchors and /paths are left alone; a colon that is not a scheme (notes:x.md) is a path. The build prints a links: summary line counting distinct targets by kind.
  • AC2 (the .md source is never altered): the tool reads the .md and writes only .artifacts/<name>.html; the file on disk is byte-identical after a build, and the embedded copy is the .md body exactly as written (front matter stripped).
  • AC3 (code untouched): the page parser (marked 12.0.2) decides what is a link, and only its link tokens change; raw HTML, including <a href>, is left as written. Nothing inside a code span, a fenced block (also one opened on a list-item line), an indented code block or a raw <pre> block changes. A Markdown link inside an inline raw <code> element is a live link under CommonMark, so it is rewritten.
  • AC4 (images untouched): images keep their destinations, inline (nested-bracket alt text included) or by reference, even when a link shares the definition.
  • AC5 (fragment links land): the page scrolls to location.hash after rendering, and a malformed % in the fragment cannot throw.
  • Usage signal: none; a build tool for internal docs. The links: summary's unresolved count on each build is the health check.
  • Tests: ✅ tools/md-artifact.test.ts (AC1, AC2, AC5 at build time against a throwaway git repo; AC1, AC3, AC4 end to end: the built page rendered in Playwright WebKit with the real marked from cdnjs, skipped with a message when cdnjs or WebKit is unavailable).

  • AC1 (probes dropped): handleError in app/entry.server.tsx sends nothing to Sentry for a GET or HEAD that matched no route (react-router's 404 route-error response) when the path's first segment is not one of our route prefixes. Segments match whole on the raw path, ignoring case as the router does: /api/x is ours, /apiz is not. Dropped on purpose, though the router would resolve them under a prefix: missing static files (/assets/old-chunk.js, served before the router), single-fetch shapes (/api.data) and percent-encoded paths (/%61pi/x). No client of ours sends those.

  • AC3 (the list cannot drift): a test builds the route config from app/routes.ts and fails if the prefix list differs from the first URL segments of the real routes. A new top-level route fails CI until the list names it.

US-42 · Knowledge refresh: source-faithful re-authoring of pathways and references in reviewed batches (added 2026-09-29, plan: docs/knowledge-refresh-plan-2026-09-29.md, Phase 0 step 5)

As Brad, the clinician who owns the knowledge base, I want every pathway and reference re-authored from fresh raw source in small batches, so that what the chatbot says stays faithful to its sources. One agent re-authors each entry from fresh raw. A script checks it (tools/knowledge-batch-check.ts, merged into main 2026-10-03 as work in progress, see the status line below). A fresh adversary and Codex review it with the raw in reach. I sign each batch before it deploys.

  • AC1 (index diff): the index.json diff after a body-only batch is exactly the listed summary corrections, each passed through the F2 split, plus, for a topic-master batch (US-50), the master keys reviewed, topics and router (check: script; owner: orchestrator).
  • AC2 (raw fidelity): the diff report carries a raw path and a sha256, and its entries pair a body line with a verbatim source quote ({body_line, raw_quote}); the checker derives the numbers itself. Every new, changed or relocated-in-place number needs an entry whose body line is an exact current line and whose quote holds the same number; an entry whose body line carries no number is allowed, its quote must still be verbatim in the raw, and it is reported as a WARN; every other entry must share a number between its line and quote, and any required number with no verified coverage fails. The emergency number in a "call 111" sentence is exempt. Drug names have no lexicon and fall under AC4. The report lives at ~/.codex-review/diff-reports/<batch>/, outside every repo, never in a commit or the image. Codex reads it through --include. The batch report commits only hashes, counts and the sign-off line. A script confirms the quote is in that raw file and the number is in the quote. The tokeniser rules are written down first: citation markers [n], years and PMIDs are excluded; 1 g and 1,000 mg are equal; en-dash ranges are two numbers; quotes match after unescaping turndown markdown and collapsing whitespace. This filter feeds Brad's review. It does not prove the raw supports the claim (check: script; owner: orchestrator, then Brad). Reports are append-only: a wrong entry is marked "void": true with a non-empty void_reason instead of being deleted (a void entry without a reason fails), is excluded from coverage, and is listed in the batch report for review. After its first write a report is never edited, not even to append (Brad 2026-10-20): every correction is a sibling <handle>.addendum-<N>.json (N = 1, 2, 3 with no gap), which may only append entries, void an entry with a reason (changed_tokens, current_view_basis, deleted_sentences, extra_raw, ask_brad, and the informational grokipedia_claims and positions_drift, which no check reads; never needs_pubmed, which carries safety work items), or set a non-empty proposed_summary_correction; an unknown key, a reasonless or repeated void, or a numbering gap fails, and a file that only looks like an addendum is a WARN. Several extra_raw entries may name one path: the path is accepted when any of their sha256 values matches, and the others are INFO "superseded sha". The batch report prints each report file and addendum with its sha256, each void as section, index, source (base or addendum-N) and a short hash of the reason, never the reason's text, and each summary correction an addendum set. Addenda repair a base report only when its sole faults are voids without a reason; any other fault needs a fresh report.
  • AC3 (hedging): matching is by whole word. The per-entry count of hedge words does not fall, except for hedges inside sentences the report lists in deleted_sentences with a justification; each such loss is printed as a WARN. Hedge tokens: may, might, can, could, likely, possibly, appears, suggests, associated with, linked to, observational, limited, preliminary, modest, some evidence, no evidence, unclear, insufficient, mixed, not established. Every line that loses one, or gains a hardening token, is listed. Hardening tokens: causes, prevents, treats, cures, reduces risk, proven, should, must, safe, will, effective, improves, lowers, no side effects, recommended, not been observed (check: script; owner: Brad reads the list).
  • AC4 (deleted sentences): every sentence removed anywhere in a body is listed with its justification against the new raw. Every heading present before is present after, unless the batch's exceptions file records its removal or rename with a reason and the orchestrator's name (a section whose only support was a source the refresh rejects, or a heading the source itself renamed). The corpus uses at least 178 escalation headings outside any short regex, and 82 pathways would match none (check: script; owner: Brad).
  • AC5 (answer quality): each refreshed entry has at least one fixed-handle answer check, drawn from its source diff and pre-registered before the agent runs. Topic-master batches (US-50) may run theirs after publishing, on the brad@microvitamin.com test account (Brad, 2026-10-20). It lives in its own fixture field, so it never joins the router suite or shifts the loop's denominator. None falls below baseline under the flip rule (check: harness; owner: orchestrator).
  • AC6 (no agent writes to Shopify or index.json): agents run without the claude_business .env. Article updated_at is snapshotted on both stores before and after each batch (check: script; owner: orchestrator). Exception, topic masters (US-50, Brad 2026-10-20): the orchestrator rebuilds index.json with the script, and publishes a master's web pages after the deploy is verified, under US-50 AC9.
  • AC7 (reference hygiene): excluded handles are never regenerated. No body cites Grokipedia. The product-mention count per body does not rise. Every [n] in a reference resolves. DOIs and PMIDs resolve. No body contains "Top Pick", "What CL Found", "ConsumerLab approved", a CL test result or a brand ranking. A primary study first seen in ConsumerLab or Grokipedia text is cited only after its own PubMed abstract is in the raw and quoted under AC2 (check: script; owner: orchestrator).
  • AC8 (Brad signs each batch): the sign-off is one line in the batch report, committed with the batch (owner: Brad). Topic masters (US-50, Brad 2026-10-20): a master whose review is clean publishes without the sign-off; Brad sees only the always-ask list in US-50 AC8.
  • AC9 (pathway shape): pathway bodies keep the doctor-deferral blockquote and the dated source line. They carry no Auckland logistics, funding criteria, phone numbers or referral machinery (check: script, PATHWAY rules).
  • AC10 (emergencies are actions): a patient-facing body states an emergency as an action ("call 111 or go to the emergency department") wherever the source marks a presentation as needing acute assessment or calls it life-threatening (check: adversary and Codex; owner: orchestrator).
  • AC11 (exceptions are recorded): an accepted exception to a scripted check goes in an exceptions file with reason, author and date. The batch report lists it (check: script --exceptions).
  • Tests: 🟡 Batch 1 (10 pathways) checked 2026-09-29, exit 0 with 3 recorded exceptions; adversary and Codex reviews run; AC5 answer checks and AC8 sign-off pending.
  • Status 2026-10-03 (recovery): the checker was stranded on an agent branch; merged to main (e5e449f5, plus the agent's unsaved edits in cb7ff272). Its behaviour changed after the batches were checked: AC3 now excuses hedges lost inside declared-deleted sentences (the story says the count "does not fall", so Brad rules which is right), AC7 FAILs a new PubMed reference without its abstract, AC2 FAILs an orphan numeric sentence, AC9 bans PHARMAC/Special Authority/"funded for" wording. Open Codex findings (2026-10-03): unpaired numeric sentences can pass without quote verification; DOI-only primary citations skip the abstract requirement; the AC3 exemption above. Spelled-out mass units in compounds are mishandled ("3 nanograms/mL" drops its unit), held as an it.fails spec in the test file. Do not trust exit 0 until these are fixed; re-run the checker on every batch before AC8. The batch bodies themselves are archived, unsigned, in archive/knowledge-refresh-batches-2026-09-29/.
  • Origin: the knowledge refresh plan v7, five adversarial rounds (docs/knowledge-refresh-plan-2026-09-29.md).

Epic D — Lab uploads & documents

(Epics D–G were deleted from this file by commit 2285724 on 2026-09-01 — a session's truncated read written back whole — and restored verbatim from bedc71b0 on 2026-09-06, with the dated notes below bringing them up to that day. build-user-stories-html.ts now refuses a build that drops a story or references an undefined one.)

US-12 · Upload lab reports

As a user with PDF/photo/ZIP lab reports, I drop them in and extraction starts automatically; I see progress per file; failures are explained and my daily quota is enforced before any processing starts.

  • AC1: Auto-process on select; per-file progress; abortable. Batch completion counts come from the provider's request_counts: processing plus the succeeded, errored, expired and canceled requests make the total. processing_status is a state string, not a count object. Results are fetched only once the batch has ended. A status with no request_counts still returns an ended batch's results (2026-10-16); tested in anthropic.server.batch.test.ts.
  • AC2: Server extracts and returns values only — stores nothing. The document's page content does go to Anthropic's API for extraction on the way; under their API policy it is not trained on and is deleted within 30 days barring usage-policy enforcement or law (retention).
  • AC3: Extraction failures surface a friendly error (and now emit upload_extract_failed).
  • AC4: One upload session owns processing, review and save progress. Hiding it preserves drafts; failures remain recoverable from the floating indicator. Closing a finished session resets it. Cancelling processing keeps a dismissed connect-first panel dismissed; only close-from-a-finished-state or discard brings it back.
  • AC5: Rapid selections start only one session. Cancel or unmount during quota/draft flushing prevents later extraction; callbacks from a cancelled session cannot change a newer session.
  • AC6: A pending save can be hidden and reopened, but cannot be discarded or submitted twice. Its indicator distinguishes saving, review, failure and completion. A save branch that throws is reported to Sentry (tag only) and keeps the session in review with drafts and an error, so a second Save retries idempotently, and a document the partial save already filed unchecks itself so the retry cannot file it twice; a document-archive errorCount with values saved still completes. A thrown ordinary lab-original archive remains retryable after saved values refresh into read-only history; the retry saves the original without resaving those values. A value the record refuses, a lab unit it does not take (US-21 phase 3) or a blood test value outside the range the record accepts or not a number it can store (US-35 AC17), is a settled outcome, not a save error: a retry can never change it, so the save completes, upload_saved fires, and the done screen names each refused test once on its own line with no "try again". When another branch fails and the session stays in review, the same lines show at once, beside the retry message. Usage signals remain upload_started, upload_extract_failed and upload_saved, plus upload_outcome per run (AC10) and measurement_refused per refused test and reason (US-35 AC17).
  • AC7 (2026-10-02, Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-6W, sentry-fix 2026-10-02): PDF extraction works on browsers without Promise.withResolvers (Safari 16.4–17.3, Chrome 94–118, Firefox 94–120; on Chrome 94–97 a large image reused across scanned pages can still fail, as pdf.js calls structuredClone there): the upload bundle installs it on the main thread and in the pdf.js worker before pdf.js runs. Without it, pdf.js 4.x threw inside getDocument, the per-file catch swallowed the error, and every PDF ended as "No readable files found". Residual: Safari below 16.4 still cannot run pdf.js 4.9, because its worker uses a class static block, syntax no shim can fix.
  • AC8 (2026-10-13, decimal comma): a value or reference bound printed with a decimal comma is read as a decimal ("5,2" is 5.2, "0,87" and "0,870" are 0.87, "5,2000" is 5.2), by the form's own parseLocalisedNumber; stripping the comma used to read "5,2" as 52. One to three digits, a comma and exactly three digits ("250,000", "1,050", "1,020", "-1,050") is refused: it reads as US thousands or a European decimal, 1000x apart, and either reading passes the count guard (250,000 cells/µL as 250, 1,050 pg/mL B12 as 1.05). That rule is the model-output path's alone; the form keeps its own. A number followed by a flag or unit keeps the number ("5.2 H", "5,2 H", "141 mmol/L", "5.2*", "6.1 ↑", "6.5 % (48 mmol/mol)") only when no digit follows it, a final bracketed alternate print aside. On a count row that bracket is no way out: a string value or bound is a readable bare number and at most one flag (H, L, HH, LL, *, ↑ or ↓, any case, bracketed or not: "7.5 H", "250 (H)"), and anything else refuses the whole row, bounds included, counted. A bound that reads as nothing ("150,000") refuses the row too, even beside a numeric value: with no range left the count guard cannot check the scale. "7 (X10³)", "7 (10³)", "7 (E3)", "7 thousand", "250 K" and "7 (K)" under cells/µL read as 7 or 250, and with bounds printed the same way stored 0.007 ×10⁹/L. On every row the general rule fails closed: a range, ratio, exponent or second number after the first ("1 234", "5 to 7", "4,5 bis 5,5", "1:160", "1/80", "7 x 10^3", "5·2", "5 und 7", "250 x10^9/L") is dropped and counted, never read as its first number. Listing those shapes one by one missed the next each review round; "7 x 10^3" cells/µL read as 7 stored 0.007 ×10⁹/L. A count row is a per-µL or per-mm³ count label (mm3 or mm³, not "mm^3", which the catalogue refuses anyway), any prefix or none ("cells/uL", "células/µL", "/mm3", "cells/cumm", and every cubic millimetre normalizeLabUnit folds to µL: "cells/cmm", "cells/cu mm", "cells/cu.mm", "cells/c.mm"). On it dot thousands ("250.000") is refused too, in the value or in either string reference bound: 250 between "150.000" and "450.000" stored 0.25 ×10⁹/L. The same print written as a JSON number ("value": 250.000) parsed to 250 before any guard saw it, so since 2026-10-13 (follow-up) every parse of the model's answer, on the website, the batch poll and the BYOK Pages build, quotes a value, referenceLow or referenceHigh that is a bare number with exactly three decimals before JSON.parse (parseExtractionJson). It then takes the string path: a count row refuses it, and any other row reads 1.020 as 1.02, as before; a JSON string holding that text is untouched. Under any other unit the dot is a decimal ("2.345" mIU/L TSH, "1.020" SG), and a count label that already carries a multiplier is no count row, so the dot is a decimal there and the general rule applies: a power of ten ("×10³/µL", spaced "10 ^ 3/uL" too, as normalizeLabUnit folds it), "M/µL" or a word before the slash ("4.567 Mio/µl", "7.500 K/uL", "250.000 tys/µl"; also thou, thousand, Tsd with no dot after it, mln, mil, million). A minus printed as U+2212 is a minus ("−2.5" is -2.5); a range in any dash, tilde or ellipsis holds a digit after the number, so it is refused, and a bound so drawn becomes unknown. A number that mixes comma and dot ("1.234,5", "1,234.5", "1,234,567"), or that does not start the string ("<5", ">2000", "trace"), is dropped, never guessed. parseLocalisedNumber reads plain decimals only: "0x10", "1e3" and "Infinity" are refused, where Number() read 16 and 1000. A string or unreadable reference bound, or a null unit on an additional value, never fails the whole file: the bound parses or becomes unknown (on a count row it refuses the row), the unit becomes empty. Each value row parses on its own: a malformed row (a null unit on a core value, an unknown confidence, a missing or blank name, an object value) is dropped, counted and the rest kept; a malformed file shape still fails. One parse serves the website, the BYOK Pages build and the connector's import_documents. Saved screening answers read the same way: a pack-years or PSA answer of "4,5" is 4.5, where parseFloat read 4 and missed the PSA above 4.0 suggestion; a blank one is stored as null. The connector says so too: an import_documents file entry carries droppedValues and a hint to relay (US-35), since once filed the report dedups as already_imported. Tests: lab-extraction.test.ts, app/lib/anthropic.server.test.ts, anthropic.server.retry.test.ts, anthropic.server.batch.test.ts, byok-upload.test.ts, parseNumber.test.ts, mappings.test.ts and roadmap-store-data-safety.test.ts "US-12 AC8" cases; mcp-tools.test.ts and app/lib/mcp-import.server.test.ts "partially refused report".
  • AC9 (2026-10-13, every file accounted for; a guest's nine lab PDFs saved with no error shown, then the feedback "can't read PDFs produced by my lab"): the review, done and error screens name every file the upload picked up and did not fully read, with a plain reason: could not open (password-protected, damaged, or not a PDF, photo or .docx file; a pdf.js throw, a timeout and a file with no pages all land here; a ZIP that will not open is named itself, and an empty ZIP or one of unsupported files is named "No files we can read inside this ZIP"; open gaps: unsupported members of a ZIP that also holds readable files, ZIP entries past the 200 cap, and a pick past 200 files are skipped without a notice); too large (over 10 MB, listed beside the files that were read, never wiped by the run starting; a ZIP member is checked too, after it inflates and before pdf.js or the image resize, on both paths); "This file is long, so only its first part was read." (a PDF past 20 pages, a PDF page's text past the text-page cap, or a .docx cut, AC13; review 2026-10-18, the wording was "only the first 20 pages", false for the other two); filed as a document with no blood test values found; no blood test values found; "N values could not be read" (rows the parse refused, AC8); the server could not read it; the daily upload limit was reached; "Claude declined to read this file, so trying again will not help" and "The file is too long to read in one go" (a refusal or a max_tokens stop, on every path and both builds, since 2026-10-16, US-15 AC34). The batch path (20 or more files) names each file by its own result: results carry their request index, so a failed, expired, unparseable or missing entry is that file's server error, never "Unknown file" or "no values found", and the originals and each document's sourceFileName carry the real name. The results file is read record by record, whatever its key order, whitespace, blank lines or CRLF, and a result counts only under its exact file-N id (2026-10-19, PR #155 by @robertaustinbell): file-01, file-0junk or file--1 is skipped, a damaged record cannot swallow a complete record after it, and a record split by a literal newline is still rejoined. Known gap (Codex, 2026-10-19): a split record that opens with result rather than custom_id, right after a damaged one, is joined onto it and lost. When no result carries an index (an old server answering during a deploy), results map by position, the order the old server sorted them in, but only when there is one result per file; otherwise every file is a server error, since position then says nothing. A run that fails whole (the batch refused, its poll failed) names every file not already named, with the daily limit when that was the cause and a server error otherwise. Files are told apart by their whole path, verdicts matched one for one, so two files with one short name in different folders ("a/results.pdf" that will not open, "b/results.pdf" refused by the limit) each get their own notice and their own count; the list shows the short name, or the whole path when two listed files share it. A file that gave values and nothing else goes unlisted. The list sits inside the Clarity-masked modal, and file names go nowhere else: since 2026-10-13 (follow-up) the batch request carries each file's pages and no name (it can hold a patient's name), results come back by index, and the server schema strips a name an older widget sends. Each file still carries fileName: "file-1", "file-2" and so on, a compatibility label that names nothing: CI ships the widget before the server, and a server older than 2026-10-13 refuses a batch file without the field, so without it every 20+ file upload failed until Fly deployed. Drop the label once every live server strips it. The BYOK console log names a failed file by its index. The GitHub Pages build has no server of ours and no daily limit: the user's own Anthropic key reads each file, so there the last two reasons read "Anthropic could not be reached or could not read it" and "Your Anthropic key hit its rate limit. Wait a minute and try again" (a per-minute 429 from that key, once read as the daily limit), the error screen says the same, and the upload_outcome keys do not change. A key Anthropic refuses (401 or 403) reads "Anthropic refused your API key. Check the key in the "Ask about your plan" panel", and an account with no credit (a 400 naming credit or billing) reads "Your Anthropic account has no credit. Check its billing, then try again": trying again never helps there. Both still count as serverError. Since 2026-10-13 a ZIP member is named zip/member ("labs.zip/results.pdf"), and that name is its document's dedup key, sourceFileName, so members of two ZIPs on one path stay apart. A name past 255 characters is cut once, by zipMemberName from the whole path, on the website and the connector alike, so both file it under one name. A ZIP imported before then, or downloaded again under a new name, offers its document-only members again, pre-ticked; off-cloud, saving one adds a second metadata row. Lab values are unaffected (they dedup on metric and date), and archived originals dedup by content hash.
  • AC10 (usage signal for AC9): each upload run past the quota check fires one upload_outcome event when it reaches review or fails, and a pick of only oversize files fires one too. Its metadata is integer counts only: picked, withValues, documentOnly, noValues, openFailed, tooLarge, truncated, serverError, limitError, refused, tooLong (both since 2026-10-16, US-15 AC34), valuesDropped, docx and picturesOnly (both since 2026-10-18, AC13), undatedPrevious (AC14), unitsGuessed (AC16) and unitsRefused (AC15), each 0 to 1000 (limitError counts the daily limit and, since AC17, each file past the 200-file cap of one upload); a zero is not sent (every key is optional), so a reader takes a missing key as 0. picked is every file seen, a ZIP counted by its members, or as one file when it gives none; valuesDropped counts values, not files, and only values the parse refused: a creatinine refused for its unit is unitsRefused (AC15), except from a widget that predates AC15, whose server adds it to valuesDropped; docx counts the picked .docx files, a kind, so it overlaps the rest; picturesOnly is a .docx of pictures and no text, a verdict like the others. Never a file name, a unit, a value or free text. The server refuses a string, a negative, a fraction, a count over 1000, any other key (even one another event may carry, such as provider or count), and these keys on any other event. It skips the once-per-tab throttle so a second upload in the tab still counts; the events route's per-visitor and per-IP limits bound it.
  • AC11 (2026-10-16, a customer's one-page baseline sheet): a core lab test the model files under additionalValues is saved as that core value, not as a lab row. In the live run, systolic and diastolic BP and ApoB came back as systolic_bp, diastolic_bp and apolipoprotein_b additional rows, so the plan said "Blood pressure — not entered" and the ApoB row stayed empty; PSA did the same in 1 of 3 runs. toUnifiedResult resolves each additional name with resolveCoreMetricName and moves it into values, converted by the same unit path, only when all three hold: the name is one of the 11 extracted metrics (VALID_METRICS); its unit is one that test is measured in (reportedToCanonical), since a name alone can be another test or carry no unit to convert (an ApoB with no unit stays a lab row); and no core row holds that metric yet. Creatinine is never promoted: a urine creatinine prints in mg/dL and µmol/L too, and serum creatinine drives eGFR. Otherwise the row is handled as before. The website and the BYOK build keep it as a lab row: nothing is dropped, and a second reading of a held metric is kept. The connector's import_documents refuses it into unrecognized, as it always has for a core name (appendLabValue, US-31 AC5). Weight, waist and height also resolve as core names but stay lab rows: the review takes the 11 only. Every path that parses the model's answer gets this: the website batch, the BYOK Pages build and the connector's import_documents. The review shows a row for every core value it would save: BP rows follow the blood tests, since save takes every cell, and before this a BP the model did put in values was saved with no row shown. A saved BP on a date the upload brings is seeded as context, so a differing value is a conflict like any held slot (US-13 AC3); BP on other dates adds no column. Upload history carries every active measurement (UploadHistory.measurements, renamed from bloodTests). Lab cells key on lab:<name>, so a lab row saved under a core name before this change (systolic_bp, psa) never shares, or hides, the core cell. Those old lab rows stay as they are: no migration. A fixed-unit chip (BP's mmHg, PSA's ng/mL) is static, not a toggle that did nothing. The extraction prompt also says a measured blood pressure printed as one reading ("120/80 mmHg", a generic example) is systolic_bp and diastolic_bp, both in values; the promotion stays as the safety net. Lab rows are named by their own name to screen readers, never by that key. Tests: lab-extraction.test.ts, ReviewTable.conflict.test.ts and ReviewTable.screening.test.tsx "US-12 AC11".
  • AC12 (2026-10-18, a customer's sheet with a "Prev." column): a previous-results column that prints its own collection date becomes that date's values. The prompt (unifiedSystemPrompt, rule 2) extracts each of its rows as its own entry with recordedAt (YYYY-MM-DD), from the ONE most recent dated previous column only, older ones ignored: a cumulative report with several dated columns would multiply the output and run past the website's SINGLE_FILE_MAX_TOKENS (10000), failing the whole file as too long (review 2026-10-18); the primary column, the most recent collection, carries none. A trend graph, or a value that cannot be tied to one printed day, is ignored, as before; a previous column dated with a month only, or not at all, is read since AC14. That rule is the full prompt's, for the website and BYOK; the connector's metadata prompt keeps the base rule, every previous column ignored, until the MCP 1.0.2 review ends (US-35 AC5). At most one entry per metric per date. The shape is the one the connector's file_results already takes (US-36 AC1): ExtractedValue.recordedAt and AdditionalLabValue.recordedAt, "this value's own day, when it differs from the file's"; no new shape. The parse reads it on every value row and never lets it cost a primary value (review 2026-10-18): null, absent, "" or blank is the primary column; any other non-string (20250902, an object, an array) is unusable and left out like a bad day; a datetime is cut to its day first ("2026-03-10T08:00" on a 2026-03-10 report is the primary column); a day equal to reportDate is the primary column, the report date cut to its day too ("2026-03-10T08:00:00"); a report date that is not a calendar day orders nothing, so own-dated values are left out. A value whose day is still not a full calendar day ("2025-09", "2025-02-30", "02/09/2025"), is on or after the report's date (a previous column cannot be later: this catches a future day, and a DD/MM swap only when the swapped day lands after the report; one that lands before it still passes), or has no report date to be ordered by, is left out on its own: never counted as unreadable, never moved onto the report date. AC11's promotion is per (metric, day), so an ApoB filed as an additional value on two dates becomes two core values. The review gives each printed date its own column, and a file's own primary reading of a (metric, day) wins over another file's previous-column read of the same slot, whichever file comes first, and claims it even when it equals what the record holds, so the previous read never shows as a conflict against the saved row. If the two differ, the previous read is not shown (no in-batch conflict yet: a conflict cell is built to correct a SAVED row, correctsId, and two unsaved readings need their own control); editing the report's date moves only the primary column (each date is its own source in the review's date state). Save writes ordinary dated rows: one active row per (metric, day), dedup on (metric, recorded_at), so a previous value the record already holds is context, and a differing one is a conflict with Replace unticked (US-13 AC3). The same parse serves the BYOK build, which keeps these values, and import_documents, which leaves them out until the MCP 1.0.2 review ends (US-35 AC5). A tab opened before this deploy ignores recordedAt and would file a previous value on the report date, so only this widget's requests (single file and batch) carry ownDates: true; without it api.lab-import-v2 strips every value with its own day before answering, the batch poll included (review 2026-10-18). BYOK reads in the browser and needs no flag. Usage signal: no event isolates it yet. upload_saved {count} rises with it but cannot tell a previous column from a longer report; proposed, not added: an upload_outcome count ownDated (values carrying their own day). Tests: lab-extraction.test.ts "US-12 AC12" (the full prompt's rule and the metadata prompt's base rule, the day carried, equal-to-report stripped, blank and datetime days kept as primary, a bad, later or unorderable day left out uncounted, promotion per day), api.lab-import-v2.test.ts and upload-api.test.ts (no flag, no own-dated value; the widget sends the flag) and ReviewTable.dates.test.tsx (a synthetic two-date table: two columns, saved on their own days, held equal is context, held different a conflict, a report-date edit leaves the previous day, a primary reading beats another file's previous read in either order).
  • AC13 (2026-10-18, a customer's one-page Word baseline sheet laid out as a table: test, result, previous result, unit, reference range; the upload said "Could not open it"): a .docx file is read in the browser, on both builds, and sent as one text page, the shape a PDF's text layer already takes; the server and its schema are unchanged, and no dependency is added (JSZip is already in the upload bundle). The text is the headers, then the body, then the footers, since a report date often sits in a header. Paragraphs and table rows keep document order: each table row is one line, its cells in order joined by " | ". An empty cell is kept, so a blank previous result stays in its column; a merged cell (w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore, w:gridAfter) is padded with empty cells, so a row keeps the header's columns, and an empty vertically merged cell (w:vMerge) repeats its restart cell's text in its grid column, as Word shows it, so a unit column merged down a block of rows gives each row its unit (review 2026-10-18); a continued cell with its own text keeps it, an unmerged cell ends the merge in every column it spans, a deleted row neither starts, ends nor copies one, and a merge never reaches into another table. Reading stops once the text passes the cap by a small margin, merge copies counted by one running total, and the file is marked cut short, so copied text never fills memory; the rows still open keep the text read so far, each paragraph or nested row its own line, before the usual cut, up to a deleted row. A row nested in a deleted row is deleted with it. Tables nest at most 64 open rows deep; past that, reading stops the same way and the file is marked cut short (Word never nests near that deep; ruling 2026-10-18), so a crafted file of thousands of nested rows finishes at once. An all-empty row is dropped. A text box's paragraph is its own line, after the text of the paragraph it sits in so far, so a label stays before its boxed value. XML entities are decoded once; half a surrogate pair stays as written. Characters written as tags are read: a non-breaking hyphen as "-", a positional tab as a space, and a w:sym as its character (the Symbol font's < > ≤ ≥ µ ± × ° · α β γ, its digits and punctuation, or a code outside the private-use area as itself); a symbol it cannot map shows as "?", never nothing; a soft hyphen is dropped. Formatting, tracked deletions (a deleted table row whole, and a deleted run with all it holds, a w:sym, tab or hyphen included; a row's deletion marker deletes the row whether written self-closing or as an empty pair, whitespace allowed), text moved away with tracked changes (w:moveFrom; the moved-to copy is kept), the old properties a tracked formatting change keeps (w:trPrChange, w:tcPrChange, w:pPrChange, w:rPrChange, w:tblPrChange, w:sectPrChange, so an old merge never re-applies), field codes and a text box's fallback copy are ignored; a self-closing fallback drops nothing, and a fallback nested in another is dropped whole. The w: and mc: prefixes are the ones the part's root binds to the WordprocessingML and markup-compatibility namespaces; an attribute is read with either quote and spaces around its =. Only those XML parts are inflated, at most 50 header and footer parts in all, and inflating stops past 4 MB of XML in all, so a ZIP bomb never fills memory; the 10 MB per-file limit still applies first. The text stops at 60,000 characters, about the 20 PDF pages the website reads, and the file gets the truncated notice a long PDF gets ("This file is long, so only its first part was read.", AC9). Every cut (cut-text.ts) falls at the last line end, else the last space, else the cap backed out of a number, and never splits a surrogate pair. A PDF page's text is cut the same way at 100,000 characters (IMPORT_LIMITS.websiteTextPageChars), with the same notice, and the server's labImportPageSchema (validation.ts) refuses a text page longer than that as a backstop; an image page is not capped. A .docx that will not open, holds no text or passes the XML cap gets the could-not-open notice, which now says "not a PDF, photo or .docx file"; one with pictures and no text says "This Word file holds pictures, not text. Save it as a PDF, or upload a photo of the page." A .docx a browser reports as a ZIP is still read as a .docx. A legacy .doc is not read: its notice says "Word .doc files cannot be read. Save it as a PDF or .docx, then upload that." The picker offers both, so the .doc notice can be seen. Not covered: a .docx inside a ZIP (the shared importable list, health-core IMPORTABLE_EXTENSIONS, is unchanged); the connector's import_documents, which sniffs a .docx as a ZIP; and formatting that carries meaning: hidden text is read and superscripts flatten into the line ("10^9/L" reads "109/L"), as in a PDF's text layer. Equations (m:oMath) are not read. Usage signal: upload_outcome gains docx, the count of .docx files picked, and picturesOnly, the count of .docx files of pictures and no text (AC10). Tests: docx-extract.test.ts, cut-text.test.ts, pdf-extract.cut.test.ts, file-kinds.test.ts, health-core lab-extraction.test.ts (the capped inflater, shared with the connector) and validation.test.ts (the text-page cap), and UploadModal.outcome.test.tsx "US-12 AC13".
  • AC14 (2026-10-19, Brad's decision; a customer's Word baseline sheet with no dates anywhere: its blood results sat only in a "Prev. Result" column, "Today's Result" blank for those rows, so nothing useful was extracted and Haiku 5.5 flipped between readings): a previous-results column with no printed full day (no date, or a month and year only; Brad, 2026-10-19) is read too, as its own column marked undated. The full prompt's rule 2 takes the ONE most recent previous column, dated or not (with no dates printed, the one beside the current results), and each of its rows even when the current result is blank. A dated column gives recordedAt YYYY-MM-DD, as in AC12. An undated or month-only one gives the reserved recordedAt "undated" (UNDATED_PREVIOUS): the prompt says never to invent a day such as the 1st, and a month-only recordedAt ("2025-09") that still arrives is left out, as in AC12. A month-only column also gives printedMonth (YYYY-MM). The parse keeps it only beside "undated", and only when it is a real month no later than the report's month, whether the report date is a full day or a month only (Codex review, 2026-10-20: a month-only report skipped the check); anything else is dropped and the value stays. The review names it. A string in the existing field, not a new boolean, because every guard that keeps own-dated values off a path already tests recordedAt: api.lab-import-v2 already strips it without ownDates: true, and now also without undatedPrev: true (below), and prepareImport's previousColumn skips it on the connector unchanged. The parse accepts only the exact marker (trimmed; "Undated" or "none" is left out, uncounted), checks it before the report-date match, so a report date of "undated" never makes it primary, and needs no report date to keep it. It keeps it only for the full prompt: every call names its mode (toUnifiedResult(parsed, mode), no default); the website's single call and batch and BYOK pass full, the connector metadata. Also in the full prompt only: a sheet whose main content is a table of test results is a lab_report, even when it also lists body measurements or lifestyle metrics (Haiku had filed such a sheet as "other"); a letter, discharge summary or scan report that only contains a section of blood results keeps its own type (narrowed in review, 2026-10-19; not yet measured against Haiku, since the test key is capped until 2026-11-01). The metadata prompt, the connector's, is unchanged word for word. The review shows the undated column first, left of the report's own, with no date: its header reads "Pick a day", or "Pick a day in Jun 2024" for a printed month, over an empty picker (DraftDateCell with needsDay and a placeholder), and it is keyed undated:<file> before and after its day is picked, so it never merges with its own file's report column, another file's column, or any month, and its own header shows the picked day (review round 2, 2026-10-19: a merged column moved another file's date and could lock Save). Its rows meet held rows and other readings on the picked day: an equal held value shows as context in its own column (a BP too, US-13 AC3), a different one is a conflict. One reading per (test, day) is shown and saved, claimed in the save's own order: a report's own reading first, then a dated previous one, then an undated one, then file order. A reading equal to the saved row, and not edited, is already recorded: context, shown in its own column too, never counted. Within one rank, a winner that only matched the saved row does not block a differing reading, which becomes the conflict with Replace unticked, as US-13 AC3 says; across ranks the winner holds the slot either way. A losing reading is hidden, as above, and never silently: one notice line counts it when it differs from the winner or either side was edited, and names the tests and days, never a value ("2 readings not saved: HDL Cholesterol, Sodium on 2 Sep 2025 already have another reading"; a test printed twice in one undated column not yet picked is "in the undated previous column", and several such columns make one group, "in the undated previous columns"). A reading equal to the saved row never overwrites a conflict another reading of the same test already put in its column. Editing a value rebuilds the matrix once, so the notice follows the edit. Save's own count is what it writes; its per-slot check stays as a backstop (review rounds 3 and 4, 2026-10-19). Save stays disabled until the user picks a past day for it (US-13 AC8) before its file's report day when that is known (the reviewed column date, else the printed one, even when the file shows no report column), so a stray "today", such as an iOS picker dismissed, never dates it. A pick on or after that day is refused and not written, and the header names every limit it has: "Pick a day before 10 Mar 2026", or "Pick a day in Jun 2025 before 10 Mar 2026" for a printed month. A report day moved to or before a picked undated day blocks Save until either moves. It is never saved on the report date or this month. A column whose cells are all cleared writes nothing and needs no day, so it never blocks saving the dated report (review 2026-10-19). Once picked it is an ordinary dated column: a primary reading still wins its (metric, day) slot, and a held value is context or a conflict, as in AC12. A tab opened before AC14 also sends ownDates: true but reads "undated" as a malformed date, so this widget's requests (single file and batch) also carry a separate undatedPrev: true, and api.lab-import-v2 keeps undated values only when both flags are present, the batch poll included. Two flags, not one versioned field: the widget deploys before the Fly server, and the live server's schema (6a4c8902) takes ownDates: true only, so ownDates: 2 would get a 400 there, while the old schema strips the extra key (review round 2, 2026-10-19). Usage signal: upload_outcome carries undatedPrevious, the integer count of value rows read from an undated previous column (core and lab rows; values, not files), zero omitted like every key, optional in the server schema, listed in the product-health LOOP.md key list. Tests: lab-extraction.test.ts "US-12 AC14" (both prompt rules in full, month-only marked undated with its printedMonth, neither in metadata; a bad, late or misplaced printedMonth dropped, late meaning after a full-day or a month-only report's month, the same and an earlier month kept; the marker kept with or without a report date, matched before it, exact only, left out in metadata; a dated column as before), api.lab-import-v2.test.ts (stripped without ownDates and with ownDates: true, a dated value kept; and with undatedPrev alone, a dated value kept; kept with both; ownDates other than true refused; single file and batch), upload-api.test.ts (both flags sent, and both bodies pass the live server's schema from 6a4c8902), DraftDateCell.test.tsx (an empty picker for a missing day, the placeholder), UploadModal.outcome.test.tsx and product-events.server.test.ts (the undatedPrevious count), mcp-tools.test.ts (the connector never offers it, even from a full parse) and ReviewTable.undated.test.tsx (a synthetic undated two-column table: its own first column, never merged; Save blocked until picked, even with a dated report; rows saved on the picked day; no dates anywhere needs both picks; a future pick blocked; a day on or after the report's blocks Save, and so does a report day picked later that falls before it; an all-cleared column needs no day; an edit or a clear before the pick survives it; a Replace tick never moves to another saved row; a held day gives context and a conflict; a pick on or after the report day refused with the limit named, the file's report date used with no report column; picked on another file's report day it keeps its own column, moving that file's date never moves it, and that file's reading wins the slot; two undated columns on one day save each slot once; with no dates anywhere both columns on one day block Save, and either column recovers it; an edit on a held day is a conflict judged by its edited value, Replace unticked, or saves nothing when it equals the saved row, and saves once the day moves on), and ReviewTable.slots.test.tsx (differing readings in both file orders: two undated columns, an undated over a dated previous one, lab rows; the notice counted and Save's count equal to what it writes; equal readings no notice; an edited loser counted; a held BP as context in the undated column; a Replace tick cleared with its box; every limit named; within one rank a held-equal winner lets a differing reading be the conflict, report or dated previous, both orders; across ranks it still holds the slot; an undated reading equal to the saved row is context in its own column under a report reading; editing the winner counts its equal loser; the notice names tests and days; a test twice in one unpicked undated column, core and lab, named in words; a test twice in one undated column, one equal to the saved row, keeps the differing one as the conflict in both orders).
  • AC15 (2026-10-20, issue #166: urine PCR and ACR results saved as serum creatinine; Brad approved: never guess a creatinine unit, show what was printed, urine or ratio rows are never core creatinine): a creatinine whose printed unit the unit table does not know, blank included, is never converted or saved, as core creatinine or as a lab row named creatinine ("Cr" alone stays a lab row: it may be chromium). Before refusing, the extractor's unit step (never lookupUnit) reads a creatinine unit once more with a trailing flag dropped (the AC8 value-flag grammar: H, L, HH, LL, *, ↑, ↓, any case, bracketed or not; a bare letter only after a space), "µmol/I" as µmol/L, "mg%" or "mg %" as mg/dL and "mcmol/L" as µmol/L; brackets and words are never stripped ("mg/dL (24h)" stays unknown; "mg/dL (urine)" is a urine unit). The rule lives in toUnifiedResult, so the single file, the batch and the Pages (BYOK) build apply it. The connector's import_documents (its metadata prompt mode) refuses only a urine unit (ratio, timed or urine-marked); a blank or other unknown unit is inferred from the number's size and stored in SI, as before (D7a, Brad 2026-10-20: "save it as SI unit"; AC16, US-13 AC11). mmol/L is no guess there: it converts exactly, ×1000 to µmol/L (0.09 is 90; 1.5 is 1500 and asks "Was this a blood test?"; 3.2 is 3200, which the save range refuses), never by the size guess, which read a urine ACR's 3.2 mmol/L as mg/dL, 283 µmol/L. A refused row comes back in refusedValues (metric, printed value and unit, reason; a ratio or timed urine unit, such as mg/mmol, mg/g, mg/24h or mL/min, any ratio whose mass or amount denominator names creatinine ("mg/g creatinine", "mg/mmol creat", "g/mol Cr"; "µmol/L creatinine" is no ratio), or a unit carrying a urine marker between letter edges ("urine", "urin", "urinary", "urina", "orina", "Harn", "moczu", whatever punctuation is around it), "U-Creat", a trailing " U" or ",U", or "(U)" (fix 3, Brad: never treat a urine row as blood creatinine; "U/L", "IU", "mU/L", "(uric)" and "(uncorrected)" are no marker), says "This unit is usually a urine result."; any other, mmol/L included, "This unit could not be read as a blood creatinine."). The review and done screens list it once under "Not saved", with "If one was a blood test, add it to your blood test table after saving"; there is no unit pick. A file whose only lab values were refused is not called "No blood test values found." and is not counted noValues. droppedValueCount stays parse drops only; the route adds refused rows to it only for a widget that does not send refusedRows: true, so an old tab still says values were dropped. import_documents lists each refused row as an unrecognized line, never as a candidate or a dropped value. Stated limit until the specimen guard (Step B): a urine creatinine printed in µmol/L or mg/dL as bare "Creatinine" still converts; above 500 µmol/L the review asks (US-13 AC11).   • AC17 (2026-10-20, Brad: "I don't see why the limit can't go up? just use the batch function?"; W42 saw 25 files refused at the daily limit): one IP may send as many files a day as one upload takes, 200, so any batch the upload window accepts fits a fresh day. One constant, IMPORT_LIMITS.websiteFiles, sets the window's cap (UploadModal.tsx MAX_FILES), the batch schema's maximum and the server's per-IP daily limit, which was 60 until now, so a batch of 61 to 200 files was refused whole. The per-machine $-cap (machineFiles, AI_DAILY_FILE_CAP, default 2000) stays the cost guardrail; raised from 500 to 2000 on 2026-10-21 (Brad: three people at 200/day could exhaust 500); 20 files or more already go through the Message Batches API at half price. Past the limit the server answers 429 "Daily upload limit reached. You can upload more tomorrow.", and the upload names each file "Not read. The daily upload limit was reached." A ZIP opens into more files than the window counted, so after unzipping the run sends the first 200 (ZIP members first) and names each one past them "Not read. It is over the 200-file limit for one upload. Upload it separately.", sending it nowhere; it counts under limitError in upload_outcome (zip-extract.ts caps one ZIP at the same constant). A file is charged unless its batch was definitely refused: the IP is refunded when the machine cap refuses, the busy answer (MAX_ACTIVE_BATCHES) is checked before any charge, and the IP and machine are refunded when createBatch throws BatchRefusedError (no API key, or a non-OK answer). A timeout, a network failure or an unreadable 200 keeps the charge, since the batch may exist. Ten IPs at 200 now reach the 2000-file machine cap. Tests: api.lab-import-v2.test.ts "US-12 AC17" (a fresh IP's preflight says 200; a 200-file batch is taken, the next file refused with that answer; no charge when the machine cap refuses or Anthropic refuses the batch; a timeout, a network failure or an unreadable 200 keeps it); anthropic.server.batch.test.ts "US-12 AC17" (BatchRefusedError for no key and a non-OK answer only); api.lab-import-v2.sweep.test.ts (busy charges nothing); UploadModal.outcome.test.tsx "US-12 AC17" (a ZIP of 200 plus one loose file: 200 sent, the loose file named and not sent).
  • AC18 (2026-10-20, Brad's decision; revised the same day after review: the poll never deletes, so a re-poll after a lost answer gets the results for at least 10 minutes): an ended batch is deleted at Anthropic, which otherwise keeps what we sent and what came back for up to 29 days. The 10-minute sweep does every delete (deleteBatch, DELETE /v1/messages/batches/{id}); the poll never does. A poll that reads a batch's results stamps it served (servedAt) and keeps answering it; the first sweep at least 10 minutes later deletes it, so it normally goes 10 to 20 minutes after its first answer, a re-poll in that time still gets the results, and a poll after that 404s. Each poll still needs the upload's capability token before it can share pending work or progress. Concurrent polls of one batch share one provider read, including its results fetch; value-free processing counts are reused for two seconds after the read finishes. Terminal health values serve only the current requests and are not retained on the server between polls. A sequential retry of an ended batch therefore still re-reads the provider. These retries return ordinary poll answers, not rate-limit errors. A failed read clears the pending work so another poll can retry. Progress and pending work use the existing batch table and its expiry, not a separate cache. Each response keeps the upload's day-column and refused-row flags. Tests: api.lab-import-v2.poll-reuse.test.ts (real action, proxy HMAC and provider parsing through synthetic fetch: no terminal health-value retention, ten-minute retry/expiry, concurrent poll coalescing, two-second processing pacing, capability isolation before progress/pending work, rejection recovery, upload-time response projections, capacity/sweep recovery and unserved expiry; also US-15 AC34's once-only stop reporting). A served batch is judged by servedAt alone, so one first served past its hour still gets its 10 minutes. The sweep also deletes a batch nobody polled to the end (the tab closed), an hour after its upload. Only an ended batch can be deleted, so a failed delete cancels the batch (POST …/cancel), and each sweep retries until it is gone (a 404 counts as gone). It stops trying 25 hours after the upload, since every batch ends within 24. A delete failure logs its HTTP status alone, to the console and Sentry (Lab import: batch delete failed), never a provider body. The sweep timer lives in app/lib/lab-batches.server.ts with the batch table, and the authenticated server action arms it once (armSweep) after the first successful batch upload; neither module starts a timer that reaches server-only code on import, so the provider deletion import never reaches the client build. A denied upload does not arm it. It still cleans up uploads that are never polled, and its ten-minute phase starts at that first successful upload. Test: api.lab-import-v2.sweep.test.ts "arms once" (non-aligned idle start, repeated uploads and never-polled cleanup); npm run build verifies the client/server boundary. Sweeps never overlap (an in-flight guard), and the interval does not hold the process open (unref), as rate-limiter.ts does. Residual: the list of batches to delete is in memory on one machine, so a restart, or a machine stopped while idle, before the sweep leaves a batch to Anthropic's 29 days; so does an upload whose answer was lost (a timeout, a network error or an unreadable reply), since the batch may exist at Anthropic but was never tracked (adversary R2 on PR #203). No batch path elsewhere: the connector import (US-35) calls extractOrClassify file by file, and the self-host BYOK "batch" is a client-side queue of single calls. Tests: anthropic.server.batch.test.ts "US-12 AC18: deleteBatch" (the DELETE request; a 404 counts as gone; a 409 cancels, logs the status and no body; a network failure is false, never a throw); api.lab-import-v2.test.ts "US-12 AC18" (a second poll of an ended batch gets the same results, nothing deleted); api.lab-import-v2.sweep.test.ts (a sweep 1 ms after the first answer keeps the batch, a re-poll just short of 10 minutes still gets the results, the first sweep 10 minutes on deletes it, 404 after; a first answer just past the hour still gets its 10 minutes; an unserved batch deleted after an hour, not before, and not again; a failing delete retried each sweep, given up after 25 hours).

US-14 · Document archive

As a user, my uploaded reports/letters become organized markdown documents (+ original file when my cloud can hold it) that I can reopen in a lightbox.

  • Note (2026-09-04, US-35 AC8): a file imported through the connector lands here as a metadata-only row — fileRef: "", contentHash, sniffed mimeType, extractedText: "", metadata.importedVia: "connector" — with the original left where the user put it; a lab report's row takes the shape the website's upload writes (pathology_report, hidden from the Documents list). The website archives the blob behind such a row on the next upload of the same bytes (US-13 AC1).
  • AC1 (2026-10-20, PR #186 by @robertaustinbell; moved here from US-12): GitHub and WebDAV document reads and writes URL-encode each logical path segment once, preserving folder separators and literal #, % (including the text %23), spaces and Unicode. A lone UTF-16 surrogate, including one created by title truncation, keeps the URL boundary’s previous U+FFFD replacement instead of throwing; valid surrogate pairs and a leading U+FEFF are preserved. Stored document refs and title sanitization do not change. WebDAV keeps the configured base URL's escaping and optional trailing slash. GitHub keeps its default-branch and SHA retry behavior and its private-repository write guard. Legacy reads: before this change the raw ref was joined onto the URL, so a document whose ref holds # was stored under the name cut at the #, and literal %xx text was decoded by the server. A read that gets a 404 at the encoded URL, for a ref whose old raw-join URL differs, retries once at that old URL (fragment dropped) and returns those bytes; a plain ref makes one request. Writes always use the new encoding. Two titles that differed only after a # were saved to the same cut name before this change, so the later file overwrote the earlier one; that earlier file cannot be recovered. Tests: storage/document-url.test.ts (real adapters, mocked HTTP requests, including WebDAV collection creation; legacy reads seeded at the old location for # and literal %20, both providers); live-provider acceptance is not verified.
  • AC2 (2026-10-20, security; adversary R2 on PR #186): a document's file path never leaves its folder. The date in a ref comes from the model reading the uploaded file (reportDate, documentDate, only z.string().nullable() in the extraction schema), so a crafted PDF could return "../../x" and point a WebDAV or GitHub URL outside the configured folder. buildDocumentRef takes the date only when it is a real calendar day (isCalendarDay); anything else, like a missing date, becomes today's local date. The row's own date field is unchanged. Tests: document-path.test.ts "US-14 AC2" (../../x, a date with a slash, .., an impossible day, a short date, empty, null and undefined all give today's date in one folder).
  • AC3 (2026-10-20, security; found by an outside scanner, verified in code): an archived original never runs script on the app's origin. "View original file" opens a blob: URL, and a top-level blob: URL runs with the page's origin, beside the cloud tokens in localStorage; an archived SVG or HTML file could read them. (a) The viewer opens a file in a tab only when its ref's extension names a passive type (.pdf, .png, .jpg/.jpeg, .heic) and the stored bytes carry that type or none (Dropbox and GitHub return untyped bytes); it re-types the blob as that type before opening. Anything else, an SVG, HTML, XML, a .docx, a mismatch (.png bytes typed image/svg+xml), an unknown or missing extension, is re-typed application/octet-stream and downloaded under its ref's name, never opened. A stored type that is a non-standard alias (image/jpg, image/pjpeg, application/x-pdf, as WebDAV or Drive may return) is a mismatch too: the original downloads rather than opens, which fails safe. This covers SVGs already in users' archives. (b) The upload reads a photo only by allow-list: JPEG, PNG, HEIC or HEIF, by type or extension. Any other image/* (SVG, WebP, GIF) is no longer read as a photo; it gets the "Could not open it ... not a PDF, photo or .docx file" notice (US-12 AC9) and nothing is archived. Tests: file-kinds.test.ts and image-resize.test.ts "US-14 AC3"; DocumentLightbox.test.tsx (an SVG, a .png typed SVG and a .docx download, a PDF from untyped bytes opens as a PDF).
  • AC4 (2026-10-22, redone from PR #164 by @robertaustinbell; AC1 was taken by PR #186): a document row whose blob write failed keeps its bytes' contentHash. Before, it was saved with an empty hash, so a later upload of the same bytes could not find it and the document was listed twice. Now the row is a pending original, as a connector row is (US-13 AC1): a later upload replaces it, a new row with the blob, every such row of its kind is tombstoned, but only once the blob lands. A second failure behind a held row, a connector's or an earlier failed save's alike, is a settled outcome, never an error, so an original that can never be stored (a size cap) does not loop on "Failed to save". The held details stay, unless the review changed the title or date: then a new metadata-only row (same hash, the reviewed title and date) replaces the held rows. Either way the done screen says "The original file couldn't be stored; its details are saved." (unstored), never a silent checkmark. The rows replaced are read inside the commit from the record as it then is, so a same-hash row merged in from another device during the upload goes too (orchestrator calls 2026-10-22, after review). A first failure still degrades to a metadata-only row as before. It is replaced only by an upload of its own kind (Brad 2026-10-19): a lab archive by a lab archive, a shown document by a shown document, read by isLabArchiveDocument, not by the document type, which is the model's per-run guess. Otherwise both stay live: rows merge with deleted OR-ed, so a letter tombstoned by a lab re-read of the same bytes would be gone for good. A deselected letter is archived only behind a shown-document row, never a lab-archive one. One helper (pendingRowsFor) picks these rows for the card and the store. The review card of a document that will replace them starts from the newest one's title and date (2026-10-22), a missing date staying unknown, so a retry shows the earlier edits, and the user can still change them; what the card shows is what is saved (US-13 AC6). Hashless rows saved before this cannot be matched and are not migrated. Accepted trade-offs (orchestrator call 2026-10-22): a held row's unknown date wins over a fresh extraction, so a date the user cleared stays cleared even when the new read has one; and older same-kind rows for the same bytes (say from another device) are replaced although the card shows only the newest. Tests: roadmap-store-archive-retry.test.ts, roadmap-store-data-safety.test.ts, UploadModal.session.test.tsx "US-14 AC4"; ReviewTable.document-dates.test.tsx "starts from the failed row" and "starts from the newest such row".
  • Tests: ✅ document-path taxonomy; ✅ view-original type gate (AC3); ✅ failed-blob retry by kind (AC4); 🟡 archive-payloads synthesis; ❌ store deleteDocument/readDocumentFile. Deferred.

Epic E — Chat

US-15 · Ask about my plan

As a user, I can ask the assistant about my suggestions; it answers with my plan as context, cites Brad's content, and its name matches the store I'm on (Brad AI / MicroVitamin).

Decided (Brad, 2026-09-10). The blog chat bubble (widget-src/src/site-chat.tsx) and the chatbot embed (widget-src/src/chatbot-embed.tsx) both read the widget's cached inputs out of localStorage (loadGuestInputs()) and send them as context with every message, and neither bundle sets VITE_LOCAL_FIRST, so the server stores the whole transcript. Both open questions are answered. The cached values keep being sent: the answer is worse without them, and they are the person's own values, already stored in that browser (since AC10, 2026-09-26, that includes their saved measurements, which may have arrived by a lab import, another device or an assistant, not only what they typed). The transcripts join the 30-day purge, so the text does not outlive the audit that needs it (AC8). The README and the privacy addendum now say that.

  • AC1: Server-proxied on Shopify surfaces; BYOK on Pages (chat reaches no Brad server there; the build itself still calls api.google-token for Google sign-in, api.reminders-v2 if the user enrols, and Sentry for scrubbed errors).
  • AC2: chat_opened now measures adoption.
  • AC4 (2026-09-07): Main-LLM, router and classifier failure telemetry contains only bounded diagnostic categories and numeric timing/counts. User messages, assistant content, provider response bodies, author identifiers and arbitrary error strings never enter Sentry events or failure-path console logs. Conversation storage is unchanged.
  • AC4b: Discord admits at most three active responses and ten waiting messages. Further eligible arrivals receive the busy reply. Completion, provider failure or a failed wait releases its reserved capacity. Tests: discord-bot.queue.test.ts.
  • AC3: A transient upstream failure — a 5xx whose body is not our handler's JSON (the Shopify proxy / Fly edge answered, not our route) — is retried once before chat surfaces an error. The send POST is retried only within an existing conversation; a thread's FIRST message is never auto-retried (on the stored surfaces a retry could mint a ghost conversation). On the stored surfaces the server-side dedup absorbs an identical resend; on the widget (AC7, nothing stored) the client re-serves its own last reply when the resend is byte-identical to its last user turn, and otherwise a retry costs one more LLM call and no row. Added 2026-08-12 from Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-1M / -22 (sentry-fix loop; scoped per independent review); widget wording 2026-09-10.
  • AC6 (2026-09-09): GET/POST/DELETE reject invalid conversation IDs before database use. Omitted/null POST IDs remain new conversations. Route error diagnostics, including detached failures, never include raw database errors or IDs. api.chat-privacy.test.ts checks SDK envelopes and console output.
  • AC6a: A supplied stored-conversation ID on GET, POST or DELETE must belong to the authenticated principal, including a guest, before transcript reads, model work or deletion. Missing and foreign parents receive the same not-found response. A GET naming an id with neither a session token nor a customer answers not-found without creating a guest session. A guest is its session token plus its IP, so a guest whose IP changes no longer owns its thread: a guest's not-found carries that guest's own session token (one the changed IP may just have minted). When a guest's send answers not-found for the stored thread, the server has made no chat write or model call (a guest session may have been created), so the chat client keeps the handed-back session, sends the message once in a new conversation on it, shows that thread and drops the unreachable old thread from its list; the message is neither lost nor sent twice, and the restart mints no second session. A signed-in customer's not-found is shown, never forked into a new thread. The resend carries the handed-back token directly, so it works even when the browser refuses to store it. Opening or deleting a guest thread that answers not-found also keeps the handed-back session and drops that thread from the list. A sessionless GET's not-found carries no token. Tests: api.chat-ownership.test.ts, chat-api.test.ts, useChatState.test.tsx.
  • AC7 (2026-09-10, Brad's decision): A turn from the main widget — the surface that sends the health record with every message, identified by localFirst: true in the POST body, which only the VITE_LOCAL_FIRST builds send — writes no chat_conversations row and no chat_messages row: not the question, not the reply, not a title (titles are the first words of the question). The widget sends that conversation's earlier turns in the request from its own chat-history.json; the server uses them for the prompt and discards them. What the server keeps is one chat_match_events row per answered turn: the question text verbatim (Brad, 2026-09-10 — a number scrub was built and then dropped as over-complication: an adversarial review found nine shapes still leaking through it, so a scrub good enough to trust needed a second round of rules, and routing is about topics, not magnitudes; the audit needs the real question), the prior-turn context the router saw (on the stored surfaces only — a widget row keeps just platform: 'widget', so it can never hold a second question), the matched handles, classification, router timings, and the fallback flag and category, so article matching can be audited. Honest limits: a question can name a value ("my LDL is 4.2"), so this is "no reply and no record", not "no health information". Narrowed 2026-10-15 (US-15 AC33 review, S2; Brad confirmed 2026-10-16): the widget row now stores the question with every run of digits, in any script, masked to # ("my LDL is #"), so a value typed into the chat for run_roadmap never reaches the row. A closed list of topic names that hold a digit stays whole when it stands alone (HbA1c, B1 to B12, D2, D3, K1, K2, GLP-1, SGLT2, omega-3, CoQ10, PCSK9, T1DM, T2DM, type 1, type 2, Zone 2), so "HbA1c 41" is stored as "HbA1c #" and a glued "LDL4.1" as "LDL#"; router_raw and router_error get the same mask (third review, 2026-10-15). This narrows the verbatim-question decision above: the topic words stay for the article-matching audit, the numbers go. A number written in words ("four point one") still passes. Amended 2026-09-10 (public-repo privacy audit): the question text is now kept for 30 days, long enough to audit article matching, and then removed; the handles it matched stay on as counts, so the audit signal outlives the text. A daily cron does the removal on every platform (app/lib/chat-purge-cron.server.ts, lock chat_text_purge): past 30 days message goes null, router_context.first/.recent are dropped, and router_raw and router_error are blanked too (2026-09-10 — the router's raw output is the model's answer about the question and the error text can quote it), while matched_handles, classification, the timings and is_fallback stay forever. guest_chat_sessions.ip_address holds a salted HMAC of the address (hashClientIp, HKDF from the app-proxy secret — equal addresses still match, no address reads back) and the session's audit entry carries no address at all, so a retained question is no longer linkable to an IP. The blog chat bubble (site-chat), chatbot-embed, Discord and YouTube store messages exactly as before, for router optimisation. router_context.platform names the surface on every row (widget / shopify / discord / youtube); the chat_match_events → chat_messages and → chat_conversations foreign keys are gone, so a user's delete no longer removes router telemetry. A widget row carries only a whitelisted set of columns (redactForWidget), so a reply or error text cannot ride along unseen. Usage signal: daily chat_match_events rows with router_context->>'platform' = 'widget' against the prior 7-day shopify total (widget and blog were one number before this change), chat_opened steady, Sentry "Chat sendMessage failed" flat. No new product_events name: trackProductEvent fires once per session per name, so a per-turn event cannot live there. The history went with the decision (Brad, 2026-09-10): the 266 widget conversations stored before it — 211 guest-owned plus 55 from before the local-first cutover — were deleted on 2026-09-10 (the statement lives in supabase/rls-policies.sql). The 8 profile-owned blog conversations were kept: that surface still stores transcripts, and Brad wants them for router optimisation.

  • AC10 (2026-09-26, Brad approved; wording corrected 2026-09-28 after adversarial review): The blog chat bubble and the chatbot embed send the saved record: the saved profile, the latest saved value of each measurement with its date, and the medications and screenings on record. The embed is not muted for a returning user with a saved weight, or with only blood tests. It reads the context when each message is sent, not when the page loads.   • AC11 (2026-09-28, from the /simplify altitude review): The chat's plan counts the medications and screenings on record.

- The bug: before this AC, the Shopify chat server read the medication and screening lists as flat objects. Both clients send lists, so the server got nothing, and it computed the plan as if none were recorded. Given rosuvastatin 40 mg and ApoB 1.0, the model was handed a "start a statin" suggestion. The Pages chat already converted the lists, so the two chats disagreed.

- Now: one health-core builder feeds both. Every field is sanitized before it can reach the prompt:

- medication keys are allowlisted;

- numbers are bounded;

- a screening date must be a real calendar date (month 01 to 12, and a day that exists in that month and year): screeningsToInputs drops any other, for the widget's plan, the chat, the reminder schedule and get_plan's due list alike, so '2020-99' can no longer roll forward and read as "up to date", or schedule a reminder. A "last done" date (the six _last_date keys) must also fall in the current month or before it, as the form's own year and month lists do; the five _followup_date keys keep accepting future dates, because the form asks when a follow-up is scheduled;

- strings are capped.

- Drug names: a listed name passes through. An unlisted name still counts in the plan, exactly as the widget reads it, but the prompt shows it as "unlisted". The prompt never says "other", which is the form's own "Other GLP-1" choice and means something to the plan. An empty name is left out of the prompt, and a non-string name (null, a number or an object in a hand-edited file) drops its row, as medicationsToInputs does for the widget's plan. A name outside the character bound becomes a placeholder that means nothing to the plan. A test pins that no suggestion title carries a drug name, so an unlisted name never reaches the model.

- Doses: the plan reads the raw dose, as the widget does. The prompt drops a dose outside its range.

- Data sent: the browser sends only the fields the builder uses: no row ids and no timestamps.

- The values the model reads are the values the plan used (Codex, 2026-09-28): latestValues come from the snapshot the plan was computed from, so an unsaved value the widget sends stands in for the saved one, and the dated series fills only the fields the snapshot lacks. Before, the saved series overwrote the snapshot, so the model could explain a plan built on 3.4 while being told 1.0.

- Both chats read the same context (round 3, 2026-09-28): the Pages chat plans from the context the widget supplies, with unsaved typed values and lent drafts, as the Shopify chat does (AC10). Every chat on the page supplies that context, so the old fallback to the saved file was dead code and is gone.

  • AC14 (2026-09-29, chat audit F2): a refusal (HTTP 200, stop_reason: 'refusal') is a third outcome beside answer and fallback.
