  • AC16 (2026-09-29, Brad's decision, chat audit F3): the web chat streams the answer. The widget POSTs stream: true; the route answers application/x-ndjson, one line per thinking or text delta, then a done line carrying exactly the JSON the unstreamed reply would have been. A refusal or fallback done line carries isFallback: true, and the client replaces what streamed with its content. The body decides the path, not the header: an application/json answer (an older server, an error status) takes the unstreamed path unchanged; any other 200 is read as NDJSON when its first line starts {"type":, so a proxy that rewrote the type still streams, and fails as before otherwise. Without stream: true the route is unchanged. Persistence and telemetry run after the stream completes; chat_timing adds streamed and firstTokenMs. Discord, YouTube and the Pages BYOK chat do not stream. CHAT_STREAMING=false on the server is the off switch: the route ignores stream: true and answers JSON, which the client reads unchanged (default on; docs/deploy-runbook.md). A stream cut off before done is reported as a network error and not retried, because the server finishes and persists the turn after a disconnect, so a retry would duplicate it on the stored surfaces; the pre-stream transient retry (AC3) is unchanged. Tests: app/lib/anthropic.server.stream.test.ts, app/lib/chat.server.refusal.test.ts, app/routes/api.chat-stream.test.ts, widget-src/src/lib/chat-api.stream.test.ts.

  • AC26 (2026-10-04, Brad's decision; on 2026-09-27 two pasted analysis templates were stored at exactly 500 characters, cut mid-word before any lab value): a pasted lab report or "act as a doctor" template reaches the model whole. The router telemetry row does not grow with the message: chat_match_events keeps at most the first 500 characters of the question, and of the earlier turns in its router context, on every web surface (MATCH_EVENT_MESSAGE_CHARS in api.chat.ts), as it did before; the router still reads 2,000. Accepted consequence, confirmed by Brad 2026-10-04: the stored surfaces (blog bubble, chatbot embed) now keep transcripts of up to 8,000 characters per message in chat_messages for the 30-day AC8 window, up from 500.   • AC28 (2026-10-12, Brad approved; evidence: chat-health W41, docs/loops/chat-health/2026-W41.md): a router reply that corrects itself still routes. On 2026-10-07 the router sent a JSON object, then "Wait — correction", then a second object; the first-to-last-brace parse threw, and the turn got no handles and a router_error. Now, when that parse fails, the router takes the reply's top-level {…} objects (a brace inside a JSON string does not count) and uses the last one that parses and holds a handles list, so a trailing note or example object never overrides the answer. A reply the old parse accepted parses exactly as before; a reply with no such object fails with the same router_error as before. Known limit, accepted: when two handles objects are offered as alternatives, the later one wins, as a correction does. extractJsonObject is unchanged, since lab extraction shares it. The router harness (tools/test-chatbot-matching.ts) uses the same parser (app/lib/router-reply.ts) and counts a reply nothing parses, or one with no handles list, as an error, like an API error: printed, counted in apiErrors, and the run exits non-zero. Before, it scored that reply as a silent ∅. Tests: app/lib/router-reply.test.ts, app/lib/chat-router.server.test.ts, tools/test-chatbot-matching.test.ts.

  • AC31 (2026-10-12, Brad, issue #135; reworked 2026-10-14, Brad: "when someone says analyse my numbers, we should run it through my roadmap algorithm"; this was AC29 until the merge with main, whose AC29 and AC30 came first): "analyse my data" reports the roadmap's own verdicts; the model does not compute them. The chat context (buildChatContextJson, health-core chat-context.ts) carries what the plan code already computes, and nothing new: each card's description (the text the user sees), derivedValues (BMI, BMI category, waist-to-height ratio, non-HDL cholesterol, eGFR; the BMI category and eGFR withheld for a known minor, as plan.ts withholds them) and missingInputs (the plan's gating inputs it lacks: missingPlanInputs, moved from plan.ts to calculations.ts and shared). The descriptions come from the plan run over the medications the prompt shows, so an unlisted drug name or an out-of-range dose never reaches the prompt (the Lp(a) card prints the statin's name and dose); a card that run lacks keeps its title and has no description. Payload for the OA1 profile: 3,187 to 7,603 bytes; 7,775 with AC33's units (re-measured 2026-10-15; the AC31 builder gives 7,615 on today's fixture). The rule, verbatim in app/lib/chat-system-prompt.md ("Your role"), 778 characters (677 until the AC33 review of 2026-10-15 replaced "what is on target", which invited the model to grade values the plan gives no card, with the no-card clause; the rule before AC31 had 1,190): When asked to analyse or review their data with no topic named ("analyse my data", "how am I doing?"), report what their roadmap already says: what needs work and their plan, urgent and attention cards first and the info cards in one sentence; for a value with no card or verdict in the data, say the roadmap raises no card for it rather than calling it on target. Take every verdict from the user data block (the cards and derivedValues); never judge a value against a threshold yourself. If the roadmap does not assess something or lacks a value (missingInputs), say so plainly; testing is for their doctor. With no profile, the roadmap cannot assess them yet: say it needs at least their sex and height, not that their data is empty (they may have entered other values), and do not build a plan. With no profile, values pasted into the message are no longer graded (the previous rule counted them). Why the no-profile sentence: production sends '{}' (EMPTY_CHAT_CONTEXT) whenever sex or height is missing, even when other values are entered (until AC36, 2026-10-18: now only for an empty form). Measured 2026-10-14, 3 runs each, through production resolveChatContext/buildSystemBlocks (user_context fixtures), arms production (origin/main prompt and builder) / previous (the 1,190-character rule) / shipped: OA1 3/3, 3/3, 3/3; OA2 3/3, 3/3, 3/3; E1 (empty profile) 6/6, 6/6, 6/6; X3 (values entered, no sex) 1/6, 5/6, 6/6 (production says "your health data is empty"; the first shipped wording, without "not that their data is empty", 4/6); X4 (values pasted, no profile) 2/3, 2/3, 1/3 (shipped: one reply was a pre-fill tool call with no text, one opened a numbered list with "To get your plan:", which the check's pattern counts; the first shipped wording 3/3). Read answers, shipped: no card ids in 15 own-data answers (previous 1, production 0); the rule's own labels ("what's on target", "what needs work", "three parts", "the suggested plan") recited in 5 of 6 empty-profile answers on the previous rule and 2 of 6 on the shipped one, which also says "I won't judge the numbers myself" in 2 of 3 X4 answers; with data, every answer orders attention cards first, gives the cards' own grading, names ApoB and creatinine as missing and leaves testing to the doctor (production added Lp(a) testing the plan does not suggest); two empty-profile answers say "the data block is empty". The rule lives in the prompt and the payload; the router is unchanged. Usage signal: the chat-health loop's weekly count of these asks from chat_match_events, and these checks staying green.

  • AC33 (2026-10-14, Brad: when a user types values that are not in their profile, the bot runs the real algorithm code on the saved profile plus the stated values and answers from its output, never from its own reading of the algorithm document; saving stays the user's job; revised 2026-10-15 after a second adversarial review, below): the widget's chat and the Pages chat have a run_roadmap tool (health-core run-roadmap.ts). Its input is up to 20 stated values (field, value, unit, optional date; the form tool's field enum; the unit read through the shared unit table, so an unknown unit is rejected and the prompt keeps "ask, never guess") and an optional sex, height ({ value, unit }, cm or in, through the same unit table; feet and inches as total inches) and age (whole years), or a birthYear only when that is what the user said (2026-10-16: "born 1974" needs no arithmetic by a model that may not know today's date; age wins when both come and both are usable, and a refused age, not a number or out of range, falls back to a usable stated birth year (2026-10-18, Brad: a malformed age used to hide a valid birth year)). These make a plan for a user with no profile, and they also stand in for a saved profile's sex, height or birth year for this answer (adversary R9, 2026-10-16: the behaviour since the start, now written down). runRoadmap turns the age into a birth year from today's date, in January, so the plan's age is the stated one and the US-07 AC6 gate is exactly under 18: 17 is a minor, 18 is not (adversary R3, 2026-10-16: the model used to compute "this year minus age" without knowing the date). A stated age is rounded down (16.5 is 16), and an age or birth year sent as a numeric string is read, so a usable age is never refused: with no saved birth year a refused age leaves no age and so no minor gate (adversary rounds 3-4). A stated birth year is used as stated, without a month (a different year drops the saved month), so the gate keeps its conservative no-month reading. The tool's own description carries its usage rules: call it when the user states values not in their saved data and wants them assessed or analysed; use only the user's own values, not a family member's; pass exactly the stated values and units, and sex, height or age only if stated in this conversation; on an ambiguous unit ask first and grade nothing; answer only from the result; say nothing is saved; offer to pre-fill measurements, never sex or height, which go to the roadmap tool (2026-10-20, US-15 AC36). Neither prompt names the tool. It is offered only on a turn whose latest or previous user message holds a digit (health-core chatToolsFor, on the server and in the Pages chat; the form tools keep their rule): it reads only stated values, and offered on every turn it changed answers to questions it has nothing to do with (below); the previous message counts so that "Lp(a) 75", the unit asked, then "nmol/L" still runs it. Tools render before the system prompt, so the widget's chat has two prompt-cache shapes (the form tools, and the form tools plus run_roadmap), each cached on its own. runRoadmap lays the values over the request's own guestInputs (a stated value is the latest for this answer only; nothing is saved) and returns exactly buildChatContextJson's output, the same anti-injection boundary as the user data block, beside applied (field names) and rejected (field names and fixed reasons, never a value or the model's own string). It refuses, each with a fixed reason, in this order: a date that is not a real calendar day, or is later than today anywhere on Earth (record-edits' resolveRecordedAt with latestDayOnEarth); a dated value older than the newest saved point for its field ("older than the saved value"; an undated value is today's), checked next, so a dated old value, usable or not, never touches a newer saved one; a missing or non-numeric value or unit ("value or unit missing or not a number"); an unknown unit ("ask the user which unit"); a number below US-36 AC4's unit-swap floors (UNIT_SWAP_FLOORS: LDL "3.4 mg/dL" is 0.09 mmol/L), or an HbA1c or creatinine under 20 stated in its SI unit (mmol/mol, µmol/L: "6.1 mmol/mol" is a percentage, "1.1 µmol/L" is mg/dL), again "ask the user which unit" (adversary R7, 2026-10-16: the band is for the SI unit only, so "HbA1c 3.9 %", 19.1 mmol/mol, is read); a value outside the input schema's range, with a reason by kind: blood pressure above ("treat it as a possible emergency and advise urgent medical care") or below ("treat it as possibly dangerous and advise urgent medical care if they feel faint, dizzy or unwell"), a lab above ("above the highest value the roadmap records in this unit: ask the user to confirm the value and unit; if it is right, suggest they discuss it with their doctor"; adversary R4; Brad confirmed the wording 2026-10-16) or below ("ask the user to confirm the value and unit"; reached only by an HbA1c or creatinine stated in % or mg/dL, since every other lab's ask-unit floor sits above its range's floor), and weight, waist or a stated height ("outside what the roadmap records: ask the user to check the value and unit"). Every refusal of a stated value except "older" and the "later" duplicate takes that field out of the run (adversary R2, 2026-10-16: before, only an out-of-range value did): its saved value and dated series are dropped, and so is any stated value for it dated that day or earlier, the same day included ("a later or same-day value for this field could not be used, so this one was not used either"; Codex R1, 2026-10-16: "BP 118/76 on 2026-10-14, 260/155 on 2026-10-15" used to plan from 118/76). So neither a saved number nor an older stated one answers for a value the roadmap cannot hold, and a newer usable value still answers over an older refused one (except height: it barely changes, so an out-of-range stated height keeps the saved one and the plan still runs; orchestrator, 2026-10-15); a blood pressure that is not a usable pair (one number stated, either refused, or the two dated on different days), which refuses both and takes the saved pair out, unless every stated number (one or both) is older than the saved reading, which then stands (adversary round 2, 2026-10-16: one older number used to remove the saved pair); a bare heightCm ("value or unit missing or not a number": height comes as { value, unit }); and any stated age or birth year when the saved profile is a known minor (US-07 AC6). A field with any value past the 20-value cap is taken out of the run, even when an earlier value for it was read: a history pasted in date order puts the newest values last (2026-10-16). A refused age, birth year or sex keeps the saved one (simplified 2026-10-16, Brad's Option A: with ages rounded down a refused one is only nonsense, and removing the saved one lost the inputs eGFR needs). The protein-target card is withheld, with a reason saying so, only when the run has no eGFR although the saved data had one or a creatinine was stated in this run (the reason names the cause, 2026-10-18, Brad: when the run used a creatinine but has no age to read it by, it is "the protein target depends on kidney function, which needs the user's age: ask for their age", under age; when a value was refused, it stays "… left out until the refused value is confirmed", under creatinine): without an eGFR the card falls back to the standard 1.2 g/kg, which would quietly drop a kidney adjustment (Codex rounds 2-3, adversary round 4). A saved creatinine with nothing refused shows the card as the saved plan does, kidney-adjusted when it applies; a known minor's eGFR is hidden, not lost, so it never triggers this; the potassium advice already needs a known eGFR of 45 or more, so it fails safe. withRoadmapRound is the one loop all three callers share (the website chat's getChatCompletion, the Pages chat's sendMessage, the answer-check harness): at most one round and one plan run. The values of every run_roadmap call in the first reply merge into one run under the one 20-value cap (each profile field from the first call that gives it); the first call gets the result and every other gets "Not run: one run_roadmap per turn; use the first result." A form tool beside it gets "Pre-filled for the user to review and Save." (or the medication line) only when parseProposedEdit accepts it, since the client applies exactly those, and otherwise "Not applied: the edit did not pass the form's checks, so nothing was pre-filled or saved." The first reply, thinking signatures included, is replayed unmodified; the second call carries tool_choice: none, and its text is the answer; usage is the two calls' sum; a failed second call is the ordinary api-error fallback with no tool data, and keeps the first call's usage and the round's counts for chat_timing, the audit row and the counter. The streamed chat shows "Running your numbers through the roadmap" between the calls. Units: the chat context carries units, each latestValues field's SI unit (FIELD_UNITS, the field-keyed table get_plan publishes under US-32 AC35, moved from plan.ts to mappings.ts and shared), so a bare SI number is labelled whatever profile.unitSystem says. The Pages compact prompt's form-tools line reads "without these tools … Use them only when …", so it no longer forbids every tool; nothing else in either prompt changed for AC33. Privacy: the tool's input and output never reach chat_timing (which gains only the flag roadmapRun), Sentry or any log.   • AC34 (2026-10-16, Brad's decision, no benchmark): the classifier, lab extraction (single call, batch and BYOK upload) and the BYOK chat run on Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5), up from Haiku 4.5. Each request sends thinking: {type: 'disabled'} and no sampling param, built by modelParams. Thinking is off for parity, since Haiku 4.5 never thought, and because extraction must still fit the connector's 40 s budget (US-35 AC5). Haiku 5.5 answers temperature with a 400, so the temperature: 0 shape and its branch are gone; an effort level sends adaptive thinking, as on the Sonnet 5 family. It also rejects an assistant prefill with a 400, so a malformed extraction answer is re-sent as the same request, once, within the same deadline, where it used to be re-sent with a { prefill; a second failure throws the same class-only error. Responses are read by block type, because a Haiku 5.5 response can begin with a thinking block. Cost: $0.10 / $0.50 per MTok for prompts up to 100K tokens ($0.50 / $2.50 above), a tenth of Haiku 4.5's $1 / $5, on about 30% more tokens for the same text; one live smoke call per hop (synthetic input, 2026-10-16) cost under $0.001 in all. The classifier's 923-token prompt now caches (Haiku 4.5 needed 4,096). Its output cap rose from 8 to 16 tokens: in the smoke, "MEASUREMENT", the longest label, stopped at max_tokens with all 8 used (the raw text was not kept, so whether the label alone or text after it took them is not known). The label is now read from the answer's first word, so text after it never turns a good label into ERROR, which silently fires the router; the harnesses (tools/test-classifier.ts, tools/youtube-comment-dryrun.ts) send 16 and parse the same way. Extraction caps rose for the ~30% token growth: 8192 to 12288 for full transcription in a batch and on the BYOK upload, and to 10000 for the website's single file (see below), 2048 to 3072 for the connector's metadata mode; unused tokens are not billed. Refusals, new with Haiku 5.5's safety classifiers and with no server-side fallback: an extraction refusal fails the file at once, with no outer retry, since the same request usually refuses again; a refused batch request, which still comes back succeeded, is a file error, never a parse of its partial text; on the Pages build the shared transport (byok-anthropic.ts) turns stop_reason: 'refusal' into an error carrying the website chat's line (AC14: a health-topic or unknown category points to a doctor), so partial text is never a chat answer, saved history or lab values. Not parity in every respect: with thinking off and no effort sent, Haiku 5.5 runs at its default effort, medium, and at temperature 1, the only value it accepts, so extraction is no longer deterministic between runs; every value still passes the user's review before it is saved. Extraction quality at this setting was not benchmarked (Brad's decision). Tests: models.test.ts (both Haiku 5.5 shapes, the production pins, Haiku 4.5 now throws, harness pricing), anthropic.server.retry.test.ts and byok-upload.test.ts (the re-send is the same body: no assistant turn, thinking disabled, no temperature; a leading thinking block is skipped), anthropic.server.batch.test.ts (the batch params; a result that starts with thinking), byok-chat.test.ts (the Pages chat body), chat-classifier.server.test.ts (the classifier body, its cap and the first-word parse), the refusal cases in byok-upload.test.ts, anthropic.server.batch.test.ts and anthropic.server.retry.test.ts. Follow-up (2026-10-16, after review). Extraction is one loop on one deadline: at most two calls per file, on the website and in the connector alike. The outer retry that made a malformed file cost four identical full-length calls is gone, so these now fail the file at once where they used to get one more try after 1 s: a transport failure that outlasts fetchAnthropicRaw's own two HTTP attempts, an HTTP 500 or 429 (neither in its retry list), and an empty answer that ended normally (thrown as "No text" before the parse, so it is not re-sent). A refusal or a max_tokens stop fails the file at once, with no re-send, since the same request stops the same way; only an answer that ended normally but will not parse is re-sent. Each gets its own file notice on every path (single call, batch, BYOK) and both builds: "Not read. Claude declined to read this file, so trying again will not help." and "Not read. The file is too long to read in one go.", counted as refused and tooLong in upload_outcome (US-12 AC10). The website answers such a single file 422 with errorCode: 'refused' or 'too_long' and no document text, and a batch result carries the same code. Monitoring: each stopped website file sends one Sentry message, Lab import: extraction refused or Lab import: extraction too_long, tagged with its path and, on a refusal, the bounded category, never text; a batch's messages go once, from the poll that sees it end, however often it is polled after; a connector file sends the same message (path connector) in place of its generic exception, and the assistant still sees unreadable with its hint (superseded 2026-10-19 by US-35 AC13: the assistant now sees too_long or refused, each with its own hint); a classifier refusal is its own message, Chat classifier: refusal, tagged with its category, where it used to read as unparseable output, and it still fires the router. The BYOK chat's cap rose from 1024 to 2048 tokens for the token growth; a cut-off reply is kept, as on the website chat. A batch result is read as the single call reads it, every text block joined. One copy each, in health-core models.ts: the stop codes (refused, too_long) and their mapping from stop_reason, which the server, the BYOK upload and the upload modal's types share, the refusal categories and their normaliser, the refusal lines (the website chat and the BYOK chat share them), and the classifier's labels, first-word parse and cap of 16, which both harnesses import. Throughput, measured once (synthetic text, thinking off, 2026-10-16): 2,041 output tokens in 9.3 s, 219 tokens a second including time to first token, so a full 12,288-token answer would need about 56 s against the website's 60 s non-streaming timeout. The single file's cap is therefore 10000 (about 46 s), its own constant (SINGLE_FILE_MAX_TOKENS in anthropic.server.ts); the batch and the BYOK upload have no such call and keep 12288 (EXTRACTION_MAX_TOKENS). The single file also gets one 60 s deadline for its calls, so a malformed answer's re-send gets what is left, not a fresh 60 s; a timed-out HTTP attempt is still retried once in a fresh window (fetchAnthropicRaw, kept for capacity blips), so the worst case for a very slow file is about 120 s. On the Pages build a max_tokens stop with no text is too_long, not empty. A Pages chat reply that ends with no text to show (cut off before any text, or holding only tool calls that did not parse) is an error, "Empty response from Anthropic. Try again.", never a blank answer saved to history, as the website chat falls back (byok-chat.test.ts). Streaming that call is the option if long transcriptions need more. Tests: anthropic.server.retry.test.ts (one call on a refusal or a max_tokens stop; at most two on malformed answers; the 10000 cap), anthropic.server.batch.test.ts (refused and too_long codes and their category, handed back, not reported; joined text blocks; the 12288 cap), api.lab-import-v2.test.ts (the 422 answers, the 60 s deadline, a batch's stops reported once), mcp-import.server.test.ts (the connector's stop signal), models.test.ts (the stop codes), upload-api.test.ts, byok-upload.test.ts, UploadModal.outcome.test.tsx (both notices and counts on both builds), chat-classifier.server.test.ts (the refusal signal), byok-chat.test.ts (the 2048 cap).

Every chat_match_events row on every surface (both websites, YouTube, Discord) carries router_output_tokens, the router's output token count from Anthropic's usage. A reply that arrived but failed to parse (cut off at max_tokens, a refusal) keeps its real counts, so the long replies this measures are not lost (adversary R1, 2026-10-18); a row with no reply (timeout, API error) reads 0, as router_input_tokens does, and its router_error says why; the column is null when the router did not run. The web chat_timing line carries routerOutputTokens beside routerCacheReadTokens. Both hold a number only, never text. Why it matters: on 2026-10-14 the router timed out twice in a row, and a slow upstream and a long reply (up to max_tokens 200) looked the same. With the count logged, latency can be judged against reply length: on replies that arrived (a slow success, a retry after a first-try timeout, a reply cut off at max_tokens), since a timed-out try itself has no reply to count. Usage signal: the column itself, read by the sentry-fix loop through the read-only product-health role. Ordering: ALTER TABLE chat_match_events ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS router_output_tokens integer (supabase/rls-policies.sql) must run in production before the code deploys, or every match-event insert fails. US-16 · Chat can fill my form

As a user, when I tell the chat my numbers ("my LDL is 3.2"), it proposes structured form edits that I confirm — it never silently writes data.

  • AC1 (2026-09-25): one reply can carry several field edits: "120/80" is a systolic and a diastolic, and a weight can come with a waist. Each edit the page has a place for lands in the form, and the next save saves them all. Known gap (adversarial review, 2026-09-25): a blood-test edit sent before the blood-test matrix is on the page (a first-time user who has not given a weight yet, form stage 2) is dropped, and the chat still says it pre-filled it; an LDL alone is dropped the same way. It predates this AC; holding the edit until the matrix mounts is the fix owed. A chat value pre-filled into the vitals matrix is typed into its cell in the unit the chat stated, and the focus stays there: it no longer jumps to the email field, which on a phone pulled the page to the plan tab, away from the cell the user was asked to review. Found by the 2026-09-25 cleanup review: for a first-time user each edit rebuilt the form from the same copy, so only the last survived, and the next save wrote half a blood pressure.
  • AC2 (2026-10-20, Brad: "the chatbot should be asking the user to input the missing values, which it can do either in the chat or in the tool itself"): the website chat (the widget's own chat and the Pages chat, never the hosted connector) can save a stated sex and height, with the user's confirmation. A third form tool, propose_profile_edit {sex: male or female, height: {value, unit cm or in}} (health-core chat-edits.ts), goes wherever the other two form tools go (US-15 AC19). The model passes the height as stated (5 ft 10 in as 70 in); the parser converts it to cm and holds it to the plan schema's range (50 to 250 cm), and refuses the whole edit for an out-of-range height, a sex outside the enum, an unknown unit or key, or an empty edit, as a measurement with an unknown unit is refused; the tool result then says "Not applied". The form writes sex and height on change, so the widget never puts the proposal into the form directly: a banner shows it in the user's units ("Save to your profile: Male, 178 cm?", or 5'10" for conventional units) with Save and Not now. When the profile already holds a different sex or height, the banner names the value it replaces, in the same units ("Save to your profile: height 178 cm (replaces 175 cm)?"; orchestrator, 2026-10-20). A field the profile already holds with the same value, as the user's units show it, is left out, and when no field changes there is no banner and no counter. Save sets the fields as typing them would, the profile saves through the same path (LWW profile scalars, US-10 AC6), and the plan computes. Not now writes nothing. A tool-only reply says "Please check the details shown and press Save to add them to your profile." The no-plan rule (US-15 AC36, NO_PLAN_CHAT_RULE and its copy in chat-system-prompt.md) now asks for the missing values and, once they are stated, proposes saving them with the tool when the chat has it; the user can also enter them in the roadmap tool. run_roadmap's description offers the same. Both prompts' tool sections describe the new tool. Usage signal: chat_profile_edit with { field: sex | heightCm, choice: shown | saved | declined } (once per tab per pair), the field's name and never its value; saved over shown is the measure. Tests: chat-edits.test.ts (in range in cm and in, out of range, a bad sex, unknown unit or key, the fixture round-trip, the ack), run-roadmap.test.ts (the stub, the refused stub, the description), chat.server.test.ts and byok-chat.test.ts (the rule), HealthTool.chat-profile.test.tsx (Save writes the profile and the plan computes; Not now writes nothing; feet and inches for conventional; the replaced value named; no banner for a value already saved, and only the changed field otherwise), product-events.server.test.ts (the counter's closed words). Tool-use fixture profile-sex-height ("I'm a 52 year old man, 178 cm") in tools/test-tool-edits.json, not yet run (paid harness; test key capped until 2026-11-01). Review fixes, 2026-10-20 (orchestrator): the tool and its edits go only to a client that sends canApplyProfileEdits: true beside canApplyEdits (the widget's chat from this build; the Pages chat always has it), since an older widget applied any edit that was not a field as a medication and would write a blank medication row; the client also drops an edit kind it does not know. A reply's proposal replaces any pending one (within a reply, a later stated field wins), the banner shows only fields the profile does not already hold, and erasing the data or the user setting sex or height in the form clears it. sex: null or height: null is absent; an unknown key inside height refuses the edit. The banner and the medication Undo banner stack in one fixed column (.chat-banners) that carries the Clarity mask (US-09 AC8). The answer-check fixtures require the proposal itself (expect_profile_edit). Tests: the above, plus chat.server.run-roadmap.test.ts, api.chat-stream.test.ts, chat-api.stream.test.ts, clarity-masking.test.tsx and test-chatbot-matching.test.ts.
  • AC2a (2026-10-21, split from outside PR #207 by Austin Bell; reworked after review): a re-read that brings no erase keeps an unanswered profile proposal and the medication Undo, an empty record's included. Before, the page read an empty record as an erase and dropped them, so an empty guest's proposal vanished at the first re-read. Each banner now stands for the erase the record was at when it was made: meta.eraseEpoch and meta.erasedAt (RoadmapStore.eraseIdentity). An erase moves them, this tab's or another device's once this tab re-reads the record, and the banners go, even when post-erase rows came with it. The store takes in and announces a re-read whose only change is the erase (contentOf and visibleContentOf now include it), since an empty record erased again can differ in nothing else. The page also marks on the store the erase its screen shows (RoadmapStore.showErase), set at load, by each re-read it shows and by its own erase once the store holds the erased copy. While the store holds a different one, the screen's values are pre-erase: this tab's erase is still writing, its write failed (the store keeps the erased copy, the next hide retries the write, and the device mirror carries it to the next session; US-11 AC7), or the relay holds a remote change behind an unsaved profile edit (US-34 AC4). Then a chat reply applies none of its edits, medication, field or profile, since it comes from the conversation the erase tombstones; and Save and Undo write nothing and the banner goes (review R4). Undo's prior values come from the store, the copy the check reads, not the screen; so a form change still on its 300 ms debounce when the chat changes the same medication is not what Undo restores (review R1, 2026-10-21). The store itself refuses every write (adversary R6, 2026-10-21; it replaced the page's per-path guards, which kept missing one): from its own erase's swap to the end of that erase's write, and whenever the write's stamp is not the erase this copy holds. The stamp is the erase the page showed when the write was asked for: a keystroke or chat reply arms the medication, supplement and screening saves and the profile's 500 ms auto-save with it, a matrix save takes it as it is asked for, the first-time vitals fields' save as the field is left, a reminder enrolment as it begins, and an upload's screening dates as the upload's save begins (skipped outright when the erase moved meanwhile); a write that passes none takes the page's mark as it runs. This tab's erase also cancels the vitals fields' pending save. A global mark alone could not tell a save armed before an erase from one asked for after the page showed it (Codex R3, adversary R3). A document upload is stamped as it starts, refused before any upload if already stale, and checked again at its commit, since an erase can land while the blobs upload; the connector's metadata-only row it upgrades is tombstoned only inside that commit, so a refused upgrade leaves it as it was (Codex R1-R2, adversary R4). Every write method answers a refusal with its own error result, never a throw, and changes nothing: a measurement, correction, profile, medication, supplement, screening, lab, upload, document deletion, Lp(a) unit, email-capture flag or reminder setting; the last three now answer true or false too. A reminder token the record refuses is cancelled on Brad's server and the enrolment fails, as a superseded silent enrolment always did (adversary R2), unless the file already holds that token active (Google's lane hands back the existing token): then nothing is cancelled and the switch marker stays (re-check adversary R1). Callers show it as they show a failed save: a matrix keeps its draft and says it was not saved; an upload counts its rows as errors; a medication, supplement, screening or profile save says "That change was not saved: your data was just deleted, here or on another device", once per erase however many saves it refuses (adversary R5), and never for the leftovers of this tab's own erase, and the page re-reads, which also releases a remote change the relay held behind the edit (US-34 AC4), except during this tab's own erase, which throws the change away anyway. So a save the form scheduled before an erase, or the profile's 500 ms auto-save firing during it, never lands in the erased record, and a successful erase clears the form's save timers too. While this tab's erase runs, the whole form, both matrices included, also sits in a disabled fieldset (a number already typed into a field can stay on screen, saved nowhere). A save that folded a remote change in and then failed on a later pass now announces the change, so the page catches up (adversary R3). A chat drug or dose change resets that drug's escalation answer when one is saved or one the form holds is still waiting to save, unless the same reply states one. The change is judged against the form's drug and dose as well as the saved ones, so a chat dose equal to the saved one still resets an answer given after a form dose change not yet saved (Codex full review R2); only a saved answer is Undo's to restore (US-06 AC12, Codex re-check R1). A store replacement inside one page does not happen in production (initRoadmapStore runs once per page load; every connect path reloads), so it needs no rule of its own. A successful erase also clears the lab rows, documents and supplements the page holds, and every re-read now takes the supplements in too; they stayed until a reload (adversary R1). A later erase from elsewhere at the epoch already held now clears the matrices' drafts too, as a higher one did (adversary R6). The PR's first version announced an erase before the stored record was read, so an erase refused because the cloud could not be read (US-09 AC23) blanked the medications and screenings on screen until reload. Now that refusal changes nothing, on screen or in the on-device copy; the screen changes only once an erase lands. An erase whose write fails is not that refusal: the store keeps the erased copy and retries it, so the screen shows that copy too and the alert says the write failed (review R5). Whenever this erase moved the store's erase, written or not, both matrices' drafts and the Lp(a) check's kept answers go too, from the device and from the screen, so a draft the chat filled into a matrix the user never opened cannot come back after a reload and be saved into the erased copy (Codex full review R1). The page tells the two apart by whether this erase moved the store's erase, not by whether the screen is behind one: a refused erase while a remote erase is held back leaves the form, an unsaved edit and the banners as they were (Codex final check R2). Tests: HealthTool.chat-profile.test.tsx (an empty guest's proposal through an unchanged re-read, then Save; Undo through one; a proposal made after this tab's own erase kept; another device's erase written to a shared MemoryCloud and re-read by this tab's own store, for an empty record, again at the same epoch, and with a post-erase weight, at a higher and at the same epoch; Save refuses when the page was not told; an erase refused because the cloud read failed leaves the chat context and mirror unchanged; a successful erase empties the upload view's history; a chat reply during this tab's erase write applies nothing, makes no banner and writes no pre-erase medication back; a height typed during the erase write is not saved; after a failed erase write the screen shows the erased copy and the next reply shows its banners; a medication save scheduled just before the erase does not land in the erased record; a chat statin change resets an escalation answer still waiting to save; an erase refused while a remote erase is held back changes nothing on screen; a chat dose equal to the saved one resets an answer given after an unsaved form dose change; after a failed erase write a chat-filled matrix draft is gone from the device and the chat context; a height typed just before Delete and saved by the profile timer during the erase write does not land; a profile save refused behind a held remote erase says so and shows the erased record; a chat medication change armed before another device's erase is shown does not land after it, with one alert for two refused saves; this tab's erase and another device's both clear the supplements on screen; a supplement edit refused behind a held remote erase says so and saves nothing; and in HealthTool.journey.test.tsx, a vitals cell committed during the erase write reaches nothing), roadmap-store-erase-guard.test.ts (each of the 14 write methods refused, with its answer and an unchanged record, both while the page shows another erase and while this copy's erase writes; with no page mark and after the erase lands, writes land; a save whose later pass fails still announces a folded remote change; a write asked for before an erase is refused after the page shows it; a blob upload landing after the erase appends nothing; a refused archive upgrade leaves the metadata-only row; a same-epoch erase clears the drafts), reminders.test.ts (a refused token is cancelled and the enrolment fails; a reply landing after an erase the page has shown is refused by its stamp and cancelled; a refused reply carrying the token the file holds active cancels nothing), UploadModal.outcome.test.tsx (a screening date is written with the save's stamp, and not at all when the erase landed while the document saved).
  • Tests: ✅ chat-edits parsing + the paid tool-edit harness (tools/test-tool-edits.json). ✅ 2026-09-25: HealthTool.journey.test.tsx (one reply carrying a blood pressure, or a weight and a waist, leaves both in the first-time fields, and a save saves both).

US-49 · A signed-in customer can pause, skip or cancel a subscription in the microvitamin.com chat — built 2026-10-16 (Brad: "it would be relatively simple just to add on the API stuff with Appstle so that people can actually edit their subscription via the chat", "the code should be shared"); off until Brad switches it on; not deployed

As a customer signed in to microvitamin.com, I can ask the chat to pause one of my subscriptions, skip its next order, or cancel it, see exactly what will change, and confirm it with one press, so I do not have to email or find the account page. Deliveries stay every 3 or every 6 months, and nothing moves an order earlier.

  • AC1 (commerce only, off by default): only health-tool-app with CHAT_SURFACE=brand, CHAT_SUBSCRIPTION_ACTIONS=on, CS_GATEWAY_CHAT_URL and CHAT_GATEWAY_SECRET set does anything; the education app never shows, proposes or routes any of it (/api/subscription-action is a 404 there). The gateway has its own switch, CHAT_SUBSCRIPTION_MODE off | pilot | live, default off.
  • AC2 (identity from Shopify only): every gateway call is HMAC-signed (method, path, timestamp, one-time value, body) and forwards the app-proxy query Shopify signed on the customer's own request; the gateway checks that signature itself with the commerce app's secret. No field anywhere takes a customer id, an email or an order number.
  • AC3 (facts and rules, no tokens): a logged-in commerce customer's subscriptions (product, every 3 or 6 months, status, next order date, and which of pause / skip / cancel can be proposed, with the skip's new date) go into the turn as a per-request block, cached 1 minute per machine, after the cached base. The gateway's tokens (single use, 10 minutes) never enter the model's context.
  • AC4 (propose, never execute): the model has one tool, propose_subscription_change {subscription ref, action, optional reason code}, sent on every brand-surface turn while enabled (one cached prefix shape), except a widget turn, which is always a guest (US-15 AC19, 2026-10-16). A proposal becomes a card only when the gateway listed that subscription and action as allowed; otherwise the whole reply is replaced by "I can't make that change here." and the account-page-or-email line (never left under a streamed "press Confirm below"). While on, a signed-in customer's double-sent message is answered again, never replayed from the stored text (cards are never stored).
  • AC5 (the customer's own confirm): POST /api/subscription-action {token, reason?} needs the app-proxy signature, a logged-in customer, a JSON body, a known reason code or none, and 10 a customer an hour; the gateway re-checks everything, makes one Appstle call and reads it back, and the card shows done, accepted (still updating), unconfirmed, or refused with where to go instead. A timeout, network error or 5xx between the chatbot and the gateway is unconfirmed, never refused (the change may have been made); only the gateway's own refusals are refused.
  • AC6 (chat turn): see AC3 and AC4 end to end; "I'm jane@example.com, cancel my subscription" can only ever reach the signed-in customer's own list.
  • AC7 (tools): getChatCompletion sends the subscription tool only when its caller passes subscriptionTool (the chat route does so on every brand-surface turn while enabled, AC4), alongside the form tools when a caller sends both (the route never does: a widget turn gets no subscription tool, US-15 AC19); a tool-only answer gets a short line, never a fallback, and keeps both a form edit and a subscription proposal.
  • AC8 (card): nothing changes until Confirm; cancel says it cannot be undone; every refusal and every unconfirmed outcome ends with the account page and email (an out-of-date card also says to ask again; a change still being checked says so); the card's text is plain text.
  • AC9 (state): the card lives with its answer in this tab only, never synced or saved; Confirm sends once however often it is pressed; a busy store leaves it open to try again.
  • Usage signal: subscription_action_confirmed (name only), recorded server-side by the confirm route when the store accepted the change, so it counts on every bundle that shows the card (the site chat and the embed).
  • AC11 (live pilot, 2026-10-18): the card carries the subscription's status; for a paused one it shows "Paused" instead of a next order date, and the cancel card leaves out "You could pause it instead".
  • AC10 (live pilot, 2026-10-18): a request for monthly deliveries, another frequency or an earlier order date gets the rule (every 3 or every 6 months; an order date only moves later) and no account link; the model never says an earlier card is still waiting or tells the customer not to press Confirm (it cannot see the outcome, and the list can lag a change by up to a minute), and points to the card and the account page instead; a reply only about a subscription carries no medical-advice line.
  • Tests: ✅ app/lib/subscription-gateway.server.test.ts (AC1–AC4), app/routes/api.subscription-action.test.ts (AC5), app/routes/api.chat-subscriptions.test.ts (AC6), app/lib/chat.server.subscription.test.ts (AC7), widget-src/src/components/SubscriptionChangeCard.test.tsx (AC8), widget-src/src/hooks/useChatState.subscription.test.tsx (AC9). The gateway side (private repo): customer-service-gateway/test/chat.test.js. Not yet: WebKit check of the card, and the live pilot test.

US-50 · Topic masters: one current page per supplement, and the chatbot loads it instead of old posts (added 2026-10-20, plan: docs/chat-topic-masters-plan-2026-10-20.md, Brad decisions D1–D20)

As Brad, I want each supplement's reference page to carry my current view, and the chatbot to load that page rather than my older videos' posts, so answers reflect what I think now and a change of view lands in one place. Extends US-15 (chat) and US-42 (refresh rules for references).

  • AC1 (master shape): a rewritten master has one-line frontmatter keys reviewed: "YYYY-MM-DD" and sources: (single-line JSON: name, url, checked, fingerprint); a ## Current view (reviewed …) section whose every sentence cites Brad's posts (a link to the post) or his position files (products.md, the clinical files, the system prompt, the guidelines) as "(Brad's current guidance, D Mon YYYY)", each backed by a verbatim quote in the report; a ## Current evidence position section, which never claims to be his view, is used when neither holds a position; a ## Brad's videos on this topic list (date, title, one-line take, "superseded on X" where it applies); a review that agrees; and a rewritten index summary (check: US-42 checker extended for master keys; owner: orchestrator). Under --masters, --check-ids resolves every DOI and PMID in each batch file's references, retained ones included, one request a second, unless --check-ids-cap <n> limits it (the default without --masters stays 60).
  • AC2 (post links): video posts may carry topics: [...] (master handles) and, only when the whole post is about one master's substance, router: hidden. Drug, lifestyle and test posts are never linked to a supplement master. Post bodies are never edited. rebuild-blog-index.ts, BlogIndexEntry and the claude_business /blog-post index writer carry topics, router and reviewed (check: unit test; owner: orchestrator).
  • AC3 (router view): the router's index block, handle allow-list and stated entry count omit a router: hidden post only when its master's reviewed is on or after the post's publishedAt; every other post, every master and every pathway stays. TOPIC_MASTER_HIDE=off restores the full view. ROUTER_VERSION is bumped. The matching harness uses the same view. loadBlogIndex() is unchanged, so YouTube still finds every post by video ID (check: unit tests including a mixed-topic post and a newer-video-than-master post; owner: orchestrator).
  • AC4 (no frontmatter to the model): loadMatchedContent() strips frontmatter before content reaches the answer model and before it counts against MAX_BLOG_CHARS (check: unit test).
  • AC5 (precedence): loaded blocks carry a header naming type and date ("[reference — reviewed …]", "[video post — published …]"), plus the title and links. The answer prompt says the system prompt, products.md and the answer bank outrank every loaded block; a master's current view outranks a post published before its reviewed date; a post published after that date wins over the current view, since it may record a change the master has not caught up with; a reply says plainly when the position changed, as Brad's view on the doctor surfaces and in the assistant's own voice on the brand surface. Within a reference, only Current-view sentences that cite a Brad post are his view; posts and the answer bank keep the "Brad's stated views" rule (check: prompt test + answer fixtures; owner: orchestrator).
  • AC6 (YouTube): a comment loads its video's post as today, with its publish date, plus the Current view or Current evidence position section of each master the post names, followed by that master's body sections whose heading names safety, side effects, cautions, interactions, contraindications or who should not take it (Brad, 2026-10-20), de-duplicated against the router-matched entries that actually loaded (a master the cap skipped still adds its sections). Each safety section brings the bibliography lines its [n] markers cite. Every master's view goes in first; a view runs to the next ## heading or --- line, and one over 6,000 characters is dropped and logged. A master with key safety points adds those instead of its safety sections (AC12). For the others, safety sections fill the rest of an 80,000-character total (views and key points count against it) in topics order: first every master's Drug Interactions, then the Safety and Side Effects sections, never for a master whose interactions were skipped; each skip is logged with the master's handle (review rounds 1 and 2, 2026-10-20). Sections go in whole, never trimmed mid-section. The block's heading names both ("current view and safety notes"), and the prompt calls the safety sections evidence summaries, never Brad's view. A video published after a master's reviewed date wins on Brad's view today. The dry-run tool builds the same context. These sections never count as router-matched content for the reply-or-skip rule. A reply may say publicly that Brad's view has since changed (Brad, 2026-10-20) (check: unit test + a skip fixture).
  • AC7 (lint): in test:all, static only: a post naming a missing master; a rewritten master without sources; a hidden post whose master fails the gate (warn); a current-view DOI missing from products.md for a product ingredient (warn). In the weekly US-43 lint: a master reviewed before its newest linked post; a source checked more than 35 days ago; a master whose current-view hash changed while a place registered for its topic in lint-topics.json (anchored by text, never line number) did not, unless waived in lint-allowlist.json with author and date; overlapping masters that disagree. Master hashes are written by each batch's publish commit. An answer-bank entry older than a master's reviewed date on the same topic is flagged (weekly). (check: lint tests).
  • AC8 (review and publish): masters are written by Opus under US-42's rules, checked by the US-42 checker, and reviewed by a fresh adversary and Codex (adversary alone when Codex is out of quota, Brad 2026-10-20). A clean master publishes. Brad sees only the always-ask list: a recommendation that changes direction, a dose change, a safety warning added or removed, ConsumerLab or NIH disagreeing with Brad's latest video, any claim about a Brad product, and any change that touches products.md, the system prompt or the three clinical files (owner: orchestrator; Brad for the list).
  • AC9 (web pages): after Brad's deploy is verified, the drstanfield.com article is updated, its ID resolved by handle through the API, the store chosen explicitly (--edu), the old body saved for rollback; then the microvitamin.com copy is rebuilt and published (Brad, 2026-10-20: commerce copies follow the master) (check: before/after updated_at snapshot).
  • AC10 (triggers): /blog-post proposes topics and router for a new post and compares its position with each named master: same view on a rewritten master moves reviewed forward; a master not yet rewritten is queued, never given a reviewed date; a changed view queues a master update. A monthly local session re-fetches NIH ODS and ConsumerLab (only the sections supplement-wiki allows), compares normalised fingerprints, and queues a draft on change. No literature search (Brad, D4).
  • AC11 (omega-3 brand, Brad 2026-10-20: products.md wins): on the doctor surfaces, when a user asks which omega-3 Brad takes or which one to buy, the bot gives the EPA/DHA criteria and says he takes and recommends WHC UnoCardio 1000 Fish Oil, with the products.md Amazon link, and says "Brad earns a small commission through this Amazon link." (Brad 2026-10-20: disclose commission; on YouTube that sentence is exempt from the do-not-copy rule and the length limits, and the products.md "what does Brad take" list follows the same scope); Dr Stanfield still sells no omega-3. The doctor posture and the competitor-brands rule name this exception. The brand surface gives the criteria only, since its posture never presents Brad's routine as an endorsement (check: prompt tests on the files and the assembled doctor and brand prompts in app/lib/topic-masters-prompts.test.ts).
  • AC12 (key safety points, orchestrator 2026-10-21): a master with a view carries ## Key safety points directly after it: 3 to 8 bullets ranked by clinical weight (serious drug interactions such as warfarin first, then who should not take it, then dose ceilings and toxicity, then common side effects), each one or two plain sentences with the [n] markers of the master's own References, no claim its safety, interaction or view sections do not already make, hedging kept, at most 1,500 characters (heading and body). On YouTube, the view and these points always go in, uncapped, and the master's whole safety sections do not. The points go without their reference lines and with the [n] markers stripped, since a marker with no line is noise in a comment reply (estimated 2026-10-21: about 3,000 characters per master, about 42,000 for 14); masters with key points never use the 80,000-character cap, which masters without them still compete under; points over 1,500 characters or with fewer than 3 bullet lines ("- ", "* " or "1. ") are dropped and logged, and that master falls back to its safety sections under AC6. The weekly lint warns (master-key-points) on a master without sound points until the retrofit lands; the batch checker's --key-safety-points, passed with --masters on new batches, fails it (check: unit tests app/lib/youtube-bot.masters.test.ts, tools/knowledge-lint-masters.test.ts, tools/knowledge-batch-check.test.ts).
  • AC13 (a master over the content cap, 2026-10-21): when routed topic masters would push the loaded content past MAX_BLOG_CHARS (120,000, separators counted), no master is dropped while a smaller form fits. A master has three forms: whole; reduced with its Recommended Dosing section (where the upper limits live); reduced without it. A reduced form is the master's header, an internal note ("do not quote… for anything not below, say the full page covers it and give its link"), then its Current view (or Current evidence position; a view of 6,000 characters or more is dropped as malformed, as on YouTube), its Key safety points (dropped when malformed by AC12's checks: over 1,500 characters or under 3 bullets) and every safety section (reducedMaster() in youtube-context.ts, AC6's section rules), followed by the reference line of every [n] those sections cite; when a reduced form loads, a dropped view or key points is logged once with the handle, as on YouTube (a master that loads whole logs nothing). Every entry leaves room for the smallest form of each master routed after it. A master takes its largest form that leaves that room, else the shortest form that fits, so a large first master yields. A non-master loads whole only if it leaves that room, so a large post routed before or between masters yields too. A master also leaves room for each later post, whole, when that post still fits with every routed master at its smallest form: a post has no smaller form, so masters shrink first, and [vitamin K, vitamin A, lithium] loads all three with vitamin K reduced. Otherwise the post yields as above. A handle the router returns twice loads once. A master whose smallest form cannot fit is skipped and listed, as is a non-master that does not fit (US-15 AC23). Every ordered pair of the current masters loads both, inside the cap: [vitamin D, vitamin K] loads vitamin D whole and vitamin K reduced with its warfarin section; [B vitamins, multivitamins] loads B vitamins reduced. Every ordered pair with one of the three largest non-masters before or between them also loads both masters, inside the cap: [lithium, probiotics, vitamin K] skips probiotics and keeps vitamin K's warfarin section (before 2026-10-21 the re-check measured 197 of 1,140 such pairs dropping a master with the post between, 42 with it first). Three or more routed masters whose smallest forms together pass the cap can still lose one. The connector's search_knowledge gives a master's whole Current view, up to 4,000 characters (US-41 AC7), since the writer contract puts who should not take it last (check: unit tests app/lib/matched-content.test.ts "vitamin D + vitamin K: both load, with vitamin K's warfarin lines", "every citation in a reduced master keeps its reference line…", "a large first master yields…", "every ordered pair of masters loads both…", "a reduced master keeps its Recommended Dosing when it fits…", "the separators count against the cap…", "a non-master entry that would overflow is still skipped whole", "a master whose reduced form still does not fit is skipped", "[lithium, probiotics, vitamin K]: vitamin K loads with its warfarin lines", "[probiotics, vitamin C, B vitamins]: a non-master first leaves both masters their room", "a non-master that fits alongside the later masters' reserve still loads", "every ordered pair of masters with a large non-master first or between…" (a post between two masters loads whenever it fits with both at their smallest), "[vitamin K, vitamin A post, lithium]…", "a handle routed twice loads once", "a reduced master logs what it dropped once…"; app/routes/mcp.knowledge.test.ts "a master excerpt is its whole Current view…", "every served master's Current view fits MAX_MASTER_EXCERPT_CHARS"; app/lib/youtube-bot.masters.test.ts "reducedMaster keeps the malformed-view check", its three key safety points cases (reducedDrops), and "a master the router picked but the cap skipped, even reduced, still adds its current view").
  • AC14 (masters before older posts, Brad 2026-10-22): when a question is about a topic with a master, the master loads, not the older posts; an older post loads only when the user asks about that post. After routing, in code (the cached router prompt is unchanged), each [article] the router picks whose topics name at least one master (AC1: a reference with reviewed) is replaced by its masters in its slot, but only when every one of its topics is a master reviewed on or after its publish day, AC3's exact rule (covered(), shared with the router view): a post with any topic not yet a master stays whole (multivitamins-are-no-longer-expensive-urine: 5 topics, 3 masters), as does one newer than any of its masters, or undated (AC5). A post's masters rank by where the current message names their topic, earliest first, then by the post's topics order. A master's names are each part of its title before the colon, split on "(", ")", ",", "/" and " and "; each part also without trailing generic words (supplements, boosters, powders, powder, fish oil, oil, peptides, extract; a dropped "fish oil" still names its master); and its first word when that has a digit or hyphen or is in capitals of 2 or more letters (omega-3, NAD, NMN); a final "s" is optional. So "is the vitamin A in a multivitamin safe in pregnancy?" puts vitamin A's master first, "Is omega-3 better than B vitamins for the brain?" and "fish oil or B vitamins" put Omega-3 Fish Oil first, and "NMN" names the NAD Boosters master. The article also stays when it is named: the storefront chat is open on it (optional body field articleHandle, which site-chat.tsx sends from a /blogs/<blog>/<handle> path; the server treats it as untrusted, uses it only as a lookup against article handles and microvitamin.com slugs, ignores anything else and never stores it), or the message gives its handle or slug in a /blogs/<blog>/<slug> path or URL, or as a bare hyphenated word of at least 4 words ("calcium-rich-foods" and "resting-heart-rate" name nothing), or it is the YouTube video's own post. Naming reads the whole message as accepted (up to its 8,000-character cap), not the router's 2,000-character cut, as a lookup only, never logged; it is linear in the message (an 8,000- or 10,000-character run takes under 50 ms). The filter runs only on a turn the router ran: when the classifier skips the router, nothing loads and nothing is forced in. At most 3 handles, filled in passes: (1) every pick the router made that stays, masters included, in its own slot, never dropped; (2) for each replaced pick, in slot order, its first-ranked master not already in, in that slot (each pick owns a slot, so one always fits, and replaced lists only picks whose master loaded); (3) the open post, when the router picked nothing or one of its masters is in after passes 1–2 (picked or brought in by a replacement), then each post the message names that the router did not pick, router-hidden ones included, in the order the message names them (the YouTube video's own post is never forced in: it is already in the bot's context); otherwise the open post is not forced in, since the reader may ask about something else; (4) the ranked masters of every named, open or YouTube-own post that stays, covered or not, picked ones in slot order, then pass-3 ones (so a picked post whose URL the message gives loads as [post, first master, next master]); (5) the remaining masters of replaced picks, in slot order. The list is in slot order; a post added in pass 3 sits right after the first of its own masters (in its ranked order) in the final list, else at the end; duplicates drop. Pathways, guidelines, references and posts with no master topics are untouched. The filter runs on the web chat (storefront bubble, widget, app), YouTube and Discord; MCP search_knowledge is untouched (its own ranker, AC7 of US-41). The router harness's answer check and the YouTube dry run apply the same filter. Usage signal: chat_match_events.router_context.replaced (picks that gave way) and .reduced (masters loaded in AC13's reduced form), index handles only, absent when empty; matched_handles stays the router's own picks (check: unit tests app/lib/router-view.test.ts "preferMasters (US-50 AC14)" and "namedArticles (US-50 AC14)", app/routes/api.chat-masters.test.ts, app/lib/youtube-bot.masters.test.ts "…(US-50 AC14)" (YouTube and Discord), app/lib/discord-bot.server.test.ts "US-50 AC14: the row records…", app/lib/matched-content.test.ts "names each master that loaded reduced…", widget-src/src/lib/assistant-config.test.ts "resolveChatArticle (US-50 AC14)", widget-src/src/lib/chat-api.test.ts "the open blog post (US-50 AC14)").
  • Usage signal: loaded characters per routed turn, and the share of supplement turns whose first loaded entry is a master (chat_match_events).
  • Tests: 🟡 AC2–AC6 built on branch claude/topic-masters-chat, except AC2's claude_business /blog-post index writer, which is NOT yet done (a separate claude_business change) (unit tests: scripts/rebuild-blog-index.test.ts, app/lib/router-view.test.ts, app/lib/chat-router.view.test.ts, app/lib/matched-content.test.ts, app/lib/youtube-bot.masters.test.ts, app/lib/topic-masters-prompts.test.ts, harness tests in tools/test-chatbot-matching.test.ts). Answer fixtures (tools/test-queries.json, category topic-masters) and the YouTube skip dry run are pre-registered, not yet run. AC1, AC7–AC10 ⬜ not built. AC12 🟡 built on claude/key-safety-points (2026-10-21); the masters' retrofit is not done. AC14 🟡 built on claude/us50-ac14-master-routing (2026-10-22), unit tests green, not deployed.

US-43 · The chatbot's knowledge base stays consistent (weekly lint) — added 2026-09-29 (Brad, knowledge-refresh plan decision 6); deterministic half built and run, model half built and not yet run

As a user asking the chatbot, the pathway, the supplement reference and the plan my answer draws on agree with each other, or they differ where Brad chose to; as Brad, a weekly check finds the contradictions and the knowledge base gets fixed, while my algorithm is only reported.

  • AC1 (deterministic rules; no model, and no network unless asked): tools/knowledge-lint.ts checks every entry in docs/blog, docs/pathway and docs/guideline for citation markers with no reference line and reference lines nothing cites; DOI and PMID shape, and links whose text and target differ; bodies that cite Grokipedia, with the sentences resting only on it; a number plus unit in the index.json summary the body never states (the refresh plan's AC2 tokeniser); and product mentions above the stored baseline. --check-links sends HEAD requests for the due entries' DOIs and PMIDs, 1 s apart, capped at 500.
  • AC2 (the report fits the loop): counts come first and the markdown report never passes 150 lines, however many findings; --json holds every finding.
  • AC3 (the selector): docs/loops/chat-health/lint-state.json holds the last run date, the slice cursor, a hash per algorithm topic and, per entry, a content hash and product baseline. The due list is every entry new or changed since the last saved run, every entry paired with an algorithm topic whose text changed, and one of 13 stable hash slices, so a full pass takes 13 weeks. --dry-run prints it and writes nothing. Only knowledge-lint-compare.ts --run advances it: every comparison attempt is recorded, a missing, refused, truncated or unparseable answer marks it retry and leaves cursor and hashes alone, three in a row park it (listed, no longer blocking), a comparison's id carries both excerpt hashes so a body rewritten mid-cycle is compared again, and a capped run works through what is owed, oldest attempt first, over the following weeks. Dead links are checked once per identifier and reported against every entry that cites one. Algorithm-side findings print with both quotes, each cut to 200 characters, never dropped.
  • AC4 (divergences are deliberate and written down): every rule, deterministic or model, consults lint-allowlist.json; a handle entry with no rule covers every rule and model comparison on that handle, and the compare step counts the model findings it drops; an entry missing its rule, its handle or pair, its reason, date or who stops the run. The loop proposes entries and never edits the file.
  • AC5 (the model half has a known cost): tools/knowledge-lint-compare.ts builds the entry-versus-algorithm, pathway-versus-reference and reference-versus-reference prompts for the due entries and prints the token estimate and cost at the pinned Sonnet 5.5 price (PRICES in models.ts) before anything runs. It calls the API only under --run, refuses --run without a --max-calls cap, refuses a --max-usd that is not a positive number, and before each call stops if the spend so far plus that call's worst case (estimated input plus the output cap) would pass it. A response that fails to parse, or carries any finding with a missing or malformed quote, side, handle or severity or an unverifiable quote, is rejected whole: that pair's retry, keeping none of its findings and clearing nothing; every other pair's result is kept. An instruction-shaped quote leaves a WARN line naming the handle and the span (cut to 120 characters), never a queue item. A model item resolves only when its pair was compared again with both quotes inside the excerpts sent; otherwise it keeps its status and records unverified. A dead-link item resolves only on a run that got a 2xx/3xx for that identifier on behalf of that entry in this week's slice (a timeout, network error or 5xx is inconclusive), and every item a run covers records last_checked. A reference excerpt takes its dosing, intake, upper-level, safety and interaction sections first, and every side records characters sent against characters available, printed as a CUT line when it did not fit. The first --run waits for Brad's written yes on the cost line.
  • AC6 (external text is data): excerpts and their labels sit inside the data frame; a closing tag inside one is escaped; the model has no tools. Injected text cannot reach the model as instructions; a planted finding is caught by the batch protocol (Opus writer, AC2 raw quotes, Brad's sign-off), not by this tool. The tool keeps a finding only if both quotes are verbatim in their excerpts and its fix names one of the two handles, drops one whose quote reads like an instruction, and flags instruction-shaped text rather than following it.
  • AC7 (who fixes what): every knowledge-side finding joins lint-fix-queue.json once: model findings from --run, deterministic ones under --queue with their rule name, deduped across weeks by rule, handle and item (a repeat refreshes last_seen). Algorithm-side findings go to the report only, and a pathway against the algorithm is always algorithm-side; any other fix aimed at a pathway body is report-only, never queued. A fixed or resolved item that recurs becomes regressed; an open or regressed one that a run covered and did not see becomes resolved with the date; the Grokipedia item's detail carries the counts; both tools print open, regressed and resolved counts. The loop reports and queues; a build session (Fable orchestrating, Opus writers) fixes queue items under US-42's batch protocol (AC1 to AC8), and Brad signs each batch. No lint step edits health_roadmap_algorithm.md, evidence.ts, roadmap_text.html, index.json or the allow-list.
  • Usage signal (declared): metrics.csv lint_* rows and the queue's open count, falling quarter over quarter.
  • Baseline (2026-09-29, corrected run after the adversarial review; allow-list of 2 entries): 1,024 entries; 87 unresolved markers in 5 entries (73 in diet, whose markers point to the AHA paper's list), 207 uncited reference lines in 39, 39 bibliography-only lists, 1 DOI shape, 1 PMID shape, 3 links whose text differs from the target, 67 bodies citing Grokipedia (506 reference entries), 12 summary dose mismatches in 10 entries (now counting %, mmHg and pmol/L). Estimated model cost: about $0.27 this week; about $3.83 for the 13 weekly slices ($9.37 at most); $2.80 for one --all pass.
  • Tests: ✅ tools/knowledge-lint.test.ts (AC1 to AC4 and the deterministic half of AC7 on fixtures, plus the corpus shapes the first run surfaced). ✅ tools/knowledge-lint-compare.test.ts (AC3, AC5 to AC7; every fetch is a stub, no test calls the API). ⏳ The first --run waits for the test key's cap to lift (2026-10-01) and Brad's yes on the cost line.

US-45 · The chatbot answers Potassium Fiber questions from the signed label — added 2026-10-07 (Brad approved: "build those, then deploy")

As someone who asks either chatbot about the Potassium Fiber drink, I get the label's real numbers and its warning, no health promise, and, on Dr Brad's education surfaces, no sales pitch and a plain statement that he profits from it. Source: docs/products.md § "Potassium Fiber Drink" (the Makers Nutrition panel Brad signed on 2026-10-06, and its editor notes).

  • AC1 (facts): the bot quotes the panel as written: 8 g of fiber (29% Daily Value) from 10 g of acacia gum, a scoop of about 15 g, 500 mg of potassium as potassium citrate (11%), 45 calories. It never gives the pre-panel figures: 10 g of fiber, 36%, a 12.9 g scoop, 20 calories.
  • AC2 (the warning decides): when the user has kidney disease, has been told to limit potassium, or takes an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin receptor blocker, a potassium-sparing diuretic or another potassium supplement, the bot gives the label's 500 mg and sends them to their doctor. It never clears the drink for them or suggests it, including on the brand surface when they ask which product to buy.
  • AC3 (no health claims): nothing ties the drink or its doses to blood pressure, the heart, cholesterol, the gut, bowel regularity, a prebiotic effect or blood sugar. Nutrient-content statements only ("high in fiber", "a good source of potassium"). Saying the drink makes no such claim is fine. Asked whether the drink helps any of these or any condition, the bot says it makes no health claims and is sold for its nutrient content, gives the per-scoop amounts, and does not summarise potassium or fiber outcome research; no answer about the drink cites an outcome study (orchestrator ruling, 2026-10-07, after a sampled brand answer summarised potassium blood-pressure trials). General potassium or fiber questions that don't mention the drink are unaffected.
  • AC4 (surfaces): the doctor surfaces (drstanfield.com, YouTube, Discord) never volunteer, recommend or link the drink, never name a store and give no price unless asked the cost. They name it only when the user does, answer the factual question, and say that Brad owns the company that sells it and profits from its sale. The brand surface (microvitamin.com) may describe it and link https://microvitamin.com/products/potassium-fiber-drink, with no outcome claims; the brand posture's structure/function wording and its "MicroVitamin is a daily multivitamin" line do not apply to the drink.
  • AC5 (never organic): the bot never calls the product organic. Only one ingredient's name, Inavea™ Essential Organic Talh, holds the word.
  • AC6 (the harness tests a surface and a claim): a tools/test-queries.json entry may carry surface: "doctor" | "brand". The answer check then adds that surface's posture file (app/lib/chat-posture-<surface>.md) after the products block and before any articles, the order production's buildSystemBlocks uses. An unknown surface stops the harness before any API call. Entries without it are scored as before. An entry may also carry must_not_claim (added after the Codex review of b322d5d7 and two adversarial reviews): a phrase stated as fact fails. A negation (no, not, never, cannot, without, nor, nothing, none, neither, n't) excuses it only within the 12 words before it and inside its clause; a semicolon, dash, "but" or "and" ends the clause. So "it makes no claim that it can lower blood pressure" passes, while "it has no added sugar and can lower blood pressure" and "it isn't a medicine, but it keeps you regular" fail. Affirming idioms that hold a negation word ("no doubt", "not only", "no wonder", "no question", "without doubt", "none other than") never excuse a claim (Codex, range review of 2026-10-07). Markdown emphasis is stripped and curly apostrophes straightened. It is a heuristic, so the phrases stay claim-shaped. Referral checks ask for "your doctor" (so "Brad is a doctor" does not count) and disclosure checks ask for both "owns" and "profit", with "n't profit" and "not profit" forbidden.
  • AC7 (medicine spacing): asked about taking the drink with other medicines, the bot gives the live store's direction: "Take other medicines at least two hours before or after a scoop." (potassiumfiber.com product page and FAQ; products.md since 0cc47a16). This is product-label guidance in the chatbot's product knowledge only, not a roadmap suggestion, so the three-file clinical sync (algorithm, evidence.ts, roadmap_text.html) does not apply.
  • Usage signal (declared): no new event. Questions naming the drink show in the stored transcripts of the blog chat bubble, chatbot embed, Discord and YouTube (30-day window, US-15 AC8). The main widget stores no text (US-15 AC7), so its answers cannot be audited after the fact.
  • Known limitations (orchestrator ruling, 2026-10-07: leave the router and posture files as they are):

- Routing is not asserted. Router rule 7 names only MicroVitamin and Sleep as Brad's products, and on 2026-10-07 it sent most Potassium Fiber questions to the potassium, psyllium, kidney, hypertension and ACE-inhibitor entries. Each fixture pins the 3-run router intersection for its text (the router sees no surface), minus what production skips at the 120K article cap (US-15 AC23). A later change in what the router returns is not caught here.

- The posture files name only MicroVitamin, MicroVitamin+ and Sleep. The drink's surface rules live in the products.md editor notes.

- The doctor fixtures model the drstanfield.com web chat only. YouTube and Discord also use the doctor posture but add their platform prompt (YouTube caps a reply at 90 words), which the harness does not load; nor does it load the evidence document, the knowledge overview or user data, as before this story.

- The limit-potassium fixture's "your doctor" can be met by echoing the user's own words.

- Nothing reruns this category automatically when products.md or a posture file changes; run it by hand before such a deploy.

  • Tests: ✅ 24 fixed-handle answer checks, category product-potassium-fiber in tools/test-queries.json (12 doctor, 12 brand; AC1 to AC5 and AC7). The five AC3 fixtures require "health claim", "nutrient content", "8 g" and "500 mg", and the brand ones forbid "daily multivitamin". The two AC7 fixtures (added 2026-10-07 without router pins, because the test workspace was out) require "at least two hours" and "before or after" and forbid "no more than two hours"; the AC3 fixtures also forbid a stated "makes health claims".
