Run: npx tsx tools/test-chatbot-matching.ts --category product-potassium-fiber --fixed-handles-only --answer-check-runs 3. 2026-10-07: 22/22 at 3 runs each (majority) on products.md at 8ad6a7bc, before the research rule and the medicine-spacing direction; the paid suite has not run since (the test workspace is out until 2026-11-01), so the research rule was checked live instead (see the chatbot changelog); 3/22 at 1 run on products.md before a97d629e (the three that pass are the guards that need the drink absent from the answer: two doctor-surface "never volunteer" questions and the brand kidney-disease "which product" question). ✅ tools/test-chatbot-matching.test.ts (AC6, offline: each answer call carries its own surface's posture, after products and before articles; a referral-free answer, a stated claim and a claim after an unrelated negation or an affirming idiom fail, and so does an outcome-research summary (the five AC3 fixtures forbid "lowered systolic", "systolic pressure by", "mmHg", "meta-analysis", "randomized trials", "randomised trials" and "Cochrane"), while denials pass; a liveness check confirms every other fixture fails on a stub answer).

Epic F — Staying engaged

US-17 · Email reminders — the retention engine (cloud lane BUILT 2026-08-13; typed lane = US-23)

As a user who has connected a cloud and entered real screening/blood data, I am reminded by email when something comes due without having had to hunt for a setting — because a reminder I never receive is the whole reason the tool failed to change my behaviour.

Reframed 2026-08-14 (constitution): reminders are not a settings feature — they are the product's retention engine, and email is the primary surface for the primary avatar. This story covers the provider-verified (cloud-connect) lane, which the funnel shows is the rare path; the typed-email lane — ~10× larger and therefore the trunk — is promoted to its own story, US-23. Shared mechanics that apply to BOTH lanes (full-schedule-in-every-email, the annual floor, calendar links) are specified in US-23 AC3/AC6 and US-24 to avoid duplication.

Status: the opt-in design was a proven failure; the opt-out replacement is built (2026-08-13). The old behaviour was explicit opt-in behind three barriers (cloud-connect → scroll past the disclaimer to the bottom of the results panel → two clicks). Result: ~1 genuine opt-in in two months (the second reminder_optin_v2 row is Brad's own e2e test). Nothing was broken — cron healthy, sends correct, nothing yet due (earliest 2027-05-12) — the feature simply never reached anyone.

What now ships (autoEnrolReminders, standalone/reminders.ts): every app load on a reminders-capable cloud enrols the user unprompted, unless the file already records a decision. Details that are load-bearing, not incidental:

  • No credential, no popup (rebuilt 2026-09-10 — see AC7). Auto-enrolment reads the account email in the browser (Drive: a signed ID token, which grants nothing; Dropbox: get_current_account; GitHub: /user/emails) and posts only that. It never opens a Google popup — it runs at page load, where a popup is both browser-blocked and unasked-for — and the popup path that used to send a Drive ACCESS token as proof is deleted. Failures are swallowed: an enrolment nobody asked for must not raise an error nobody asked for. Pinned by a real (unmocked) test on the adapter, storage/drive-reminder-identity.test.ts.
  • The disclosure renders ABOVE the widget, not inside the plan panel. The plan is slide 2 of the mobile tab layout and every connect path reloads onto slide 1, so a notice inside it would announce itself to an off-screen panel; it is also absent from the no-data-yet render branch — exactly the user who just connected. It is the reminders control itself, so the off switch is one click from the sentence announcing it, and it survives a reload (sessionStorage) until dismissed.
  • Shopify surface only (a deliberate narrowing of AC1's literal text — Brad to confirm). The Pages/self-host build is marketed as almost no Brad server (the record and the chat never reach us; Google sign-in, reminders and scrubbed Sentry errors do) and runs uploads + chat on the user's own key; enrolling that user unprompted would post their account email to Brad's server at page load, the one thing they chose that build to avoid. They keep the manual toggle. It also matters for the kill criterion: trackProductEvent no-ops off-Shopify, so a Pages opt-out would be invisible to the very ratio this decision reverts on.
  • "No email to give" stops the retry loop permanently (hr_reminders_autoenrol_blocked): a GitHub token without the email permission, or a pre-openid Drive grant, will answer the same way next visit. The manual toggle still works and asks the user to type the address once (AC9) — never a silent enrolment on a typed address. Transient failures are not blocks.
  • Switching clouds moves the enrolment, it doesn't duplicate it. Server rows are keyed by email, so a fresh opt-in cannot replace one made under a different provider; the old row is cancelled first. Not counted as an opt-out — a storage switch is not a user's verdict on reminders. A refused cancel stops the switch (2026-10-14, adversary R3). Enrolling anyway wrote the new token over the old one, the only key to the old row, so any 4xx, 5xx, 429 or network failure orphaned it for good. Now the file keeps the old opt-in and the next visit on the new cloud retries the cancel, then enrols. Tests: standalone/reminders.test.ts (400, 429, 500, 503 and a network failure: no enrolment, then the retry).
  • Removed 2026-10-15 (Brad: not needed); a failed reminder cancel on erase is reported to Sentry only.
  • Brad, 2026-10-15: email-box (typed) sign-ups stay cancellable ONLY by the email link. The browser never receives their token: handing tokens out for rows a request did not create would let anyone who types an address take over its reminders, and Brad does not want that exposure. Rows that may have stayed active while cancels failed (2026-09-10 to the AC4 fix) are left as they are: every reminder email carries a working unsubscribe link.
  • Erasing your data reaches the server row (AC1b — tombstoned, or deleted when Drive can prove the inbox), via a pre-erase hook — the capability token that authorises the delete dies with the file, so it cannot run afterwards.

The decision (Brad, 2026-08-11): move to reminders on by default, opt-out rather than opt-in. Sends are rare by design (screening 90d / bloods 180d / med-review 365d cooldowns), so the cost to a user who ignores them is near zero while the value to one who forgets a colonoscopy is the product's entire thesis.

Two constraints that bound the redesign (they are not negotiable and any implementation must satisfy both):

1. RETIRED for Dropbox, GitHub and typed on 2026-09-10 (Brad; see AC7–AC10). Drive alone keeps the provider's word, via the ID token. Former text: The email must be verified — the provider's word, or proven delivery (superseded 2026-08-14; original wording said "never a client-typed address … only after a confirm-link round trip"). The threat is unchanged: anyone can enter victim@example.com and make Brad's server email a stranger. What changed is the accepted proof: Brad rejected the confirm click (loses 20–40% of honest users) in favour of delivery-validation + defense-in-depth**, now specified in US-23 — bounce/complaint webhook un-enrols, 3-day quiet period before any reminder, server-side label allow-list (no attacker-authored text can transit), typed writes can never touch a provider-verified row, refreshes preserve token + cooldowns (no resend amplification, no broken unsubscribe links), one plan-ready email per address ever, prominent in-body unsubscribe. A typed address with none of those protections remains forbidden.

2. Default-on must stay visible, never silent. Auto-enrolling silently would push every cloud-connected user's due-dates + labels to Brad's server without them knowing — quietly weakening the "your health data lives in your cloud, not our servers" promise that the product is marketed on (architecture-v2.md), and inviting spam complaints that damage the sending domain shared with transactional mail. Recommended design point: at the cloud-connect success moment, a visible, pre-checked "Email me when something comes due" with a one-line plain statement of exactly what leaves the device (due date + label + email — never values), unmissable on one screen, plus a permanent off switch in settings.

Where the audience actually is (live pull, 2026-08-10 — this reorders the work): Klaviyo holds 874 captured emails on the commerce list (+39 edu), still growing ~4–5/day (135 in the last 30d). cloud_connect_success has fired 2 times ever. So the provider-verified lane covers ~2 people and the typed-address lane covers ~900: the typed lane is not a nice-to-have Phase 2, it is the entire audience. Build order follows the numbers, not the ease.

Confirmation email sends via Resend, never Klaviyo (decision 2026-08-11). Reminder consent must never be coupled to the marketing list: Klaviyo suppression is list-wide, so a supplement-promo unsubscribe would silently stop "your colonoscopy is due" — a marketing preference overriding a health reminder, with no error and nobody noticing. Two consents, two systems, two suppression lists. Supporting reasons: the confirm mail is textbook transactional (one-time, user-triggered, expected in seconds); a confirm landing in spam fails the whole redesign silently, and transactional streams land better; Resend is already wired (reminder-v2.server.ts, email.server.ts). Precedent already in the code — api.reminders-v2.ts takes verified.email for reminders and a SEPARATE marketingEmail for Klaviyo, fire-and-forget so Klaviyo can never fail an opt-in. Bonus: confirming before adding to Klaviyo filters typos/fakes, which raises Meta/Google audience match rates and cuts per-contact spend.

No confirm-click gate (Brad, 2026-08-11; reaffirmed 2026-09-10 when the credential proof was dropped — the confirm-link alternative was planned, reviewed and rejected for the same reason). Double opt-in loses 20–40% of legitimate signups — taxing every honest user to catch a rare bad one. Instead the plan-ready email (US-22) does the work: a bounce proves the address is dead, and delivery is the enrollment trigger. The residual risk a bounce can't catch is a typo into a *valid stranger's* address (john@ for johnn@), which delivers fine; AC2c bounds that (rare sends + prominent one-click unsubscribe). A click on that email is a strong ownership signal but is never required — treat clicks, not opens, as real (Apple Mail Privacy Protection fakes opens).

The ~900 existing captures (still needs a Brad call): they gave an email for a report, not for reminders, and predate any send. A bulk "want reminders?" mail is a re-permission campaign to people who never asked — real complaint risk on a domain that also carries transactional mail. Preferred shape if we do it: one genuinely useful email (plan re-entry + the reminders offer), once. Both lists are single_opt_in today, so no confirmation habit exists with these contacts.

  • AC1: On cloud-connect success (Drive/Dropbox/GitHub), enrollment happens immediately and without any user action — true opt-out (Brad, 2026-08-11). A user who reads the line and clicks away IS enrolled; only an explicit toggle-off unenrolls. The disclosure is a visible statement + already-on switch on that same screen, never a gate.
  • AC1b: Consequence of AC1, accepted knowingly: every cloud-connecting user's due date + label + verified email reaches the server, where before only explicit opt-ins did. Still no measurement, lab value, or reasoning — the local-first invariant holds — but the population sending metadata widens from ~2 to everyone who connects. Amended 2026-09-10 (review of aae35a3): a toggle-off or erase TOMBSTONES the row (schedule emptied; email + token kept) on every lane; it is DELETED outright only when the request also carries a valid Google ID token for the row's own address. Reason: a bare-token delete made optin→cancel→optin mint a fresh isNew — and a fresh plan-ready email — every cycle. Consequence, stated plainly: for Dropbox/GitHub/typed users "delete all my data" leaves their address in a tombstone on Brad's server until they unsubscribe from an email. Bounded 2026-09-10: a row switched off stays 90 days, then is deleted — the daily reminder cron sweeps emptied rows older than TOMBSTONE_TTL_DAYS (purgeTombstones in app/lib/reminder-v2.server.ts), after the day's sends, and a purge failure is reported to Sentry rather than failing the run. Residual: past the window a replayed optin on that address is isNew again and earns one more plan-ready email — at most one per address per 90 days, under the capture route's 5/day-per-email limiter. Tests: app/lib/reminder-v2-typed.test.ts (window, live rows untouched, select failure throws), app/lib/reminder-v2-cron.server.test.ts (once per run; a purge error never fails the day).
  • AC2 (amended 2026-09-10): The enrolled email is either Google-verified (ID token) OR an address whose plan-ready email delivered without bouncing — that now covers Dropbox, GitHub and typed alike — the typed lane is now its own story, US-23 (promoted 2026-08-14: it is ~10× the cloud lane and the highest-leverage unbuilt thing in the product). No confirm-click gate — see the consent reasoning below.
  • AC2b: A hard bounce disenrolls: no reminders, and the address is suppressed (unsubscribed, not deleted) in Klaviyo — matching US-22 AC3's reversibility decision.
  • AC2c (widened 2026-09-10): Because a delivered-but-mistyped address belongs to a stranger, EVERY reminder to EVERY lane carries the one-click unsubscribe prominently in the body, not just the header. Rare sends (90/180/365d) + one click to stop = bounded, self-correcting harm.
  • AC3: A user can turn reminders off permanently in one action, from the results surface and from any reminder email (RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe already ships).
  • Known residual risks, accepted not fixed (adversarial review 2026-08-13). (1) If a user moves their health-roadmap.json to the Drive trash, the app sees a legitimately-empty query result — indistinguishable from a new user — and re-enrols, minting a token that invalidates the one in the real file; the next schedule push 404s and flips them to cancelled. A silent unsubscribe, very narrow. (2) Drive does two tryServerRefresh round trips per load until enrolment succeeds (one in resolveBackend, one in getReminderIdToken), on two adapter instances sharing localStorage. Refresh grants don't re-issue the refresh token, so no credential can be stranded — it's waste, not risk.
  • AC4: Turning reminders off survives a sync from a second device (see the 2026-08-07 incident below — this AC exists because that exact bug shipped).

- Bug fixed 2026-10-14 (failing test first; live since c2d4192e, 2026-09-10): with no Google proof the client posted the cancel as {op:'cancel', token, idToken: null}. The route's zod idToken: …optional() accepts a missing key but rejects null, so it answered 400 "Invalid input" and never reached the row. Every cancel on Dropbox or GitHub, and a Drive cancel without a silent ID token, failed: "Turn off" showed an error, while the cloud switch and "Delete all my data" (AC1b) left the server row active. Those three were the live failures. (Corrected 2026-10-14, adversary R5: this line first said every hidden-tab cancel failed live too. The keepalive cancel, the age gate's, arrived in d9020aad on 2026-10-14 and was never deployed.) The client now leaves the key out when it has no token (postCancel), on all three cancel paths; the server is unchanged. Optin and update never send a null. Test: app/routes/api.reminders-v2.client-contract.test.ts feeds the client's exact body into the real route action (Turn off on Dropbox, GitHub and tokenless Drive; the age gate's keepalive cancel; erase; the cloud switch): 200 and cancelByToken called. reminders.test.ts no longer pins the null body.

  • AC5: The server still receives only due date + label + verified email + capability token. No measurement, lab value, or reasoning ever leaves the device — default-on must not widen the data sent. Open nuance for Brad (adversarial review, 2026-08-13): a label can carry an inference even though it carries no value. 'Lung screening (low-dose CT)' is emitted ONLY for a ≥15-pack-year smoker, 'Medication review' only for someone on active medication, and result-dependent intervals make some dueAt values a function of a result. Under opt-in the user chose that knowingly; under default-on they didn't. The shipped copy was changed to be concrete rather than reassuring ("the NAME and due date of each check-up, for example 'Colonoscopy — due May 2027'") instead of the earlier "never your measurements or results", which was true and misleading. If Brad wants the inference closed rather than disclosed, the options are generic labels ("A screening is due") or dropping the lung item.
  • AC6: Local-storage-only users (no cloud, no account email) are never enrolled and are never shown a broken control.
  • AC7 (Brad, 2026-09-10 — a ChatGPT audit found enrolment posting the Dropbox access token and the GitHub PAT as "proof of email"; a PAT confers write access to the repo the health data lives in): No storage credential ever leaves the browser for reminders. The optin request carries the account email + the schedule (+ the optional typed marketing address). Google Drive alone still sends its signed ID token — it grants nothing, and the server reads the verified address from it. api.google-token is unchanged (Drive connect needs it; its idToken passthrough now also feeds the browser-side email prefill).
  • AC8: An address-only optin follows the typed lane's rules, for every lane. A NEW address creates the row, receives its capability token ONCE, gets the plan-ready email (US-22) and sits out the 3-day quiet period. An EXISTING address is a schedule refresh (except a Google-verified row, which the address lane never refreshes: US-23 AC7): provider immutable, token never rotated and never returned on the ADDRESS lane (returning it there would hand the cancel capability to whoever typed the address — the silent-unsubscribe attack). Scoped 2026-09-10: the google-drive lane ALWAYS receives its token, new row or existing, because the caller proved the inbox with a signed ID token; withholding it stranded every Drive user on a second device and every user whose squatted row had just been rotated (no token in the file means schedule pushes never start and the toggle-off is a no-op). An address-lane row's token still rotates when a Google-verified caller proves that address. Email-link unsubscribe is a tombstone for every lane, and a tombstoned token refuses schedule pushes so the device flips its own file to cancelled. Accepted, plainly: the refreshed-vs-new reply is a bounded membership oracle — an unauthenticated optin reveals whether an address is enrolled. Bounded by 5/day per email and 20/hour per hashed IP (the capture route's numbers); accepted by Brad 2026-09-10 over the confirm-click alternative. Residual (review of aae35a3): after an email-link unsubscribe, an address-only optin naming that address refills the schedule silently (a tombstoned Google-verified row is the exception: never refreshed by this lane; no plan-ready email, since it is not isNew), and the widget offers that inbox no off switch other than the link in the next reminder. Token squatting is closed: a Google-verified optin ROTATES the token when the existing row was not itself Google-verified (provider = 'google-drive' means verified; the widget's no-ID-token Drive fallback enrols as 'typed'). Per-email limiter key is normalised (case, +tag, Gmail dots) — the stored address is not. Transient Drive refresh failures never set the "no email" block; a fresh connect clears it.
  • Lane B note, deferred 2026-09-10 (late): the tombstone refill. AC8's residual is that an address-lane optin naming a tombstoned address refills that row's schedule silently. The better answer is to send the owner a mail instead: an address-lane optin that hits a tombstone emails that address a "turn reminders back on" link carrying the row's own token, so the person who owns the inbox decides, and nobody else can restart a schedule by typing their address. Not built. It has no usage signal yet — we have never observed the case — and per the constitution a feature we cannot evaluate does not get built.
  • AC11 (2026-09-10): A google-drive optin without an ID token is REFUSED with a 400 by the request schema, never downgraded to the address lane. A body naming the verified provider must carry the proof that provider's lane rests on; accepting the address instead would let anyone write a row wearing the verified label. Before this AC (deployed c2d4192, the morning of 2026-09-10) the address lane accepted that body; a row it wrote would have kept a squatter's token across the owner's verification. Checked the same day: every google-drive row (9) predates that deploy, so no such row exists and nothing is rotated. Two stated residuals on the verified lane: an existing verified row re-enrolled from a new device now shows that device the one-time "reminders set up" notice, and a Drive device whose file records no decision refills an email-link tombstone on its next visit (it always did; the email's off link works every time).
  • AC9: When the provider has no email to give (a GitHub token without "Email addresses: read-only"; a pre-openid Drive grant), auto-enrolment stops and the control asks for the address once, visibly — never a silent enrolment on a typed address. An address already enrolled elsewhere shows "already set up for x@…; use the link in any reminder email to turn them off", never a broken "on".
  • AC10: reminder_optin is counted by the SERVER when a new row lands, for every lane (it is in SERVER_ONLY_EVENT_NAMES; the client emission is deleted). Only the server knows the enrolment landed, and abuse enrolments count rather than hide — the ratio stays honest. reminder_optout is unchanged.
  • AC12 (2026-10-14, adversary R1/R2/R4): A cloud switch to the same email keeps the row. Rows are keyed by email, so the old token still owns the only row there is. Before cancelling, autoEnrolReminders compares the new cloud's address with the file's (trimmed, lower-cased). When they match it posts nothing, keeps the token and writes only the new provider, so the next load does nothing. Before this, the switch cancelled the row and opted the same address in again; the server refreshed it and returned no token, the file kept the old provider, and every load repeated both posts. After five a day the limiter's 429 left the row tombstoned, and the next push's 404 wrote a cancelled the user never chose. A different address still cancels, then enrols, and defers on any failure. If the new address already holds a row (refreshed), the file keeps the old opt-in and the next visit tries again. From the moment a switch's cancel is sent until the new enrolment lands, pushReminderSchedule sends nothing from the new cloud, on load or on tab hide, on that visit and on later ones in the same browser (see the sub-bullets); on load the push runs after the enrolment, so it never races the cancel. A switch that never cancelled holds nothing, and the age gate's cancel still runs. A refused switch cancel goes to Sentry (op: 'switch-cancel') with its status code only. Tests: standalone/reminders.test.ts (Dropbox to GitHub and Drive to Dropbox, same email; the refreshed switch; the held push and the pushes that still run: no switch on this page, local and self-host, Pages, the age gate; the Sentry event), all failing first except the pushes that still run.

- Orchestrator decision (2026-10-14): when the new cloud gives no address yet, the switch stops BEFORE the cancel, so the old row and its reminders continue (the control reads "on → old address") and the next visit retries. Test: reminders.test.ts "a switch to a cloud with no address keeps the old row" (fails without the guard).

- Codex R1/R2 on a9966d80 (2026-10-14): the switch re-reads the opt-in after the identity lookup and acts only if it is the same active opt-in (an erase, a toggle-off or another device's change during the lookup is never overwritten; US-11 AC4); a switch TO Google Drive compares the browser's Drive account email, because Drive's identity carries an ID token, not an address, so a same-address switch to Drive keeps the token too. Tests: reminders.test.ts "the same-address shortcut, to Drive and across an erase" (both failed first).

- Deploy-gate adversary (2026-10-14): the push is held only from the moment THIS page's switch cancels the old row until the new enrolment lands (switchHoldsOldToken), and on load the push runs after the enrolment, so it never races the cancel; a switch that never cancels (no address, unverified email, a stale block) keeps pushing with the old token and keeps the 404 unsubscribe probe. Tests: reminders.test.ts "…enrolment did not land, the push is held" (fails without the hold) and "…no switch run on this page keeps its schedule current".

- OPEN for Brad (adversary R1, 2026-10-14): a DIFFERENT-address switch whose new address already has a row (typed capture, an earlier cloud) gets refreshed with no token every visit: the old row is cancelled, the address row stays live, the control reads the old address, and Turn off / erase reach only the dead token. Rare (two addresses plus an existing row), bounded by the 5-a-day limiter. A proper fix needs a file state for "enrolled elsewhere, no token" (a FileReminderOptIn schema change, merge semantics) and a control line pointing to the email link. Also accepted: after a same-address switch, a second device still on the old cloud pushes the same row from its own file.

- Deploy-gate adversary R1/R2/R4 on 028a627a (2026-10-14). R1: the in-page hold died with the page, but the tombstone lives on the server, so a switch that cancelled and then failed to enrol (5xx, 429, network, no address) let the next visit's push 404 into a cancelled nobody chose. The switch now writes hr_reminders_switch_cancelled (the old token, in localStorage) before its cancel, clears it on a refused cancel and when the new token lands, and a thrown cancel keeps it. The push is held while the file's opt-in belongs to another cloud and either the page flag is set or the marker names its token; a 404 on a token the marker names is never written as cancelled. R2: after the switch's identity recheck the silent enrolment still awaits the cancel, a second lookup and the optin POST, and an erase or a Turn off in that window was overwritten by the new token (US-11 AC4, AC4). Once the optin answers, the silent path re-reads the opt-in; if it is no longer the one the enrolment began from (for a first enrolment, still no decision) it writes nothing and cancels the new token's row, uncounted, with a refused cancel sent to Sentry (op: 'superseded-cancel', status code only). A file that meanwhile holds the same token active (the verified lane keeps its token) is left alone. The manual toggle is unchanged. R4: the load push waits for the enrolment, and GitHub's email read had no timeout, so it now gives up at 10 s like Dropbox's. Tests: reminders.test.ts "a switch's cancel is remembered across visits" (7) and "a decision made during a silent enrolment stands" (5); github.test.ts "a hung read gives up" (1); all failed first.

- Residual (accepted with R1): the marker lives in one browser. Another device on the same new cloud never saw it, so if its own switch attempt stops before the cancel (a failed or empty address lookup, the block key), its push of the old token 404s into a cancelled that syncs to every device. A browser with blocked storage keeps only the page flag. Both need the same file state as the OPEN item above. Also open: a user who goes back to the old cloud before the new enrolment lands keeps an active opt-in whose row is a tombstone; its 404 is no longer written as cancelled, so the control reads "on" while nothing sends.

  • Usage signal (Lane B, declare before code): reminder_optin fires on enrolment (auto or manual; server-side since 2026-09-10, AC10) and reminder_optout on disable — both wired 2026-08-13, both in the shared PRODUCT_EVENT_NAMES enum. reminder_sent fires server-side on each successful reminder send (nil-UUID sentinel; metadata = provider + due-item count, never labels or addresses) — added 2026-08-30 (W35 backlog #3, Brad-authorized live) after the first real send proved sends were invisible. Server-only event names and the nil sentinel are rejected at the client event route, so a browser cannot forge these counters (adversarial review, same day — closed the pre-existing report_email_* hole too). The ratio is the honest measure. Kill criterion: if opt-out exceeds ~30% of enrolments, or spam complaints appear in Resend, the default-on decision is wrong and reverts. Caveat to read the first numbers with: trackProductEvent is Shopify-surface-only and throttles to once per event name per tab session, so these are session counters, not per-user counts.
  • Evidence: ~1 genuine opt-in ever (live query 2026-08-10); reminder_optin 0 fires since instrumentation went live 2026-08-06 — but both existing opt-ins PREDATE instrumentation, so zero events measures reach, not rejection. First default-on week (2026-W33): 18 enrolments, 0 opt-outs (kill-ratio 0% vs the 30% threshold); reminder_optin_v2 2 → 20 rows all-time. Week 2 (2026-W34): 38 enrolments (+111%), still 0 opt-outs ever (0/56 cumulative); rows 58 all-time (52 typed + 6 google-drive, ~9:1). Week 3 (2026-W35): 31 enrolments, still 0 opt-outs (0/87 cumulative); rows 89 (81 typed + 8 drive, ~10:1); 0 bounces, 0 complaints. The first genuine reminder send happened 2026-08-28 (W35): a row enrolled 08-25 with an item already due 08-01 carries a last_sent stamp — the typed lane enrols overdue-at-capture items, so "nothing due until 2027" is stale; sends are live now (evidenced by the cron stamp; no send event existed at the time — reminder_sent shipped 2026-08-30, W35 backlog #3). Cron reminder_v2_cron healthy (lock acquired daily; a transient-lock-error day-skip class was hardened 08-28 — see US-28). Week 4 (2026-W36): 20 enrolments and the first opt-out ever (kill-ratio 1/109 cumulative vs the 30% threshold — reminder_optout's emit is now production-verified); rows 109 all-time (101 typed + 7 drive + the first dropbox row); reminder_sent fired twice (typed, 08-31 colorectal + 09-01 breast) and matched the window's only two last_sent stamps exactly — the event and the stamp now corroborate each other, so sends are observable (W35 backlog #3 closed). Weeks 5–6 (2026-W37/W38): 26 + 14 enrolments; second opt-out ever (2/149); rows 149 (136 typed + 11 drive + 2 dropbox); reminder_sent 2 in W37 (matching the two last_sent map dates) and 0 in W38 (no date in the window — corroborated). Week 7 (2026-W39): 47 enrolments (46 rows: 42 typed / 3 drive / 1 dropbox; 195 all-time), 0 opt-outs (2/195); reminder_sent 3 (09-22/24/25) = 3 last_sent dates, one-to-one. The opt-out count is biased low (annotated 2026-10-14, adversary R4). From 2026-09-10 (c2d4192e) until the AC4 fix is live, "Turn off" failed for Dropbox, GitHub and Drive without a silent ID token, and reminder_optout fires only after the server confirms the cancel, so it could not fire for them. Their opt-outs are missing from every week since, and the kill ratio is lower than the truth. In the widget only Drive users with a silent ID token could opt out; the email link's unsubscribe page counts its own reminder_optout server-side and worked throughout. The product-health trend should note this beside each week's ratio for that window, and not read its zeros as acceptance.
  • AC13: A reminder's exact YYYY-MM-DD date displays its stated calendar month and year, including west of UTC and at year boundaries. Timestamp inputs retain their existing local-time display. Due-date arithmetic does not change. Tests: packages/health-core/src/reminders-date-only.test.ts (New York pinned even on UTC CI) and packages/health-core/src/reminders.test.ts, with schedule/email controls.
  • Tests: ✅ schedule/due logic + store persistence (2026-08-07); ✅ enrolment path — rebuilt 2026-09-10 for AC7–AC10: standalone/reminders.test.ts (25 — AC1 auto-enrol/token, AC7 Google sends only the ID token and Dropbox/GitHub only the address, AC8 refreshed → no file write and no notice, AC9 no-email blocks / transient retries / ReminderEmailNeeded / typed address, AC10 no client reminder_optin, AC4, AC6, Pages no-op, cloud switch, erase teardown, reminder_optout only on a server-confirmed cancel), storage/drive-reminder-identity.test.ts (4 — the real adapter opens no popup, decodes and persists the ID-token email), app/lib/reminder-v2-typed.test.ts (27 — the silent-unsubscribe attack returns no token and rotates nothing, the tombstone refill is not isNew, tombstoned tokens refuse pushes, every-lane quiet period + tombstone), api.measurements.test.ts (7 — enrolByEmail refresh sends nothing), storage/roadmap-store-data-safety.test.ts (2 — an opt-out survives an erase; no token or address survives it). What they do NOT prove: reminders.test.ts mocks at the module boundary, so it pins the fetch payload and the branch logic, not that a real user gets enrolled. ✅ send observability (2026-08-30): reminder-v2-cron.server.test.ts pins reminder_sent on send success and its absence on send failure. ❌ still manual: the live cloud-connect → enrol → notice-visible journey on real WebKit (needs a real provider round trip).
  • Incident 2026-08-07: store-level tests found setGlobalReminderOptout mutated rows without bumping their merge stamps — "turn off all reminders" silently reverted on the next sync. Fixed same day (routed through the stamped upsert path); regression test pins it. The "load-bearing TODO" it left is resolved (2026-08-13) — partly by evidence, partly by code. By evidence: in the v2 builds the off switch is cancelReminders(), which tombstones the server row (it deletes it outright only when the call carries a Google ID token for that address — AC1b) and flips the file's opt-in to cancelled, a stamped LWW singleton that carries the opt-out to every device; the per-category reminderPreferences UI that setGlobalReminderOptout drives (ReminderSettings in ResultsPanel) is unreachable in both v2 builds, because standalone/app.tsx is the only renderer of HealthTool and always passes remindersSection, which wins that branch. Nothing needed seeding. By code, because the first draft of this feature got AC4 wrong and an adversarial review caught it before it shipped: "Delete all my data" resets the file, and an empty file reads as "never decided" — so the next load would have re-enrolled the user, undoing an explicit opt-out via a button promising the opposite, on every device at once (a higher eraseEpoch wins the merge, and since US-09 AC20 a losing copy brings only rows it created after the erase, never its reminderOptIn, so a second device's cancelled record couldn't save them either). The erase now carries the decision without the identity: status:'cancelled', no token, no email. Same bug class as 2026-08-07 — an off switch that comes back on — which is why AC4 is stated as a survival property, not a UI feature. Separately, the dead v1 preferences chain is now unreachable code awaiting a deletion sweep (spans HealthTool + ResultsPanel + api.ts + roadmap-store; it predates this change, so it is a follow-up commit rather than a rider on a consent-model change).

US-18 · Generate my plan as a downloadable PDF (guest capture button)

As a guest, I enter my email and immediately get my whole plan as a downloadable/printable PDF — no account, no waiting on an inbox. (Corrected 2026-08-11: this story used to claim "I can email myself the report", which has not been true since 525e6be, 2026-06-12 — "NO Resend report email, and NO health data reaches the server". Nothing was ever emailed. The general print/save path is US-08.)

  • AC1: The button renders the plan and opens the save-as-PDF/print window client-side — the plan never leaves the device.
  • AC2: The typed address is subscribed to Klaviyo fire-and-forget; a Klaviyo failure never blocks or delays the PDF.
  • AC3: Rate-limited per address (guest report limit) and behind app-proxy HMAC; Shopify surface only — the Pages build has no Brad-server capture path and must no-op.
  • AC4: The PDF is the delivery. US-22 has shipped, so the UI may promise the plan-ready email; once US-23 ships, the capture UI must also carry its reminders disclosure (US-23 AC4).
  • AC5 (2026-09-10): Klaviyo receives an email address and nothing else. KlaviyoProfileData still declared sex, height, weight and birth fields, and the whole profile-properties step (create, 409, PATCH) was still in the code, with no caller filling them since the v1 teardown — dead code a skeptic screenshots before reading the callers. The fields and the step are deleted, so subscribeToKlaviyo sends the address alone, which is what it has actually done since June. The 394 live profiles still carrying those properties from v1 were scrubbed on 2026-09-10.
  • AC6 (2026-10-04, Brad; adversarial review of the product-health W40 plan): a refused print window is never silent. openPrintWindow returns false when window.open gives null, which mail and social apps' own browsers often do, and both callers ignored it: the capture marked the record captured and hid the email box with no PDF and no word. Now, when the window is refused, the capture still completes as before (the address is captured, the plan-ready email goes out, and the plan was already saved on this device as it was typed), and the person is told so beside Save as PDF, in words Brad signs: "The PDF window didn't open. Try Save as PDF again. Some apps' built-in browsers block it." It makes no claim that the plan is saved here: a device that refused storage runs from memory (US-09 AC16), and nothing tells the panel. Every Save as PDF button says the same when its own window is refused, beside the button pressed (the header, and on the Pages build the bottom one too), and each refusal is announced again. A capture whose report could not be built (getReportHtml failing) counts as a refusal, and so does a refusal on a capture that then fails to send, shown beside that error. A later window that opens clears the message, and so does an erase. Nothing sends them to another browser, which would not hold this plan. On a phone the Plan tab's height follows the message (the Swiper's auto-height is re-measured). Usage signal: pdf_window_blocked (browser, name only), once per tab session. Known limit: a window that opens but whose browser ignores print() cannot be detected.
  • Evidence: 874 addresses captured on the commerce Klaviyo list, ~4–5/day, all single_opt_in; 50 unsubscribed lifetime.
  • Tests: 🟡 copy + captured-flag tested; PDF path manual (shares US-08's untested print pipeline). AC6 (2026-10-04): ✅ ResultsPanel.skip-gate.test.tsx (12 AC6 cases: exact copy, capture completes on a refusal, re-announce, Swiper re-measure, refusal beside a send error, report not built, erase, the Pages bottom button) + product-events.server.test.ts; ✅ Chromium render at 393px on the Pages build (slide height follows the note); ❌ owed after deploy: real WebKit on an iPhone viewport, and one real in-app browser. Historical note: a guest's report email silently failed in v1 (feedback 2026-03-16) — that v1 path is gone.

US-44 · Funnel page: Save as PDF without the email box — built 2026-10-02 (Brad-approved 2026-10-02), live 2026-10-03: code health-roadmap-831/edu-97 (bdf4c160), AC3 sign-up marking health-roadmap-832/edu-98 (103adea1); setting ticked on /pages/start (template page.health-start.json) only

As someone who just gave my email on the /pages/health landing page, I reach drstanfield.com/pages/start and save my plan as a PDF without being asked for my email again. I can still ask for check-up reminders, but nothing makes me. Plan: claude_business docs/drstanfield-popup/youtube-roadmap-lead-magnet-plan.md §1 items 4–5.

  • AC1: The app block has a skip_email_gate checkbox ("Skip the email box before Save as PDF (funnel pages only)", default off), emitted on #health-tool-root as data-skip-email-gate. Only the literal true turns it on (resolveSkipEmailGate). The homepage and /pages/roadmap blocks carry no settings, so they stay gated.
  • AC2: With it on, the plan header shows "Save as PDF" from the first render and no email box gates it. The skip is a property of the page: it never calls markReportEmailCaptured() and writes nothing to the user's record, so another device or page behaves as its own block says.
  • AC3: Reminders stay available as one optional line, "Email me when a check-up is due", with a helper line saying the PDF does not need it. Submitting runs the same capture call as US-23 AC1 (sendGuestReport → klaviyoCapture { email, schedule }), opens no print window and counts no A/B conversion. A successful sign-up calls markReportEmailCaptured() (Brad, 2026-10-03), so the plan-ready and reminder emails' link back to /pages/roadmap doesn't ask for the email again in the same browser, or on any device using the same connected cloud (another browser starts empty, US-22 AC13). On the next render the page shows the captured view. The bare page skip (AC2) still persists nothing. A failure keeps the field, shows the error and marks nothing.
  • AC4: The line carries the US-23 AC11 disclosure, worded for a sign-up ("Signing up adds you to the MicroVitamin mailing list…") because getting the plan no longer adds anyone. The US-09 AC5 storage sentence stays last in the box. The line renders once, at the top of the plan, without the guestEmail id or the stage-3 highlight, so finishing the vitals never pulls focus to an optional field.
  • AC5: With the setting off, behaviour is unchanged: the email box gates the PDF, prints first, then marks the record captured. A visitor whose record is already captured sees today's captured view on either page.
  • AC6 (2026-10-04, found while building US-18 AC6): Save as PDF shows on a phone. The plan's header holds the ungated Save as PDF on the Shopify surface (captured, or gate skipped), and styles.css hid the whole column header at 768px and below (the tabs name the columns there), so on a phone /pages/start offered no way to save the PDF at all and /pages/roadmap offered none after the capture's own print. The live check of 2026-10-03 was desktop only. Now the plan column's header keeps its actions on a phone (title and step stay hidden), so Save as PDF and the US-18 AC6 message sit at the top of the Plan tab, as on desktop. The Pages build's plan header shows on a phone too (its Save as PDF was already ungated; the bottom button stays). The input column's header stays hidden on a phone (its guide link has the US-38 footer entry). Verify on a real iPhone viewport after deploy.
  • Usage signal (Brad, 2026-10-03): sign-ups on the /pages/health Klaviyo form (list WaCdqF) are the measure of funnel volume; US-44's own use (PDF saves without the gate, Remind-me sign-ups) is not separately measured, by decision. No new product event. reminder_optin {provider:'typed'} still counts this line's enrolments without a page split.
  • Klaviyo (Brad, 2026-10-03, decided): funnel opt-ins go to list TpwCKK like every other capture, and so receive flow TYaNR2 ("Quick question about your Health Plan") a day later, unless already on TpwCKK. No source marker; US-18 AC5 unchanged.
  • Tests: ✅ ResultsPanel.skip-gate.test.tsx (11: AC1 schema + root attribute, AC2 no persistence + ungated print, AC3 enrolment/failure/validation, AC4 disclosure + single box, AC5 the gated path); assistant-config.test.ts (AC1 parsing). ✅ Live check 2026-10-03 (desktop WebKit, sex + height entered): /pages/start shows Save as PDF and the reminders line with no gate (data-skip-email-gate="true"); /pages/roadmap keeps the gate ("false"). ✅ Dropbox and Google connect on /pages/start (2026-10-03, after Brad registered the redirect URI in both consoles): each reaches its sign-in page with redirect_uri=https://drstanfield.com/pages/start and no mismatch error. AC6 (2026-10-04): ✅ ResultsPanel.skip-gate.test.tsx now 28 (4 AC6: the plan header carries the phone modifier only when it has actions, the placeholder and input headers never, and a styles.css check of the 768px rule); ✅ Chromium render at 393px (Save as PDF at the top of the Plan tab, page width 393); ❌ owed after deploy: real WebKit on an iPhone viewport of /pages/start and /pages/roadmap.

US-22 · Plan-ready email + address validation — NEW BUILD, Brad-approved 2026-08-11

As a guest who handed over my email, I receive an email confirming my plan is ready with a link back to it — so I have a way back in, and so a dead address is detectable.

Why: ~900 people typed an email expecting something and got nothing (US-18). Those addresses have never been validated, and the tool has no re-entry path. This email is also what makes reminders possible (US-17 AC2): delivery — not a confirm click — is the enrollment trigger.

The old implementation CANNOT be restored. Pre-teardown sendReportEmail(userId, client) read health values out of Supabase and built an email containing waist, BP, HbA1c, LDL, ApoB, Lp(a) (git show bbd79fd^:app/lib/email.server.ts). Those tables are purged, and that design violates the v2 invariant — no health value may transit Brad's server. Lift its layout/markup for reference only.

The v2 shape carries NO health data (Brad, agreed 2026-08-11): it confirms the plan is ready, links back into the tool (where the plan re-renders from the user's own localStorage/cloud), and states what reminders they'll get. Local-first promise intact, and it still yields both signals we need — bounce (dead address) and click (ownership + re-engagement). The health specifics still reach people via the reminders themselves, which are already permitted to carry a label and a due date.

  • AC1: On capture, Resend sends a plan-ready email containing no measurement, lab value, medication, or screening data — only the re-entry link and what reminders to expect.
  • AC2: The send never blocks the user's plan; the US-18 PDF delivery is unchanged and a Resend failure is logged, not surfaced.
  • AC3: A Resend bounce webhook (new route — none exists today, signature-verified) marks the address dead → suppressed/unsubscribed in Klaviyo, not deleted (Brad, 2026-08-11: keeps the record and stays reversible if a bounce is misclassified) and never enrolled in reminders (US-17 AC2b).
  • AC4: A delivered (non-bounced) address stays in Klaviyo and becomes reminder-eligible — delivery is the trigger, no confirm click.
  • AC5: The re-entry link is click-tracked; clicks, not opens, are the ownership signal (Apple Mail Privacy Protection fakes opens).
  • AC6: Shopify surface only; the Pages build no-ops.
  • AC7: Once shipped, US-18's UI may promise the email (AC4 there).
  • AC8: New captures only (Brad, 2026-08-11) — no backfill send to the ~900 pre-existing addresses. They stay unvalidated and reminder-ineligible until Brad revisits, once real bounce/complaint rates from new sends are known.
  • AC9: Ships on both Fly apps (commerce + education) together; they share one Resend key and from-address. The bounce webhook needs only ONE endpoint, hosted on commerce: both apps send through the same Resend account, and the handler writes to the shared Supabase + the single commerce Klaviyo list.
  • AC10: The webhook also handles email.complained (spam complaint), not just email.bounced — under an opt-out model a complaint is the loudest possible "I never wanted this", and must suppress in Klaviyo AND unenroll from reminders immediately.
  • Usage signal: report_email_sent / report_email_bounced / report_email_clicked. Bounce rate on new captures is also the estimate for how much of the legacy ~900 is junk — the input to the backfill decision. First live week (2026-W33): 25 sent, 10 clicked (40% CTR), 1 bounced (4%, webhook un-enrolled it end-to-end in production), 0 complaints. 2026-W34: 35 / 21 / 0; 2026-W35: 29 / 10 / 0; 2026-W36: 19 / 11 / 0 (sent / click events / bounced; 0 complaints ever). Standing caveat from the product-health loop (W34): the email events carry one constant visitor_id and no per-recipient dimension, so click:send is an EVENT ratio, never a CTR — the all-time bounce count was 1 at W34 (2 by W39). 2026-W37: 24 / 14 / 0; 2026-W38: 13 / 8 / 0. 2026-W39: 47 / 26 / 1; 2026-W40: 19 / 17 / 0.
  • Brad prerequisite: ✅ DONE 2026-08-13. Webhook registered in Resend (bounced + complained → commerce route), RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET set via file→fly→shred. Live-verified end-to-end with a REAL bounce: signature accepted, {"ok":true,"action":"bounced","count":1}, Klaviyo suppressed, row deleted.
  • AC1 amended 2026-08-14 (US-23/US-24): the email may now ALSO carry the reminder calendar — labels + due dates with add-to-calendar links — when the capture enrolled reminders. That is the constitution's permitted footprint and US-22 AC1's own "what reminders they'll expect", not health data; the "no measurement, lab value, medication, or screening RESULT" clause stands.
  • AC11 (2026-09-10, late): a provider error names no recipient. Every Resend failure was thrown with the address it had just tried interpolated into the message, and that message ends at console.error and, on Fly, in stdout, which is unscrubbed: an outage would have written the enrolled list into the log a line at a time. The message now names no address of ours, and Resend's own text, which quotes the address back ("Invalid to field: …"), goes through scrubText before it is repeated. Applies to the plan-ready email, the reminders and the feedback path alike (resendErrorText in app/lib/email.server.ts). Tests: app/lib/email-error-scrub.test.ts
  • AC12 (2026-09-24): the email says where THIS reader's plan lives, true for each lane. The guest copy (the capture button, api.measurements) says the plan is saved in the browser they made it in, and in the PDF if they saved one; that another phone, computer or browser starts empty; that Safari can clear a saved plan after a week without a visit; and that connecting Google Drive or Dropbox from that browser puts it on any device. The cloud copy (the reminders opt-in, api.reminders-v2, which needs a connected cloud) says the plan is in their own cloud storage and loads wherever they connect the same account. Each send site passes its lane, and the lane is a required argument, so a new caller cannot default into the wrong claim. The button reads "Open the Health Roadmap": it opens the tool and cannot promise the plan. The footer says what the server keeps ("Dr Brad's server keeps your reminder calendar and this email address. Your plan is not stored there.") instead of "Your health data lives only on your device or in your own cloud storage". No em dashes (docs/writing-style.md). Why: the old copy, "Your plan reloads from your own device or your own cloud storage", promised every guest a way back that works only in the one browser that made the plan. Darren made his in Safari, followed a reminder 7d 23h later, and met a blank form (2026-09-24); of 73 arrivals from the plan-ready email, 19 showed no plan within three minutes. Residual, accepted: a cloud user who types a second, NEW address into the capture box gets the guest copy, because that route cannot know the lane without trusting the client.
  • AC13 (2026-09-24): an arrival from either email that finds this browser empty is told why. Both buttons go through /roadmap/open, which lands on https://drstanfield.com/pages/roadmap?from=email, a second hardcoded literal (EMAIL_LANDING_URL); the bare ROADMAP_URL stays for calendar text (US-24 AC2), and nothing in the click's query reaches Location. The widget reads the flag before its first await and strips it at once, keeping every other parameter byte for byte, the hash, and history.state. Only a guest session (no cloud, no reconnect) whose record is empty by HealthTool's own load test (hasSavedRecord) sees a notice above the tabs: "Looking for your plan? If you saved it to Google Drive or Dropbox, connect it and it loads. If not, it stays only in the browser you made it in, and Safari can clear that after a week without a visit. Your PDF still has it, if you saved one." Connect opens the storage picker in one click; Dismiss closes it. The check is awaited before the widget mounts, so a record read that fails shows no notice instead of rejecting into an empty mount (US-09 AC16; the adversarial review of 2026-09-25 found the await uncaught, and the notice's PDF line unhedged against the email's). Recovery is the same visitor_id then firing results_viewed (they re-entered) or cloud_connect_success (they found the plan in a cloud). US-20 · Mobile

As a mobile user, I get a tabbed layout (input/plan/chat) with CSS scroll-snap swiping, and every layout works in real iOS WebKit (not just Chrome emulation).

  • Evidence: mobile engagement is much shallower than desktop (2.6 vs 7.4+ min new-user averages) — worth watching in funnel data.
  • AC1 (2026-09-07): The deployment WebKit check fails on a missing seeded matrix, missing values, collapsed/content-box cells or page overflow, on both desktop and iPhone.
  • AC2 (added by sentry-fix 2026-09-24, Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-6Q): crossing the mobile breakpoint mid-session never crashes the widget. The tab Swiper renders only under isMobile (a live matchMedia listener at 768px), so a desktop window widened past it unmounts the Swiper and swiper/react destroys the instance, which deletes its params; swiperRef still pointed at it, and the next edit ran the autoHeight effect, which threw undefined is not an object (evaluating 't.params.slidesPerView') inside a React commit, so the ErrorBoundary replaced the whole widget with "Something went wrong" (three events, Safari 18.7 / Mac, 09-19 to 09-23). updateAutoHeight is the one reached method that dereferences the deleted params; slideTo checks destroyed itself and returns. All three call sites (the tab sync, the autoHeight re-measure, the chat hand-off to slide 0) now go through one liveSwiper() accessor that returns null once the instance is destroyed. Stated residual: the ref is never nulled, so a flip back to mobile mounts a fresh instance through onSwiper in the layout phase, before any passive effect runs, and the stale one is dropped; HistoryPanel nulls its own chart ref in cleanup and has no equivalent hole. Tests: widget-src/src/components/HealthTool.swiper.test.tsx (2: a Swiper unmounted by the layout switch is destroyed and throws the same TypeError on the real library in jsdom; the ref is read on exactly two lines of HealthTool, the accessor and the onSwiper assignment, so a direct call, ?., !. or an alias anywhere else fails the suite).
  • Tests: ✅ tools/webkit-verify.test.ts pins failure conditions; the current v2 seeded probe passed live on desktop and iPhone on 2026-09-07. Full journeys still need live verification.

US-21 · Additional blood tests on the main matrix — phase 1 SHIPPED 2026-08-07, phase 2 SHIPPED 2026-08-14, phase 3 conversion BUILT 2026-09-18 and SHIPPED 2026-09-23 (factor table verified by Brad before the deploy; recorded 2026-09-27, product-health W39 review R1); the matrix correction UI BUILT 2026-09-24; plausibility bounds still open (heading corrected 2026-09-06; it still read "DRAFT")

As a user whose lab reports contain tests beyond the core 8 (sodium, GGT, TSH, ferritin…), I can see those stored values as grouped rows under the core matrix and add a test I want to monitor via a "+" button — one place to watch everything.

What already exists (why this is surfacing, not building, for phase 1): the labValues collection in health-roadmap.json already captures every extracted additional test (FHIR status/source, value+unit as reported, reference ranges, dedup on (metric_name, recorded_at)). Today it's visible only in History and at upload-review time (ReviewTable); the main matrix never shows it. Label mapping exists (lib/lab-value-labels.ts), reference hints exist (reference-hints.ts).

Draft acceptance criteria (to iterate before build):

  • AC1: Stored lab values render as rows beneath the core 8, grouped by panel (Liver · Kidney/renal · Electrolytes · Blood count · Hormones · Lipids-extended · Other), matching the matrix's column/date alignment and scroll-sync.
  • AC2: "+ Add test" lets the user pick from a curated catalogue (searchable; canonical unit + validation range per test) or add a free-form test.
  • AC3: A known test's row always displays ONE unit; a value arriving in a different unit is converted or flagged at review — never silently mixed into the row (a U/L value charted next to a µkat/L value would be clinically wrong).
  • AC4: Upload-extracted and manually-entered values for the same test land in the same row (alias map keyed on stable metric keys — never dedup on raw LLM text, per the documented gotcha). The extraction prompt's suggested names are the catalogue's own keys, rendered from LAB_CATALOG by panel (LAB_GROUPS labels), as CORE_METRIC_ALIASES renders the core block (2026-10-18). The hand-kept list it replaced had drifted: it named seven tests by something other than their catalogue key (bilirubin, free_t4, free_t3, hs_crp, uric_acid, testosterone and transferrin_saturation, where the keys are bilirubin_total, ft4, ft3, crp, urate, testosterone_total and transferrin_sat; each still resolves through an alias), missed seven keys (mchc, rdw, magnesium, zinc and three others), and suggested nine tests the catalogue did not then hold (homocysteine, fasting_glucose and the like). AC17 catalogued all nine the same day, so a row stored under one of the old names resolves to its catalogue key (fasting_glucose to glucose, fasting_insulin to insulin, the other seven to themselves) and shares a slot (labSlotKey) with a new upload. Tests: lab-extraction.test.ts "US-21 AC4" (every key once, under its own panel; nothing else named; AC17's new keys named; the nine old names on their catalogue slots).
  • AC5: Corrections work exactly like core rows (entered-in-error + correctsId chain — the labValue shape already carries status/source). Built 2026-09-24: a lab cell opens the core matrix's editor, and the correction goes through record-edits.correctValue in the unit the value is stored in. Closing a group never drops a correction left open in it: the correction saves, and one the record refuses is still open, with its reason, when the group reopens (Codex, 2026-09-24: closing the group unmounted the editor before its click-away save ran). Tests: AdditionalLabRows.test.tsx (a phone's tap, a refusal kept), HealthTool.journey.test.tsx (over a real store).
  • AC6: Cross-device merge semantics reviewed for the new slot behavior (Fable-level judgment — merge.ts territory).
  • Usage signal (Lane B mandatory): new product event lab_row_added for manual adds; phase-1 surfacing measured via a lab_rows_viewed event (count metadata). Uploads already emit upload_saved.

Decisions (Brad, 2026-08-07):

1. Units: canonical-units catalogue — option (a). A new packages/health-core/src/lab-catalog.ts defines each test's canonical unit (units.ts discipline; conversion factors added per-metric as implemented, each verifiable). Per-lab reference ranges keep coming from the uploaded report (referenceLow/High already stored) — the catalogue carries units/grouping/aliases, not clinical thresholds, so the evidence-citation surface stays small.

2. Initial panel scope: Renal (incl. electrolytes) · Liver · Thyroid (TFTs) · Hormones · Vitamins & minerals · Inflammation markers. Grow from there.

3. Collapsed by default under the core 8.

4. Each group renders an icon to the left of its heading (kidney → Renal, etc.) — inline SVGs, same no-asset-fetch pattern as the backend-picker logos.

Remaining open questions: exact test list per panel (Brad to review the catalogue skeleton); mixed-unit handling for values stored before a metric's conversion exists (proposal: display as-reported with the unit label until the conversion lands).

Phasing (each phase independently shippable with its own signal):

  • Phase 1 — surface what exists: ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-07. AdditionalLabRows renders grouped, collapsed-by-default read-only rows beneath the blood-test matrix (inline SVG icon per group, count, mixed-unit flag, "Other tests" bucket for uncatalogued names). Logic in lib/lab-rows.ts (13 tests); catalogue resolver handles LLM underscore/space variance. Corrections deferred to phase 2 (at the time labValues had no store-level correct method; since 2026-09-03 the store writes one for the upload review's Replace — US-13 AC3 — and the matrix UI for it is what phase 3 still owes). Signal live: lab_rows_viewed — 15 events in the first instrumented week (2026-W32) vs 190 results_viewed (~8% of viewers expand the additional-lab rows); 2026-W33: 6 (novelty wear-off vs the 08-14 relayout — W34 decides); 2026-W34: 9 (~1.3/day, stabilized — novelty wear-off confirmed, relayout not implicated); 2026-W35: 8 (stable); 2026-W36: 19 (+138% against a down week — plausibly Brad's own connector live-verify sessions loading records; unattributable). AC1 layout fix 2026-08-14 (found live by Brad): phase 1 had shipped expanded groups as horizontal "dated value strips", violating AC1's "matching the matrix's column/date alignment" — expanded groups now render the same bt-* date-column matrix as the core 8 (shared BatchDateCell + CSS vars, per-group date columns, newest column pinned, name column pixel-aligned with the core matrix; layout pinned by a component test + labGroupMatrix unit tests). 2026-W37: 19 (Brad's US-36 verify week); 2026-W38: 4 (back to ~1/day organic).
  • Phase 2 — manual add: ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-14 (add only; corrections still open). "+ Add a blood test" beneath the groups (AddLabTest.tsx): catalogue picker grouped by panel, canonical unit FIXED for known tests (AC3), free-form name+unit via "Other", native date input, saves through bulkSaveLabValues under the stable catalogue key (AC4 — manual and upload-extracted values share a row), store-side same-day dedup surfaced as an inline notice. Section now renders (with just the button) even before any lab values exist. Gated exactly like the labValues fetch (isLoggedIn; always-on for the standalone build). Signal live: lab_row_added — 0 events in its first ~1.5 live days (deployed 08-14; true zero, watch W34); 2026-W34: first 3 manual adds ever; 2026-W35: 2; 2026-W36: 2. labValue CORRECTIONS remain open on the website's matrix — they move to phase 3's scope — but since 2026-09-01 they exist on the other writers: correctValue (US-31 AC3) corrects a lab row from the CLI and the MCP tools, and the upload review's Replace box (US-13 AC3) writes one for a conflicting upload. Manual adds 2026-W37: 4; 2026-W38: 1.
  • Units fix (same day, found live by Brad): the catalogue now covers the common FBC/chemistry tests that were dumping into "Other tests" (new haematology "Blood count" group — Hb/Hct/RBC/WBC/differential/platelets/MCV/MCH/MCHC/RDW — plus eGFR under renal, globulin under liver), and display units are normalized at render: normalizeLabUnit fixes report/LLM spelling ("umol/L"→"µmol/L", "x 10e9/L"→"×10⁹/L", "1.73m2"→"m²"), displayLabUnit relabels same-unit spelling variants to the catalogue canonical (haematocrit "ratio" ≡ "L/L" via per-entry unitAliases), so false "Units vary between reports" flags are gone. SPELLING ONLY — stored values stay as-reported; genuinely different units still flag mixedUnits (AC3).
  • Adversarial review 2026-08-14 (verdict: ship with fixes — applied same commit): dedup slots now resolve to the catalogue KEY (an upload's "Gamma GT" + a manual "ggt" on the same day was two active rows — the exact duplicate the notice exists to stop); Greek μ (U+03BC) normalizes to µ (U+00B5); "m^2" joins "m2"→"m²"; hs_crp resolves; save() catches store throws; future dates blocked in canSave. Residual risks accepted: (1) manual entry has no per-test plausibility bounds — a US-report user can type a g/dL number into the fixed g/L field (10× off, no warning; blast radius is display-only since additional labs feed no suggestion logic; bounds belong to phase 3 with conversion); (2) HistoryPanel still charts raw units/raw-name series (cosmetic inconsistency with the matrix); (3) cross-device merge unions by id, so a same-day name-variant pair created on TWO devices before syncing still survives merge — closed 2026-09-02 by US-10 AC3: lab slots are keyed on the catalogue key at merge time (labSlotKey), so the variants converge to one active row and the loser flips to entered-in-error; (4) eGFR reported as bare "mL/min" deliberately still flags mixed units — raw clearance is genuinely a different quantity than the BSA-normalized canonical.
  • Phase 3 — normalization + corrections: conversion BUILT 2026-09-18, factor table verified by Brad (clinical content), SHIPPED 2026-09-23 (manual deploy 3296cf2; first lab_unit_refused 2026-09-24T06:02Z). Unit conversion at the write for catalogue tests; per-test plausibility bounds for manual entry are still owed. The website matrix's own correction UI (AC5) was built 2026-09-24. The factor table lives in health_roadmap_algorithm.md §2 and is pinned to LAB_CONVERSIONS by a drift test, so a factor cannot change in one place.
  • AC7 (the storage contract, one conversion site): a catalogued test is stored in the catalogue's SI unit on EVERY writer — website, CLI, stdio MCP, hosted MCP — because all three write doors (appendLabValue, bulkAppendValues, the lab branch of correctValue) call one canonicalLabValue in lab-catalog.ts. A writer sends the number and unit as the lab PRINTED them; nothing upstream converts. A unit spelling the catalogue does not know for that test is REFUSED (unknown-unit), and the refusal names the canonical unit and every spelling that test accepts — never guessed from the number, which is the mistake that stores a US lipid as an SI one. A test the catalogue does not know has no SI definition, so it is stored exactly as reported, with its printed unit; refusing it would throw the value away. Prolactin in ng/mL is refused on purpose: the mIU/L factor is assay-dependent. So is urea in mg/dL under the bare name "urea" — a US report prints the nitrogen and the rest of the world the molecule, so mg/dL reaches that slot only under a nitrogen name ("BUN", ×0.357), which resolveLabCatalogEntry supplies by returning the entry the PRINTED name earns. The extraction prompt says so too (2026-10-18; unifiedSystemPrompt, shared by the website, the BYOK build and import_documents): it copies each row's unit exactly as printed, beside the result, else in that row's own reference range, else in the column header (a row's own print outranks a shared header, review 2026-10-18); it never converts a value or relabels its unit; it returns an empty unit when the row prints none; and it returns the printed reference range for AC8 to convert. Before, it said nothing about units: a sheet printed vitamin B12's unit only in its range column, the model labelled the pg/mL number pmol/L without converting it, and the catalogue stored it 1.35 times too high. An empty unit on a core value (null, missing or blank alike, as on an additional value, so the row is never dropped; review 2026-10-18) takes the range fallback and is flagged for review (confidence: medium with a question); on a catalogued test it is refused (unknown-unit, shown per AC11 as "Ferritin: no unit was printed, so it was not saved. This test takes µg/L.", never "unit not recognised ()"; review 2026-10-18), since its scale is unknown; an uncatalogued test (INR, a specific gravity, a ratio) is kept unitless by the website's save (bulkAppendValues). A unit of whitespace alone reads as empty at the parse, so no path stores a blank label. The assistant tools' door, appendLabValue (behind add_lab_values, file_results and the connector's import), still refuses an empty or blank unit, unchanged while they are under OpenAI's review. Tests: lab-extraction.test.ts "US-21 AC7" (the prompt text in both modes; a range-only unit and its range reach the write as printed and convert by one factor; an empty unit is never guessed), record-edits.test.ts and mcp-tools.test.ts "US-21 AC7" (no printed unit: the website keeps INR unitless and refuses ferritin; the assistant tools refuse both, as before).
  • AC8 (the range travels with the value): referenceLow and referenceHigh convert by the SAME factor as the value, on every one of those doors. A converted value beside an unconverted range would read as out of range for a result that never was.
  • AC9 (rows written before phase 3): corrected at load, never mutated. migrateFile appends a converted row with the deterministic id <id>#si, correctsId pointing at the printed row, the original createdAt/recordedAt, and flips the printed row to entered-in-error (monotonic, so a client that has not converted still converges). Same id and same content on every device, so mergeFiles folds the copies into one row — no #dup- ids, exactly one active row per slot — and a second migrate is a no-op. NO schemaVersion bump: a bump makes every older app and CLI refuse the file (SchemaTooNewError), and a converted row is readable by any version. A row already holding the right number (an accepted same-scale spelling, factor 1) is left alone — a correction row there would assert a value was wrong when it never was. Such a row therefore keeps the spelling its report printed ("ug/L" stays "ug/L", not µg/L): it is numerically identical, the catalogue reads it as the canonical unit anywhere it matters, and rewriting a label is not worth a correction row.
  • AC10 (correct_value converts): the lab branch takes a unit and converts it, as the core-metric branch already did; omitting it means newValue is already in the unit the row is STORED in. A unit on an uncatalogued test is refused rather than silently ignored — there is nothing to convert it to.
  • AC11 (a refused row is shown, not dropped): bulkAppendValues returns the refused lab rows with the reason; the website's upload done panel shows them as refused with the printed unit, and the import commit says so in words and offers the units it takes. Usage signal (Lane B mandatory): lab_unit_refused with {key, unit} — the catalogue key and the unit spelling only, NEVER the value, which is the whole point of refusing it. It is the signal that says which spelling to add next. The hosted MCP already counts unknown-unit refusals. A result flag or qualitative result is a value too (2026-10-13 review): a unit carrying one ("mmol/L H", "mmol/L (HIGH)", "Reactive", "erhöht", "pos.") or a stray * never lands with its unit: the widget sends the event with the key alone, and the server stores the row with the key alone. Digits are structural: once the constructions units are spelled with (10^9, ×10³, /1.73 m², mm3, /100, /24h) are cut, no digit may remain. Words are an allowlist of unit atoms, because three review rounds showed no denylist is ever complete: every run of letters, in any case, must be a unit atom (UNIT_ATOMS: SI-prefixed mol, g, L, eq, U, IU, kat and osm; the count words labs print in English, Polish, German, Spanish, Portuguese and French, such as cells, tys, mln, Tsd, Mio, K, thou; and time, pressure and length words), and the unit must hold at least one atom, a % or a construction. A letter standing alone as a token is refused even when it is an atom ("mmol/L L", "mmol/L-H"; "U/L" and "g/dL" are one token each), and so is a token of dashes alone ("-", "--"). Every catalogue and UNIT_DEFS spelling passes, held by a test (isLabUnitWord; tests: app/lib/product-events.server.test.ts, widget-src/src/lib/local-first-data.test.ts).

W41: 14 rows from 3 visitors, all after AC15 merged (47 rows from 5 visitors all-time); none of W40's AC14/AC15 targets came back refused. 3 of the 14 are spellings again: platelets and WBC in 10^3/mm³ and RBC in 10^6/mm³, written with a superscript ³ (the catalogue takes ASCII 10^3/mm3 for WBC and platelets, and no mm3 spelling for RBC). 9 repeat W40's by-design refusals: urea mg/dL, prolactin ng/mL and % differentials. MCH in g/dL and RDW in fL are other quantities.   • AC13 (2026-09-22 feedback: "impossible to edit a mistyped 'add a blood test'"): a mistyped value is fixed where it shows, corrected in place (AC5). Adding a test that already has a value that day no longer dead-ends: the form names the value there and offers "Replace 45 µg/L with 54", a correction through the cell editor's own door (correctsId, the same day, manual_correction), never a second row. It is not offered when the number typed is the number there, or for an "Other" test typed in another unit. Any change to the form withdraws the offer (the test, its name, its unit, the day or the number), and Replace checks again, just before it writes, that the value it names is still this test on this day in this unit; a refusal says why, in the cell editor's words.   • AC14 (2026-10-04, Brad; product-health W40 lab_unit_refused): normalizeLabUnit folds three spellings that name the same unit, for every test. gm/dL becomes g/dL (the gm fold is held to that one spelling: a bare gm/L would land on g/L, which the count tests read as giga per litre, and mg/gm stays as it was). Unit or Units becomes U (Units/L is U/L). cmm, cu mm and c.mm become µL (a cubic millimetre is a microlitre, so 10^3/cmm is ×10³/µL, which is ×10⁹/L, and 10^6/cmm is ×10¹²/L). No factor changes and no new conversion: each fold lands on a spelling the catalogue already accepts or refuses, so a test that refused the canonical spelling still refuses the folded one. Two effects follow. A stored row written before phase 3 in gm/dL (haemoglobin, albumin, total protein, globulin, MCHC) is converted on the next load by the existing AC9 path, an <id>#si correction at ×10 with its bounds and the old row entered-in-error; Units/L and cmm rows are factor 1 and left alone. An uncatalogued test's unit is folded where it is shown (an uncatalogued "Units/L" displays as U/L); the website's record keeps the printed unit, while a connector import, which files the displayed unit (mcp-tools.ts), stores U/L. The same unit either way. Unit(s) with brackets is not folded. Not folded, proposal only and Brad's call: differentials in cells/µL (a ×0.001 factor to ×10⁹/L), differentials in % (a different quantity), TSH in mInt-unit(s)/mL (an ambiguous prefix), FT4 as a T7 index (a different test). Signal: lab_unit_refused (AC11) stops showing the W40 pairs that now resolve; it records the printed unit, so a folded spelling that still lands on a refused one (a cells/cmm differential, TSH in Units/L) keeps appearing, as it should.
  • AC15 (2026-10-04, Brad): three more of W40's refused spellings. (1) White cells, the five differentials and platelets accept a count printed in cells per microlitre (cells/µL, and cells/cmm / cells/cumm through the folds) at ×0.001 to ×10⁹/L: a microlitre is 10⁻⁶ L, so 2,400 cells/µL is 2.4 ×10⁹/L. Guard: cells are counted, so a cells/µL value, or a reference bound printed with it, that is not a whole number refuses the row, never rescaled; a decimal means the lab printed thousands under the wrong label, and a value and range that disagree leave neither trustworthy. The same reasoning covers a whole number in the wrong magnitude: under cells/µL, when both bounds are printed, a value above a hundred times the high bound refuses the row (platelets 250000 with a printed 150–400), and for WBC and platelets only, a value below a hundredth of the low bound does too (a ×10³/µL platelet value of 250 mislabelled against 150000–450000). The differentials get no low-side check, because real counts sit near zero (an eosinophil count of 0, severe neutropenia), and 0 is always accepted (it reads the same on any scale). That is a check of the value against its own printed range, not a clinical threshold (proposed by the orchestrator after the final review; kept, Brad 2026-10-06: a refusal stores nothing wrong, and its one cost is a genuine platelet count near 1,000/µL, which the person can type in ×10⁹/L); real extremes (a WBC of 200,000 or 100 cells/µL against 4,000–11,000) pass. A refusal for the number says what was wrong: a decimal count, or a value and printed range on different scales. The assistant's copy of either says never to re-send it in another unit on its own but to ask the person; the person's copy of the decimal case may point them to the ×10³/µL line on their report. A correction (correct_value) runs the same check against the row's existing range, read on the canonical scale, including a legacy row still stored in a factor-1 spelling such as K/uL or 10^3/cmm. The website counts lab_unit_refused only for a spelling it does not take; a refusal for the number is not that signal. Every door checks the same row, the connector's import preview included, so a preview never offers what the commit refuses. No per-test minimum yet: Brad sets those (US-21 plausibility bounds, still open), and until then a mislabelled whole number can still land. (2) cumm folds to µL like cmm (a cubic millimetre either way), the common Indian spelling (10^3/cumm). (3) A differential printed as % stays refused (a share of the white count, not a count, and never multiplied out from the WBC), but its refusal says the absolute count is what the record keeps, so the person looks for the cells/µL or ×10⁹/L line on the same report. The assistant's copy of that refusal also says not to work the count out from the percentage. TSH in mInt-unit(s)/mL stays refused (Brad, 2026-10-04: the prefix is ambiguous, milli or a misread micro, and the catalogue never guesses from the value). Three-file sync: the cells/µL factor joins the §2 conversion table in health_roadmap_algorithm.md; evidence.ts and roadmap_text.html carry no unit spellings or thresholds that change.
  • AC16 (2026-10-12, Brad; product-health W41 lab_unit_refused): a cubic millimetre written mm3 or mm³ folds to µL, as cmm does (AC14), but only as a denominator: directly after a slash, and as a whole token (the end, a slash or a space follows it). So 10^3/mm³ and 10^3/mm3 reach WBC, platelets and the differentials at ×1 to ×10⁹/L, 10^6/mm³ and 10^6/mm3 reach RBC at ×1 to ×10¹²/L, and cells/mm³ takes AC15's cells/µL path with its whole-number and magnitude guards. 1 mm³ is 1 µL, so no value is rescaled beyond what the µL spelling already does. Three effects follow: a legacy row stored in cells/mm³ or cells/mm3 converts once on load at ×0.001 through the #si correction path, with AC15's guards; K/, k/, thou/ and thousand/ over mm3 now reach the ×10⁹/L counts, and M/, m/ and million/ over mm3 reach RBC, as the existing µL aliases do; and a bare mm³ (a volume, such as a plaque volume) is never folded.
