  • AC21 (2026-10-20, Brad, from a real user's sheet): a value no human sample reaches is refused, never rescaled. The sheet printed free testosterone as "nmol/L" while its number and range (163–473) were pmol/L, so the faithful ×1000 conversion showed an impossible result of about 312,600 pmol/L in the review, and it would have saved. AC15's count check compares a row with itself, so it cannot catch a value and range mislabelled together. A catalogue entry may carry a ceiling in its canonical unit, set only where a ×1000 upward conversion reaches it: free_testosterone and free_testosterone_calculated 10,000 pmol/L, reverse_t3 10,000 pmol/L, c_peptide 50,000 pmol/L, reticulocytes 2,000 ×10⁹/L. Troponin carries none: a real high troponin overlaps a mislabelled one. Only a row converted by a ×1000 prefix step meets the ceiling: one whose converted value, or converted printed high bound, passes it is refused (fault: 'ceiling'). A row in any other spelling (the canonical unit, pg/mL, ng/dL, ng/mL) is never refused by it, because a real result can pass it (free testosterone on heavy androgen use can exceed 10,000 pmol/L, printed as pmol/L or as a US lab's pg/mL; review R1 and re-check, 2026-10-20). A refused row goes through the path every other refusal takes (canonicalLabRow → null), so the append, the bulk save, a correction in a unit and the review table's stored-value preview all see it. The person reads "Free testosterone above 10,000 pmol/L is not a measured value, so the printed unit is probably wrong (nmol/L vs pmol/L). Check the report, then add it in pmol/L with + Add a blood test.", and reads it before Save (Brad, 2026-10-20): in the upload review the row's cell shows that same line under the value, in place of the converted preview, never the impossible number, and the line follows an edit. A printed high bound past the ceiling refuses the row whatever is typed in the cell, so the line sends the person to + Add a blood test, in the test's own unit, after Save (adversary R1, 2026-10-20). A cell already recorded shows no line (R2). The review still counts the row in its Save total, as it counts a row in an unrecognised unit, and Save refuses it as before; the assistant's copy adds that it must not re-send the row in another unit on its own. The refusal's own words never name the number. The connector's file_results line keeps the shape every row refusal there takes, the row the assistant itself sent and then the refusal ("Free Testosterone 200 nmol/L: Free testosterone in "nmol/L": …"): no telemetry, and the assistant already holds the row (review, 2026-10-20). The refusal is not counted as lab_unit_refused (the test takes the spelling). Load never deletes or rewrites a stored row: a legacy printed row above a ceiling gets no #si child, and one an older build already converted stays as it is. A number-only correction (no unit) does not convert, so the ceiling does not apply there. Two limits, stated. Without a printed range, a prefix error that lands under the ceiling is not caught (a female free testosterone of 8 printed as nmol/L stores 8,000 pmol/L). Duplicate matching (sameLabQuantity) converts with canonicalLabValue, which has no ceiling, so a re-upload of a row an older build already stored over the ceiling shows "already recorded"; stored rows are never flagged (append-only). Display rule, not a threshold or suggestion change: evidence.ts and roadmap_text.html describe no catalogue refusal. Usage signal: none new; a ceiling refusal shows on the upload summary and in the connector's "Not filed" line. The ceilings themselves are Brad's (confirmed 2026-10-20): free testosterone 10,000 pmol/L, reverse T3 10,000 pmol/L, C-peptide 50,000 pmol/L, reticulocytes 2,000 ×10⁹/L.

AC19 and AC20 (2026-10-20): ✅ lab-catalog.test.ts now 406 (a printed spelling → SI value for every new test, the panels, the FEU, pmol/L and U/L refusals, serum-only osmolality, what stays uncatalogued, new tests never one slot with their neighbours, every AC20 spelling, "Urea (BUN)" refused in mg/dL, the core names), lab-extraction.test.ts (the prompt's TARGET METRICS and ADDITIONAL VALUES lists pinned to main's, review 2026-10-20), lab-catalog.test.ts review round (osmolality and reverse T3 spellings, the % and per-100-WBC notes, each realistic BUN name in mg/dL), lab-conversions-doc.test.ts (§2 carries every new factor), instrument-scrub-parity.test.ts (literals re-pasted), mcp-tools.test.ts (the new English words pass the feedback guard; the new tests still refuse). Examples of an uncatalogued test in record-edits, migrate, lab-rows and lab-value-labels tests moved from lipase and reticulocytes (now catalogued) to plateletcrit and large unstained cells. AC21 (2026-10-20): ✅ lab-catalog.test.ts (free T 312.6 nmol/L with 163–473 refused; 0.45 nmol/L stored as 450 pmol/L; 312 pmol/L stored as printed; a value in range refused when its high bound converts past the ceiling; a row not converted by a ×1000 step never refused by it (11,000 pmol/L and 2,900 pg/mL stored, 11 nmol/L refused); the five ceilings and none on troponin; the refusal text without the number), lab-conversions-doc.test.ts (the §2 ceilings are the code's, both ways), mcp-tools.test.ts (the file_results line's shape), record-edits.test.ts (append, bulk save and correction refuse it), migrate.test.ts (rows above a ceiling left as they are at load), lab-value-labels.test.ts (the person's line), ReviewTable.units.test.tsx (the review shows the line for free T 312.6 nmol/L with 163–473 and no 312,600; none for 312.6 pmol/L).

US-23 · Typed-email reminders — THE TRUNK (Brad-approved 2026-08-14; LIVE since the 08-14 deploy — heading corrected 2026-09-06, it still said "awaiting deploy")

As someone who typed my email to get my plan PDF, I get reminded when my check-ups and blood tests come due — because my lane is ~10× the cloud lane (874+ captures, ~4–5/day vs 3 cloud connects ever). This was the highest-leverage unbuilt thing in the product; it is live, and the ~10:1 bet has held every week since (US-17 evidence).

Why it's safe now: US-22's delivery-validation machine is live and verified (signature-checked bounce/complaint webhook → Klaviyo suppression + deleteByEmail). Delivery is the consent gate Brad chose over confirm-clicks; a bounce un-enrols before any reminder could ever fire.

  • AC1: When the capture button is pressed, the client sends the schedule alongside the email — the same client-computed labels + due dates as US-17, stored as one reminder_optin_v2 row with provider: 'typed'. Nothing else crosses (constitution: calendar, not chart).
  • AC2: No reminder is ever sent to a typed address until the plan-ready email has had time to bounce. Precisely (2026-08-14, second review): the gate is a quiet period, not positive delivery confirmation — the cron skips typed rows for 3 calendar days from created_at (effective floor ~2d8h given the 08:00 UTC send hour; never updated_at, which refreshes touch), and the bounce/complaint webhook un-enrols within minutes-to-hours, comfortably inside it. This covers the overdue-at-capture case too. Residual, accepted: a plan-ready send that FAILS outright (Resend outage) is logged, not retried — the enrolment stands on the typed consent + quiet period alone. Upgrading to a Resend delivered-event flag is future hardening.
  • AC3 (both lanes): Every reminder email carries the user's full upcoming schedule, not just the due item — the email is the surviving artifact for a user whose localStorage is long gone (constitution: durability). The server already stores the whole list; this costs nothing.
  • AC4: Labels are specific ("Colonoscopy, due May 2027"), per the constitution's recall-letter decision — and server-validated against health-core's SCHEDULE_LABELS allow-list: an unauthenticated capture names someone else's inbox, so no client-authored text may ever transit into an email (the old free-text label field was the hole). The capture UI carries a one-line disclosure that typing the email turns reminders on, with the off switch named.
  • AC5: EVERY reminder to a typed address carries the one-click unsubscribe prominently in the body, not just the header (a superset of US-17 AC2c's "first reminder" — a delivered-but-mistyped address belongs to a stranger; rare sends + one click = bounded harm).
  • AC6 (both lanes): The annual floor — if the computed schedule has nothing due within 12 months, seed one "Annual health check-in" item 12 months out. Every enrolled person gets at least one touch a year; a colonoscopy-every-10-years user must not get a decade of silence (Brad, 2026-08-14).
  • AC6a: A malformed or missing active-medication review stamp contributes no candidate and cannot suppress a valid medication-review date. Keep the existing 12-month interval and annual floor without inferring or persisting a replacement date. Tests: reminder-medication-malformed.test.ts. Amended 2026-10-21 (Codex R4): a stamp that is not a real calendar date (not-a-date, 2026-02-30) reads as an unknown time at migration, never as the file's anchor, which the schedule would have taken as a review date. The whole stamp is checked, not just its day: a real day with a broken time or offset, or trailing junk (2099-01-01T99:00:00Z, 2026-05-01 junk), is not a time either. Every shape a writer emits stays valid: toISOString, a date-only day, +13:00 and +0530 offsets, fractional seconds, lowercase t/z, a zone-less time, and Postgres's text style (2025-01-15 03:00:00+00), which files imported from v1 may hold. That style needs its zone: a zone-less 2025-01-15 03:00:00 is unknown time, because the merge would read it in the machine's own zone. Residual, createdAt: a garbage row createdAt is still clamped to the anchor, as before. Reading it as unknown time would let an erase drop the row, a deletion, so it stays out of this AC. Residual, deploy order: a client older than this fix still turns a garbage stamp into its file's anchor at migration, and a file it saves keeps that anchor as a real stamp, which no later reader can tell from a genuine one. Tests: migrate.test.ts.
  • AC6b (Brad, 2026-10-21: "we always need to use international time, so that everything is standard and timezones don't break"): reminder date maths is UTC calendar arithmetic. The same file at the same instant gives the same schedule in every timezone: the annual floor, the age the rules read, v1's overdue check and the cron's re-send cooldown. Screening due dates were already zone-independent (built and read in the local zone, always the 1st of a month). The time rule (Brad, 2026-10-21: "the database is always UTC, and then it's the user interface that actually shows the correct time zone"): moments (saved, uploaded, erased, every row stamp) are stored in UTC and shown in the user's time zone; calendar dates (a lab's collection date, the birth month, a screening date) are stored as the date itself, with no zone, and shown as written everywhere; "today", the day what is due is measured against, is the user's local calendar day, computed at display time. Server-side reminder maths uses UTC days until the user's time zone is stored (AC12). The schedule is server-side reminder maths: it is pushed to the server and emailed on a day, so it uses UTC days now; the plan's own "today" (US-31 AC11) stays the user's local day. Tests: reminder-utc.test.ts and reminder-v2-cron-utc.test.ts, both pinned to Pacific/Auckland.
  • AC7: Re-capturing with the same email refreshes the schedule ONLY — the token and last_sent cooldowns are preserved, and a typed write can never touch a provider-verified row. Each of those three is load-bearing: a rotated token breaks the unsubscribe links in every email already sent (the page would claim success while the row lives on); reset cooldowns turn one re-capture/day into daily re-sends of whatever is due; and clobbering a verified row would 404 the victim's own device into a silent "you unsubscribed". The schedule too (2026-10-20, security; found by an outside scanner): until then an address-lane optin (typed, Dropbox, GitHub: email and schedule only, and the Origin allow-list is not authentication) rewrote the schedule of whatever row held that address, a Google-verified one included. Now enrolByEmail's refresh is an UPDATE filtered provider <> 'google-drive', so a verified row's schedule is left whole; its owner keeps it current through the token-authenticated update op. The filter sits in the write itself, so a verified write landing after the lookup is covered, and the reply ({refreshed: true, email}), the queries and the round trips are the same whichever row it met: no oracle beyond AC8's accepted refreshed-vs-new one. Residual, accepted by Brad 2026-09-10 and restated: an address-lane row (typed, Dropbox, GitHub, or Drive's no-ID-token fallback, stored as typed) still takes its schedule from anyone who names its address, bounded by AC8's limits and by AC6's annual floor; token, last_sent and provider stay untouched. A verified owner on the address lane gets the same reply and is not refreshed either: a device without its capability token, or the PDF-capture typed enrol (api.measurements.ts), cannot move the schedule; it stays what their token-holding device last pushed, floored by AC6. Tests: reminder-v2-typed.test.ts "US-23 AC7".
  • AC8: Abuse bound for victim@example.com (rebuilt after the second adversarial review found the first version had three bypasses): the plan-ready email fires ONLY on a NEW enrolment — a schedule-less body sends nothing (was: per-capture), a capture against a cloud-enrolled address sends nothing (was: per-capture at exactly the most engaged users), and unsubscribe is a durable TOMBSTONE for typed rows (schedule emptied, row + token kept), so a replayed capture is a refresh (no email), not a fresh enrolment (was: unsubscribe→re-capture minted a new email each cycle). Plus: per-IP rate limit (20/hr) beside the per-email 5/day, the response is CONSTANT (an enrolled field was a membership oracle for typed emails), labels allow-listed (AC4), unsubscribe links never rot (AC7 + provider-upgrade token preservation), complaint (US-22 AC10) suppresses + un-enrols immediately.
  • AC9: Shopify surface only — the capture UI is now gated on SHOPIFY_SURFACE explicitly (before 2026-08-14 Pages was protected only by its hardcoded data-logged-in="true" attribute — an accident, not a gate).
  • AC10 (2026-09-24): every reminder email, every provider, opens the tool through ${APP_BASE_URL}/roadmap/open?src=reminder, never the GitHub Pages build. Its clicks count as reminder_email_clicked (server-only, no metadata), apart from the plan-ready email's report_email_clicked; the query only picks the counter, by exact equality, and the destination stays one literal (US-22 AC13). The footer makes no storage claim that is false for a lane: "Dr Brad's server keeps your reminder calendar and this email address. Your plan is not stored there." replaced "Your health data lives only in your own cloud storage", false for the typed lane (169 of 183 rows on 2026-09-24). The button reads "Open the Health Roadmap", and the email has no em dashes. Why: the button linked drbradstanfield.github.io/roadmap/, a different site from the storefront where every reminder reader made their plan, and a 404 on the day it was found; five reminders had gone out, one since 09-18. PAGES_APP_URL went with it: the button was its only caller. The unsubscribe page both emails link to said the same false thing ("it lives only in your own cloud storage") and now says only that the health data is unaffected (adversarial review, 2026-09-25). Tests: plan-ready-email.test.ts (the button, the footer, no em dash), roadmap.open.test.ts (the counter), product-events.server.test.ts (server-only), reminders-v2.unsubscribe.test.ts (the confirm page).
  • AC11 (Brad, 2026-09-28): the capture box and the reminders opt-in name the MicroVitamin mailing list and say whose it is. The box reads "Getting your plan adds you to the MicroVitamin mailing list (Dr Brad's supplement company), and we'll email you when a check-up or blood test is due. We store only check-up names and dates, never your results. Every email has a one-click unsubscribe." The reminders control's unticked box reads "Also add me to the MicroVitamin mailing list (Dr Brad’s supplement company). Unsubscribe anytime." Why: every sign-up from both stores joins MicroVitamin's list (one Klaviyo account, on purpose), and the server records marketing consent (email.marketing.consent: 'SUBSCRIBED' in klaviyo.server.ts). The old copy named only the reminders, and the opt-in promised "Dr Brad’s evidence-based health emails", so neither said what the person was joining. Decided (Brad, 2026-09-28: "stay as is"): the capture box discloses rather than asks. The stricter EU/UK reading of GDPR consent, a separate unticked box for the list unbundled from getting the plan, was offered and not chosen.
  • AC12 (⬜ planned, Brad 2026-10-21): reminders fall due on the user's own calendar day. The enrolment saves the user's IANA time zone, read in the browser from Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone, beside the schedule, and the cron computes what is due on that zone's local day. Until then reminders use UTC days (AC6b), so a reminder can land up to a day early or late for a user far from Greenwich.
  • Usage signal: reminder_optin vs reminder_optout, both carrying provider so the lanes are judged separately; same ~30% kill criterion as US-17. Both sides of the typed ratio are counted SERVER-side: optin on the capture route (only NEW enrolments — refreshes don't inflate the denominator, and abuse enrolments are counted rather than invisible), optout on the unsubscribe page (the typed lane's primary off switch — it was structurally blind before the first review). Bounce rate on new sends stays the estimator for the legacy-~900 backfill decision (US-22 AC8, still Brad's open call).
  • The annual floor (AC6) is computed client-side AND clamped server-side on every write (ensureAnnualFloor — pure date arithmetic, so the server stays a dumb scheduler). The server clamp is an integrity bound, not UX: anyone who knows a typed user's email can overwrite their schedule via re-capture (AC7's refresh is unauthenticated by construction), which would otherwise be a silent per-user kill switch for the retention engine; with the clamp, the worst an attacker achieves is degrading a victim to annual check-ins — each carrying the one-click off switch. Tombstones (explicit unsubscribe) are exempt: an off stays off. annual_checkin is a first-class ReminderCategory (group annual, 365-day cooldown).
  • Known residual risks, accepted knowingly (second review, 2026-08-14): (1) a typed schedule remains rewritable by anyone who knows the email — bounded by the floor clamp, label allow-list and real-date validation to "someone could change WHICH canonical items/dates a victim is reminded of", with every email carrying the off switch; (2) a deliberate re-capture refills a tombstoned schedule — that's the opt-out model's re-consent path, and an attacker using it buys only rare reminder-cadence emails; (3) the rate limiters are per-process in-memory (reset on deploy, per-machine) — bounds are soft, ×2 across the two Fly apps.
  • Evidence: first live week (2026-W33, deployed 08-14): 17 typed enrolments vs 3 cloud rows all-time — the ~10:1 typed-lane bet held almost exactly; plan-ready CTR 40%. Week 2 (2026-W34): 35 typed enrolments (accelerating), plan-ready click:send ratio 60% (21 click events / 35 sends — event-level, no per-recipient dimension yet), 0 bounces, 0 complaints. Week 3 (2026-W35): 31 enrolments (typed-dominant; moved with the week's -26% reach dip, not worse); 29 sends / 10 click events (34% — uncohorted drift, not a verdict); 0 bounces/complaints in W34–W35 (all-time: 1 bounce, W33; 0 complaints). Production rows with provider 'typed' + delivered emails now exist, though the deliberate end-to-end capture walk-through the Tests line calls for is still owed. Week 4 (2026-W36): 20 enrolments (moved with the reach dip), 19 sends / 11 click events, 0 bounces/complaints; typed rows 101 of 109 all-time — and the typed lane produced the first two observable reminder sends (08-31, 09-01; see US-17) and the first opt-out (1/109). Weeks 5–6 (2026-W37/W38): 26 and 14 enrolments; sends / click events 24/14 and 13/8; 0 bounces/complaints; typed rows 136 of 149. Week 7 (2026-W39): 47 enrolments; sends / click events 47/26; 1 bounce (second ever); typed rows 178 of 195. US-22 AC13 / US-23 AC10 live 09-24: email_landing_empty fired twice in its first days (one visitor, 09-24, 15 min apart) and that visitor fired nothing else — no recovery yet (W39 backlog #4); reminder_email_clicked 0 (two of the week's three sends predate the deploy; one after — a zero at n=1).
  • Tests: ✅ 25 server/health-core cases 2026-08-14, incl. a ROUTE-level suite (api.measurements.test.ts) pinning the isNew gate, the schedule-less and cloud-row no-send paths, the constant response, the tombstone, upsertOptin's typed-refusal, the server floor clamp, and the real-date refine. ❌ live verify after deploy: a real typed capture → row lands with provider 'typed' → plan-ready email carries the calendar. ✅ AC11 (2026-09-28): ResultsPanel.local-first.test.tsx pins the capture box's list sentence; standalone/reminders-control.test.tsx pins the opt-in's label, placeholder and aria-label. ✅ Real WebKit on the live page, 2026-09-28 (edu-93, iPhone 13 and desktop), AC11: the capture box showed the new sentence, with "MicroVitamin mailing list" at weight 600. The reminders opt-in's label is pinned by reminders-control.test.tsx. Its live check is owed, because it needs a connected cloud.

US-24 · Add my check-ups to my calendar — Brad-approved 2026-08-14 (links, not attachments)

As a user reading my plan or a reminder email, I can add any due item to my own calendar in one tap — Google/Apple's calendar becomes a reminder engine Brad never operates (the zero-server rung of the reminders ladder).

  • AC1: Implemented as Google Calendar template links (calendar.google.com/calendar/render?action=TEMPLATE…) — plain URLs, no attachments (Brad, 2026-08-14: cleaner than .ics; Resend supports attachments but links beat them on deliverability and simplicity).
  • AC2: Each link creates an all-day event on the due date, titled with the label, description linking back to the tool — via the canonical storefront URL (drstanfield.com/pages/roadmap), never a fly.dev backend host: the description is visible text in the saved event, and a raw redirect URL reads as phishing (found live by Brad, fixed 2026-08-14; cost accepted — calendar-sourced returns go uncounted, only the email buttons route through /roadmap/open, since 2026-09-24 both of them, US-23 AC10).
  • AC3: Links appear wherever the schedule renders in email (plan-ready email once US-23 gives it a schedule; every reminder email).
  • AC4: Zero server-side storage change; zero new data crosses.
  • Tests: ✅ URL-building pinned (plan-ready-email.test.ts: TEMPLATE params, exclusive end date incl. year rollover, re-entry pointer); email placement pinned in the calendar-section suites.

US-25 · The mobile app — architectural destination (native iOS build started 2026-10-21; decisions: ios/architecture.md)

As the avatar's future self, I have an app that makes the whole thing automatic: on-device notifications (reminders with no server at all — the true serverless end-state), HealthKit ingestion (US labs push results into Apple Health; the app reads bloods, recomputes the plan, no typing), durable storage (no localStorage wipe anxiety). The enrolment/consent model built for US-17/US-23 transfers as-is; the server calendar shrinks toward zero as users migrate. Every near-term decision gets checked against the constitution's question: *does this move toward or away from the phone?*

  • Usage signal (Brad, 2026-10-21): App Store Connect analytics (installs, sessions, retention, crashes, opted-in users). The app sends no product events to our server; it cannot see "viewed a plan".
  • AC1 (spike, 2026-10-21): the app runs the same health-core engine as the web, in JavaScriptCore, with no WebView. For the sample record (docs/examples/health-roadmap.sample.json) at a pinned instant, the app's plan JSON equals Node's byte for byte, with the time zone pinned to UTC and to Pacific/Auckland. Tests: ios/HealthRoadmapTests/EngineParityTests.swift, goldens from ios/scripts/build-engine.mjs.
  • AC2 (spike): on launch the app shows that plan's suggestions natively, in the web results panel's groups and order (Requires Attention, Next Steps, Foundation, Skin Health, Supplements), each card opening to its full text, ingredients, guideline tags, the reason and the references, with the web's disclaimer, whose "consult with your healthcare provider" line carries the doctor framing (no plan header, so the cards start near the top: Brad 2026-10-21; My plan has a small title bar since 2026-10-21, so scrolled rows blur away under it instead of running beneath the clock; My data has none since AC17), and how long the plan took on the phone. Limits: plan under 100 ms, cold engine load under 300 ms (ios/architecture.md D2). Simulator only so far; a real iPhone is still owed.
  • AC3 (tabs, Brad 2026-10-21): two tabs, My data first and My plan second, the web's mobile order (Input, Plan); the app opens on My data. Chat is the third tab (US-52, 2026-10-21).
  • AC4 (the record lives on the phone): the app keeps one health-roadmap.json, the web's schema, in its own storage under the phone's data protection. Until the user connects a cloud (AC11) it is stored nowhere else, and it is never stored on our servers (chat and lab upload send what US-52 lists); its folder is marked for iOS to leave out of iCloud and computer backups (isExcludedFromBackup, Brad 2026-10-21). My data says so: since AC11 it names the connected cloud, or, after a Disconnect, that the copy synced earlier stays in that cloud, or that connecting one is how the record reaches the web or a new phone. First launch starts an empty record with health-core's createEmptyFile. Every write is health-core's own (updateProfile, stampProfile for the unit choice, appendMeasurement, correctValue, and since AC7 upsertMedication and upsertSupplement) run in the engine: Swift builds no rows and checks no ranges. A write reaches the disk, atomically, before the screen shows it; a refused write changes nothing on disk; a record the app cannot read is never overwritten.
  • AC5 (My data): About you (sex, birth year and month, height), units (metric or US), Vitals (VITAL_METRICS) and Blood tests (BLOOD_TEST_METRICS without PSA, as the web: PSA belongs to prostate screening). Each row shows its latest active value in the user's units, with its day. Adding a value takes the user's unit and a day (today by default, never the future); a value the engine refuses shows the engine's own words. A second value for a day that already has one asks first, and replacing it is a FHIR correction (a new row with correctsId, the old row entered-in-error). Nothing can be removed (append-only).
  • AC6 (the plan is the record's): My plan computes from the stored record whenever it changes. A record without a usable height or sex (health-core's one PlanError) asks for them in plain words, with a way to My data; any other failure shows the engine's own words.
  • AC7 (engine writes for medications and supplements, D4b 5/5, 2026-10-21): the engine's My data edits take a medication (medicationKey, drugName, dose) and a supplement (supplementKey, supplementName, dose, status active or stopped, an optional startedAt). Each is checked against the API's own medicationSchema and supplementSchema (a known medication key, a positive dose, a lowercase supplement key, a status), then written by the web's own upsertMedication and upsertSupplement (state-edits.ts): the keyed row with its lamport, an append-only history row when the change classifies (started, stopped, switched, dose changed; none for an identical re-save or an escalation answer), the file clock moved forward. A supplement's startedAt must be a real day or instant that has happened; a stop needs a supplement the record holds. A refusal answers { ok: false } with a reason and writes nothing. The tab shows them since AC8. These writes do not yet run through RecordSession.edit, so they have no save loop, merge on conflict or erase guard: follow-up, once the app keeps a session open (ios/architecture.md D4). Tests: ios/engine/my-data.test.ts (6: a medication started then dose-changed; a bad key or a negative dose refused; a supplement saved and soft-stopped keeping its start; a start that is not a real past day refused; a stop of an unknown supplement refused; a bad supplement key or no status refused).
  • AC8 (medications, screenings, supplements on screen, 2026-10-21): My data shows the web form's medication, cancer screening, bone density and supplement questions, with the web's words, options, hints and show-when rules, because both clients read them from health-core's input-form.ts (medicationForm, screeningForm; the web's InputPanel.tsx imports the same text and write rules, and InputPanel.input-form-parity.test.tsx renders the web form against them). Medications follow the plan's cascades (the plan's lipid marker and weight trigger, computed from the stored record): each step opens as the plan suggests it, flat questions without hints when no cascade runs, no section without a relevant value. An answer is written by the web's own rule: medicationWrites then upsertMedication behind medicationSchema; screeningWrites (the answer, then '' for each later answer it closes) then setScreening behind SCREENING_KEYS and screeningSchema. The engine writes only a question the form shows now, with an answer it offers (a pickable option, a month in the web's ten-year past or five-year future range, pack-years a whole number 0 to 200); anything else is refused and writes nothing. Screening questions wait for the plan's age (sex, birth year and height) and say so. PSA, under prostate once the user will screen, is a dated measurement with its own history. Supplements: the featured list as one-tap quick-add with the web's default doses, the rest of health-core's list by search, any typed name with the web's custom key, a dose and unit per supplement, and stopping as a soft stop (status stopped, a history row) kept under Stopped with "Taking again". No delete or remove control anywhere.
  • AC9 (value history, 2026-10-21): tapping a vital, blood test or PSA that has values opens its history: a trend chart of the active values and every row newest first, entered-in-error rows struck through and labelled, the plan's current value marked (or, when the plan sets it aside as out of range, marked as not used). A metric whose rows are all entered in error still opens its history. Tapping an active value corrects it (correctValue: a new row, the old one entered-in-error); there is no delete. A metric with no values opens entry directly.
  • AC10 (launch, 2026-10-21): a new user first sees a welcome screen: what the app does, that the record lives on the phone or in their own Dropbox or Google Drive and never on our servers, and that it is education, not medical advice (App Review 1.4.1); "Get started" is the only way on, and it shows once. The app asks for an App Store rating only after values were saved on three separate days, at the next opening of the plan, once per app version, after a two-second pause that leaving the tab cancels (iOS itself caps it at three a year). Only day stamps and the version asked are kept, in UserDefaults, never a health value. The app has its icon (a road rising to a heart, ios/scripts/make-icon.py), a green accent, the Health & Fitness category and Apple's privacy manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy: no tracking; UserDefaults reason CA92.1). Tests: ReviewPromptTests.swift (new user not asked; three days then the plan asks once; many saves on one day count once; a new version may ask again); the welcome screen checked by hand in the simulator.
  • AC11 (cloud sync, 2026-10-21; design: ios/architecture.md D2, D4, D5): the cloud button on My data's About you line (AC17) opens Sync, which offers Connect Dropbox and Connect Google Drive. Google Drive is wired but waits on its iOS OAuth client id (Brad creates it in the web's Google Cloud project); until then its button is disabled and says so, so only Dropbox is claimed to work. Sign-in is PKCE through ASWebAuthenticationSession with the web's own Dropbox app and an iOS client in the web's Google Cloud project; tokens live in the Keychain, this device only, and refresh with no client secret. Once connected the app's record IS the cloud's health-roadmap.json, the file the website uses. The sync is health-core's own code run in JavaScriptCore: RecordSession (save loop, re-read, merge on conflict, erase guard), SyncManager, dropbox-rest.ts and drive-rest.ts, over a small fetch and timer bridge (ios/engine/shim.ts); Swift rewrites none of it.

- AC11a: first connect when the phone and the cloud both hold a record merges them (health-core's liftDeviceCopy); neither side's rows are dropped.

- AC11b: every My data edit runs through RecordSession.edit with the erase the screen showed, so it gets the debounced save, the merge on a conflicting write (both rows survive) and the erase guard.

- AC11c: the app re-reads the cloud on launch, on returning to the foreground, and every minute while on screen; a change made on the web appears without a relaunch. An erase made on another device (a higher eraseEpoch) is taken in.

- AC11d: a save the cloud refused is kept on the phone (the device mirror, US-09 AC4) and sent with the next session; while the cloud cannot be reached the app works on the phone's copy and says so.

- AC11e: Sync shows where the record is and its state in plain words ("Synced with Dropbox", "Saving…", "Not synced: Dropbox could not be reached. Your changes are on this iPhone."). Disconnect copies the cloud record down, merged, then drops the tokens; the app goes back to the record on the phone. The cloud file is never deleted.

- AC11f: My data says where the record is kept: in the cloud the user connected (never on Dr Brad's server), or after a Disconnect on this iPhone with a copy still in the cloud synced earlier (review A3), or only on this iPhone. My plan's line claims only where the plan was worked out, since chat and lab upload send data (US-52).

- AC11g (review, 2026-10-21): an edit is checked against the record the user saw. A sheet pins the erase and the units it opened on; a value saved after a remote erase, a remote unit change or a switch of sync on or off is refused with plain words (Codex R1, R2). An edit is taken only once it is merged into the phone's file and marked pending; a phone that cannot write it refuses it and nothing changes (R3).

- AC11h (review, 2026-10-21): a reopen that fails goes back to the phone's file, and edits made while the cloud opens wait there and are merged in; a Disconnect made while an open is under way wins (R4, R5, A5). A re-read that fails says why (a revoked grant shows "Sign in again"); a Drive rate or daily limit is a retry, a full Drive says so, and none of them asks for a sign-in (R6, A8). "Synced" shows only when nothing waits on the phone (F1). Each engine session is numbered; news from a session the app no longer shows is dropped, and of two racing opens only the newest stays (F2, F4). Signing in again as a different account is refused: Disconnect first (A6). The record's account is Dropbox's account_id or Drive's about.user.permissionId.

Each reading is an appended row with source: apple_health and the HealthKit UUID as externalId; recordedAt is that instant with its offset (2026-10-21T08:30:00.000+13:00), so its date is the slot's day and the web shows it as a moment, not a UTC day. A reading whose id any row carries, entered-in-error included, is skipped. It fills an empty day, or replaces the day's earlier Apple Health reading (compared as instants) as a FHIR correction (correctsId, the old row entered-in-error, the new row keeping its own time on the same day), so the day's latest reading is active whatever order readings arrive in; it never supersedes a value a person typed or corrected. The two halves of a blood pressure (one pairId) land together or not at all: a pair missing a half, with a half out of range, or meeting a typed or later half, lands neither. Readings measured before the record's erasedAt are skipped. Height fills an empty profile height only. Out-of-range values, other metrics, readings timed after now (five minutes allowed for a device clock running ahead; compared as instants, so a reading from a zone already on the phone's tomorrow still lands) and times without an offset are skipped. A batch with nothing new returns the same record, so nothing is written. Deletions in Health are never handed over (append-only). These rules hold on one device; across devices the merge keeps the newest-written row of a slot, which can undo them (cloud-sync slice, merge-class). Blood glucose is not read: it is a catalogue lab value, and lab rows carry no externalId (Health Records labs are out of scope, D6).
  • AC14 (Apple Health out, engine rules): health-core's deviceWrites (device-export.ts) lists what the app writes to Apple Health: each slot's active weight or waist row, and a day's blood pressure once both halves are there, as one reading. A row from Apple Health, or a correction of one (judged by the chain's root), is never written back. Each write is keyed by the root id of its correction chain, with the chain's length as a rising version (both chains' for a blood pressure), so a correction replaces the sample even if the phone's clock went back. Blood tests are not written.

The open chat drops its conversation. Afterwards My data is empty, the user's units are kept (a setting, as the web keeps its unit preference), and the welcome screen does not come back. With Apple Health connected (AC15), the erase then deletes the samples this app wrote to Health (by source, all healthroadmap: sync ids) and forgets their written versions; readings other apps and devices wrote stay in Health, and the import anchors stay, so they are not imported again (D6). The confirmation says both. Health refusing the delete never undoes the record erase; the result says so and points to the Health app. Known gap: an erase made on another device erases this phone's record and reminders, but not its chat history, which lives only on the phone. Review fixes, 2026-10-21 (adversary R1-R6, Codex R1-R3): with a cloud open the chat tombstones are written by the app inside the engine's pre-erase step, after the read and before the record goes up, so a kill between the two never leaves the record erased and the chat whole (Codex R3); Connect and Disconnect are refused while an erase runs, and the erase page hides its back button, so the session the erase writes under cannot be swapped (R2); an answer streaming in the chat when the erase lands is dropped, never shown in the emptied chat or saved (R1); after a Disconnect the confirmation says that connecting that cloud again erases the same values there (the higher epoch and its listed rows win, US-09 AC23; R3); an unreadable phone record names the one way left, deleting the app (R4); a refusal other than an unreachable cloud shows the engine's own words (R5); the cloud file is described as keeping the erase, not as empty (R6). The engine's bloodPressure edit (ios/engine/blood-pressure.ts) writes both rows on that day, as the web's matrix pairs them, or neither: a half out of range, a future day or a missing number writes nothing. A day that holds either half asks first ("This day already has a blood pressure"); replacing it corrects only the half that changed (a correctsId row, the old one entered-in-error): re-correcting an unchanged half would join merge's last-writer-wins and could undo another device's fix of it (review, 2026-10-22). A half the day lacks is added; the exact same pair writes nothing. A replace carries the ids of the day's active rows the user saw (from the value being corrected, or read when the "replace it?" prompt shows); if the day's active rows differ at save time, in the phone file or through the cloud session, nothing is saved and the user sees "Your record changed while this was open, so this was not saved. Close this and enter the value again." (Codex R1, adversary R3). Tapping a value with any history pushes its page (no longer a sheet), laid out as Apple Health's: a range picker (W, M, 6M, Y, All; a range is offered only when it holds some values but not all, and with only All left there is no picker), the latest value large with its day, a Swift Charts line chart, and every value newest first with AC9's correction (no delete). Blood pressure plots systolic and diastolic as two lines; its history replays each day (orchestrator, 2026-10-22). Every row of the day, both halves, active or not, is put in write order (createdAt; at a tie a correction after the row it names, then id) and grouped into writes: a row joins the open write when its half is not there yet, it is within 5 s of the write's first row (the web, CLI and MCP stamp each half with its own clock) and it does not correct a row in that write. Each write sets its halves on the pair and leaves a snapshot; a half not yet written is a dash. The pair now is shown active and every other snapshot struck, newest first; a snapshot equal to the one before, written only by rows now set aside, is dropped. So correcting only systolic 120 to 130 shows "130/80" and, struck, "120/80"; a one-half day replaced shows "120/82" and, struck, "–/80"; edits a second apart (120, 125, 128) and an Apple Health batch of three readings keep every value. A row merge's slot reconciliation set aside (entered in error, no correction naming it) is listed, as AC9 lists every value, over the pair as it stood, but never changes the pair later writes build on, so it cannot leak into the active pair. Each history row has its own id; pairIds are the day's active rows from the engine's own slot lookup (findActiveInSlot), the ids a replace sends back. No target band: the engine gives the app no target or reference range, and the app invents none. "Add Data" (top right) opens entry. US-52 · Chat and lab upload in the iPhone app, with no sign-in — added 2026-10-21 (Brad: "chat and lab upload in the app, no user sign-in"; design: ios/architecture.md D8)

As an app user, I ask Dr Brad's chatbot about my plan and upload a lab report, without making an account, and the server that pays for the AI knows each request came from a genuine copy of the app.

  • Usage signal: App Store Connect analytics only (US-25, D9): the app sends no product events. The server's own operational counters (turns and files per day, refusals by reason) are numbers with no health value, kept in its logs.
  • AC1 (the gate): /api/app/v1/chat and /api/app/v1/lab-import answer only a request that carries an App Attest assertion from a key the server registered (/api/app/v1/attest/challenge, /api/app/v1/attest/register). Registration verifies the attestation against Apple's App Attest root CA (pinned), a fresh server challenge (HMAC'd, 5 minutes), the nonce in the leaf's extension, the key id as the hash of the certified public key, the app id (team id + bundle id, from env), counter 0, the environment's AAGUID, and the credential id; a key id already stored is a 409. Each assertion signs SHA256(method, path, SHA256(raw body)), so it covers this request and no other; its counter must be higher than the stored one, advanced atomically, so a replay fails. The key is looked up before the body is read. Any other failure is a 401 with a closed reason, and no Anthropic call is made.
  • AC2 (fail closed): with no team id configured, the key store unreachable, or on the brand surface (CHAT_SURFACE=brand), the endpoints answer 503; they never fall back to letting a request through. A key-store error is never reported as an unknown key.
  • AC3 (simulator bypass): the simulator has no App Attest. A request with the dev header is accepted ONLY when APP_ATTEST_DEV_BYPASS=1 AND NODE_ENV is development or test (an allow-list: unset or production refuses, whatever the flag says; tests prove both). The app sends the header only in a DEBUG build on the simulator (#if DEBUG && targetEnvironment(simulator), checked by reading the code: a test cannot build the other configurations).
  • AC4 (limits): per key exactly (60 turns, 30 files per UTC day, counted in the same SQL step as the counter), per IP (IPv6 by /64) and per machine (APP_CHAT_DAILY_CAP, APP_LAB_DAILY_CAP), for chat turns and lab files separately; lab files also spend the web's shared per-machine file cap (machineFiles, US-35 AC10), and the app's own cap is the smaller one so the app cannot use up the web's. Over a limit answers 429 and calls no model. Key registration attempts are capped per IP.
  • AC5 (chat): the app's turn runs the web widget's pipeline (api.chat.ts): classifier, router, the same model, posture and guardrails, NDJSON streaming (status, sources, text, done). The app sends what the widget sends: the question, the conversation's earlier turns from its own file, and chatContextOf over the record (health-core). The server stores nothing of the turn: no conversation or message rows, no guest session, no match-event row, no audit row (D9). No form edits are proposed to the app (its UI cannot apply them yet).
  • AC6 (chat on the phone): a Chat view, native SwiftUI. Before the first message a consent screen names Anthropic, says what is sent (the question, the conversation, and the health summary from the record), that Brad's server keeps none of it, and that Anthropic handles it under its API terms (no training on it, kept for a limited time); nothing is sent until the user agrees. A "Stop sharing" control withdraws the agreement. The answer streams in with its status lines and the articles it drew on. Conversations are kept on the phone in chat-history.json, written by health-core's ChatSession (the web's rule: title, cap, tombstones). A saved conversation reads back with each question above its answer, on the phone and the web (health-core's mergeMessages order, 2026-10-21).
  • AC7 (lab upload): a "+" button opens a sheet to pick a PDF, JPEG, PNG or ZIP through the iOS file importer (Files, and Dropbox or Google Drive when their apps are installed). The phone reads the file the way the web does (a PDF page with text goes as text, a scanned page as a JPEG; a ZIP's PDFs and images one by one; the web's page and size limits) and sends it to /api/app/v1/lab-import with ownDates: true and refusedRows: true (so values the report dates itself are kept, and refused rows come back as such), which runs the web's extraction (extractOrClassify) and returns proposed values. The server stores nothing. A consent screen like AC6's comes first.
  • AC8 (the app writes the record): the extracted values are shown for the user to confirm, each with its day (the value's own day, else the report's; when the report prints no full day the user picks one). A value the extractor asked about (its question, such as "Was this a blood test?") shows the question and starts unticked; one it was unsure of, or whose unit it guessed, says to check it. Only ticked values are written, by health-core's bulkAppendValues (the web's and the connector's one bulk rule) with source: lab_import: a slot that already holds a value is skipped and said so; a lab unit the catalogue refuses is listed as not saved. Values from an undated previous column are not offered (the server strips them: the app does not send undatedPrev). Non-lab documents are not filed yet.
  • AC9 (the privacy sentence, D9): the plan screen no longer says "No health data left your device", which chat and upload make false; it says the plan was worked out on this iPhone.
  • Not yet: replacing a held value from the review (the web's "Replace"), filing documents and originals, chat proposing form edits, Apple's fraud-risk metric from the attestation receipt.
  • Tests: ✅ app/lib/app-attest.server.test.ts (attestation and assertion verification against a test CA built with openssl, every refusal), app/lib/app-routes.server.test.ts (the gate, the key read before the body, the bypass refused in production and with NODE_ENV unset, limits incl. the per-IP failure budget, the chat pipeline called with the widget's shape and nothing stored, lab extraction reused), ios/engine/app-doors.test.ts (chat context, chat history through ChatSession, the lab review with the extractor's question, the save through bulkAppendValues), ios/HealthRoadmapTests/AppChatLabTests.swift (the same doors in JavaScriptCore, the NDJSON reader, the signed client data, PDF and ZIP reading), ios/HealthRoadmapTests/AppServerE2ETests.swift (opt-in: one real chat turn and one synthetic lab report against a local server, passed 2026-10-21). US-53 · The YouTube bot skips a comment it cannot reply to, and never reports that as an error — added 2026-10-22 (Brad approved; Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-74)

US-27 · YouTube bot posting caps hold when the data layer fails — added by sentry-fix 2026-08-27 (spec hole found via Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-64/65/66)

As Brad, on whose channel the bot posts publicly, its safety caps (50 replies/day, 10/video lifetime) bind under ALL conditions — including when the Supabase reads behind them fail.

  • AC1: A failed cap read (today's post count, per-video totals) fails distinguishably (throws, same convention as the tick's other pre-posting reads) — never a value indistinguishable from zero posts.
  • AC2: With either cap unknown, the tick posts nothing (top-level or follow-up), logs the skip, and retries next tick.
  • Tests: 🟡 youtube-bot.server.test.ts pins AC1 at the readPostingCaps gate (Supabase error on either read → rejects; success → both caps). AC2's tick half (catch → post nothing → log → retry) is review-verified only — tick() isn't exported; extracting it is a future testability task.
  • Origin: from 2026-08-26 an intermittent Supabase-side PGRST303 ("JWT issued at future") made ~⅓ of cap reads error; each affected tick silently re-armed the full daily budget (error was mapped to count 0 / empty map).
  • Status: shipped by sentry-fix's Tier 3 PR #30, deployed 2026-08-27; the PGRST303 class (JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-64/65/67) has been quiet since 2026-08-28T16:11Z (product-health W35, W36). Brad closed decision issue #32 as leave-to-Supabase.

US-28 · Daily crons survive transient lock errors — added by sentry-fix 2026-08-28 (spec hole found via Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-66/68)

As Brad, whose server runs five daily jobs behind a cross-machine day lock (reminder emails, trending ×2, the YouTube ops summary, the chat-text purge), a transient database error while acquiring the lock delays that machine's attempt to the next hourly tick — it never silently cancels the job for the day.

  • AC1: A transient DB error in tryAcquireCronLock (lock UPDATE or verify SELECT) fails distinguishably (throws, US-27 AC1's convention) — never the same false that means "another machine won". Permanent conditions (no admin client, missing seed row, malformed date) still return false: retrying cannot fix them.
  • AC2: On such an error the caller leaves the day unmarked and retries next tick; a genuine false still ends its day. Because the day lock itself is the cross-machine gate, a retry can never double-run a job another machine already claimed.
  • Tests: 🟡 cron-lock.test.ts pins AC1 (update error → rejects; verify error → rejects; won/lost/missing-seed/bad-date → boolean). reminder-v2-cron.server.test.ts pins AC2 for the reminder caller (rejection → re-attempt next tick then run; false → no re-attempt). The other two callers (trending, youtube-bot-summary) inherit AC2 through their existing tick catch — review-verified only (identical tick shape; exercising each would repeat the reminder test around modules that self-start on import — trending's starter is disabled under NODE_ENV=test, and the summary cron's missing test guard is flagged follow-up drift).
  • Origin: the US-27 platform fault also hit tryAcquireCronLock (JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-66: 4 events 08-26/27; -68: reminder_v2_cron + trending_cron 08-28). Every caller mapped the error's false to "day done", so one transient error made that machine skip its daily job; whether the job ran at all then depended on the other machine winning the lock.
  • The chat digest is deleted (Brad, 2026-09-10). One of the two ops summaries mailed every chat turn and reply of the past day to Brad — message BODIES, found by an audit of what a skeptical assistant reads out of this repo. Gone with it: the module, its admin trigger, its SIGTERM stop, its cron-lock name and its seed row; nothing imported it but itself. Brad: "I don't have time to read the responses anyway." The count stays five because chat_text_purge (US-15 AC7) took its place in the lock table, and the AC1/AC2 behaviour above is unchanged.
  • Status: shipped by sentry-fix's Tier 3 PR #35, deployed 2026-08-28 — the day the first genuine reminder send came due inside the fault window (US-17). REMIX-66/68 quiet since; -68 marked resolved.

US-51 · Brad's embedded-admin buttons run their action — added 2026-10-21 (Sentry 7803370248, found live after the b625b92f deploy)

As Brad, when I press a button in the embedded admin (run the trending cron, the reminders or YouTube summary trigger, create or stop an A/B test), the action runs on both Fly apps.

  • AC1: a form POST from the embedded admin reaches its route's action. Fly terminates TLS and react-router-serve sets no trust proxy, so react-router builds request.url as http://<app>.fly.dev while the browser sends Origin: https://<app>.fly.dev; react-router's CSRF check (since 7.12) compared the two and answered every admin action 400 in 3 ms. react-router.config.ts allowedActionOrigins lists exactly the two app hosts, health-tool-app.fly.dev and health-tool-edu.fly.dev. The check matches the Origin's host only, so any other origin (another host, a lookalike suffix, *.fly.dev, admin.shopify.com, null, localhost) still gets 400 before the action. The check covers UI-route actions only, single-fetch (.data) and document POSTs alike; resource routes (/api/*, /webhooks/*, /mcp) are not checked by react-router and rely on their own auth. Besides the admin routes, the one UI-route action that now passes same-origin is /auth/login's form POST (Shopify's login(), already capped by US-09 AC25). CORS is untouched. Residual, stated: each app also accepts an action POST whose Origin is the other app's host; both are ours. The list is static because the build runs once per app without SHOPIFY_APP_URL; a new app host must be added here.
  • Tests: ✅ app/routes/admin-action-origin.test.ts (the real react-router request handler with the config's list: an https Origin to an http request.url runs the action on both hosts; no Origin runs it; six foreign origins get 400 and never reach the action; a document POST without .data behaves the same, allowed and refused).
